Hailuogou glacier and hot springs
cn-sichuan-west.via: From Chengdu, about 3–4 hours by car to Mount Siguniang or Kangding; Daocheng Yading is far, most people fly on
cn-sichuan-west.avoid: The Jun–Aug rainy season brings many landslides and mudslides, and National Roads 318 and 317 often have traffic controls. Over National Day Golden Week, traffic jams at Xinduqiao and Daocheng last hours. In winter high passes ice up and close.
cn-sichuan-west.tips: Average altitude is over 3,000 m; get used to it first in Kangding or Xinduqiao, and avoid showers and hard exercise for the first two days. Strong UV; bring sunscreen and sunglasses. Larung Gar Buddhist Academy in Seda changes its rules on visitors from time to time; check before you go. For self-driving pick a high-clearance car, and carry snow chains in winter.

cn-guizhou.places: Huangguoshu Waterfall, Xiaoqikong in Libo, Xijiang Thousand-Household Miao Village, Fanjingshan, Zhaoxing Dong Village, Qingyan Ancient Town, Zhenyuan Ancient Town, Jiabang rice terraces
cn-guizhou.summary: Best: Apr and Sep–Oct; cool in summer, good for escaping the heat
cn-guizhou.climate: Subtropical plateau monsoon climate, often cloudy, rainy and misty; a local saying goes 'never three sunny days in a row'. Summer is cool, about 22–28°C, good for escaping the heat, and May–Jul is wettest; winter is grey and cold, often with freezing ice, and mountain roads ice up.
notes: About 2 to 8°C, grey and cold; often freezing ice, Fanjingshan may close for ice and snow
About 4 to 10°C; Miao villages full of Chinese New Year spirit, the mountains may still freeze

About 15 to 21°C; warm but not hot, Libo and Fanjingshan pleasant
About 19 to 24°C; more rain, waterfalls getting fuller
About 21 to 26°C; peak rainy season, Huangguoshu full of water, watch for falling rocks on mountain roads
About 22 to 27°C; cool summer escape, Huangguoshu at its grandest, crowded in the summer holidays
About 22 to 27°C; peak summer escape season, many afternoon thunderstorms
About 19 to 24°C; less rain, rice ripe and golden on the Jiabang and Congjiang terraces
About 15 to 20°C; clear and crisp; big crowds at Xijiang and Huangguoshu over National Day
About 10 to 15°C; more grey rain, fewer visitors, some Miao villages celebrate Miao New Year

Baili Azalea fields in Bijie

Xijiang Miao New Year (Miao calendar, the date changes every year)
cn-guizhou.avoid: In Jan–Feb freezing ice often closes highways and sights. In the June storm season rocks fall in the mountains. Over National Day and the summer holidays, Xijiang Miao Village and Huangguoshu are very crowded and room prices rise.
cn-guizhou.tips: The weather changes a lot; always carry rain gear and non-slip shoes. Huangguoshu and Xiaoqikong are big and need a full day each. Xijiang Miao Village's night view is worth a night's stay, but guesthouses on the street are noisy. High-speed trains link Guiyang, Kaili and Duyun; between sights you usually need to change or hire a car. Food tends to be sour and spicy.

cn-yunnan-dali-lijiang.places: Kunming, Dianchi Lake, Dali Old Town, Erhai Lake, Cangshan Mountain, Lijiang Old Town, Jade Dragon Snow Mountain, Shuhe, Shaxi Ancient Town
cn-yunnan-dali-lijiang.summary: Best: Feb–Apr and Oct–Nov, sunny dry season, spring-like all year
cn-yunnan-dali-lijiang.climate: Low-latitude plateau monsoon climate: little change between seasons but big swings between day and night. Nov to Apr is the dry season, clear and dry, with strong winds in Dali in winter and spring; May–Oct is the rainy season with many afternoon showers. Jade Dragon Snow Mountain is high and cold.
notes: Kunming days about 15°C, clear and dry, gulls at Dianchi Lake; Lijiang below zero at night

Days about 22°C; clear with little rain, Cangshan azaleas open, clear snow mountain views

cn-yunnan-dali-lijiang.avoid: Over National Day, Chinese New Year and May Day Golden Week, the Lijiang and Dali old towns are packed and room prices double. In the Jun–Aug rainy season Jade Dragon Snow Mountain is often hidden by cloud, with the odd landslide in the mountains.
cn-yunnan-dali-lijiang.tips: Plateau UV is strong; use sun protection all year. Morning and evening can be 15°C apart; bring a jacket. The big Jade Dragon Snow Mountain cable car needs real-name booking; the Glacier Park is about 4,500 m up, so watch for altitude sickness. Dali is windy in winter and spring; ride carefully when cycling around Erhai Lake. High-speed trains run direct Kunming–Dali–Lijiang.

cn-yunnan-shangri-la-meili.places: Dukezong Old Town, Songzanlin Monastery, Potatso National Park, Napa Lake, Feilai Temple, Meili Snow Mountain, Yubeng Village, Tiger Leaping Gorge
cn-yunnan-shangri-la-meili.summary: Best: Oct–Nov, many sunny days and a good chance of sunrise turning the peaks gold
cn-yunnan-shangri-la-meili.climate: Mountain plateau climate; Shangri-La is about 3,300 m up, Deqin about 3,400 m. Winter is bitterly cold, often -10°C at night; the Jun–Sep rainy season brings cloud and fog, and roads are prone to landslides; Oct to Jan has many sunny days, when Meili Snow Mountain most often shows itself.
notes: Shangri-La days about 5°C, nights about -10°C; bitterly cold but many sunny days

cn-yunnan-shangri-la-meili.avoid: In the Jul–Aug rainy season the Yunnan–Tibet road and the Deqin stretch are prone to landslides, and Meili is mostly hidden by cloud. In winter snow on the Yubeng pass may close the way. Potatso and Songzanlin Monastery are crowded over National Day.
cn-yunnan-shangri-la-meili.tips: You are over 3,300 m up; take it slow when you first arrive to avoid altitude sickness. The golden sunrise depends on weather and luck; stay 2 nights or more at Feilai Temple. The Yubeng trek takes 2–4 days; you can hire horses, and choose a licensed guide. Bitterly cold mornings and evenings in winter; bring a down jacket. Deqin's mountain roads have many bends; bring medicine if you get car sick.

cn-yunnan-xishuangbanna.places: Jinghong, Gaozhuang Xishuangjing, Menglun Tropical Botanical Garden, Wild Elephant Valley, Manting Park, Jinuo Mountain Village, Menghai tea hills, Lancang River
cn-yunnan-xishuangbanna.summary: Best: Nov–Feb, the warm dry season, a winter escape
cn-yunnan-xishuangbanna.climate: Tropical monsoon climate: a long summer and no winter. Nov to Apr is the dry season, with days about 25–30°C and often thick fog early in the morning; May–Oct is the hot, humid rainy season with many afternoon storms; Apr–May is hottest, reaching 35°C or more.

cn-yunnan-xishuangbanna.via: Bullet train from Kunming to Xishuangbanna about 3 hours
cn-yunnan-xishuangbanna.avoid: Around Chinese New Year flights and hotels are pricey and Gaozhuang is crowded. Apr–May is very hot. In the rainy season, especially Jul–Aug, it is hot and humid with many mosquitoes, and mountain roads sometimes have landslides.
cn-yunnan-xishuangbanna.tips: For the Water-Splashing Festival, book rooms 1–2 months ahead and waterproof your phone and ID. In the rainy season bring mosquito repellent and rain gear. The Tropical Botanical Garden is large; set aside a day. Seeing elephants at Wild Elephant Valley is down to luck. The China–Laos Railway stops at Xishuangbanna Station, making travel easy. Strong UV; use sun protection.

cn-yunnan-southeast.places: Yuanyang Hani rice terraces, Duoyishu, Jinjifeng peaks in Luoping, Jiulong Waterfalls, Jianshui Old Town, Tuanshan Village, Dongchuan Red Land, Puzhehei
cn-yunnan-southeast.summary: Best: Jan–Mar for mirror-like terraces and Luoping rapeseed flowers, Nov for the Red Land
cn-yunnan-southeast.climate: Low-latitude plateau monsoon climate with big differences in height. The Yuanyang terraces lie at about 1,400–2,000 m, often cloudy and misty, and are flooded in winter and spring; Luoping's flowers bloom in Feb–Mar; May–Oct is the rainy season, with fog and landslides in the mountains. Dongchuan Red Land is about 2,000 m up or higher.

cn-yunnan-southeast.via: High-speed train from Kunming to Luoping about 1.5 hours, Jianshui about 2 hours; about 4 hours by car to Yuanyang
cn-yunnan-southeast.avoid: In the May–Sep rainy season the terraces are often misty, mountain roads are prone to landslides, and Yuanyang sunrises are often hidden by cloud. Over Chinese New Year and on weekends in the rapeseed season, rooms in Luoping and Yuanyang are hard to find.
cn-yunnan-southeast.tips: At Yuanyang, see sunrise at Duoyishu and sunset at Laohuzui; stay in Xinjie town or near Duoyishu. For photos at Dongchuan Red Land get up early, and don't walk on the fields. The spots are spread out, good for self-driving; mountain roads have many bends, so drive carefully. Luoping's flower season shifts with the weather each year; check flower reports before you go.

cn-yunnan-tengchong-nujiang.places: Ginkgo Village and Rehai hot springs in Tengchong, Heshun Ancient Town, Volcano and Geothermal National Geopark, Beihai Wetland, Bingzhongluo on the Nujiang River, Wuli Village, Ruili
cn-yunnan-tengchong-nujiang.summary: Best: Nov for golden ginkgos, Mar for Bingzhongluo peach blossom
cn-yunnan-tengchong-nujiang.climate: Low-latitude plateau climate; Tengchong is about 1,600 m up, with no bitter cold in winter and no fierce heat in summer. The May–Oct rainy season brings lots of rain, and landslides often cut roads in the Nujiang Gorge; Nov to Apr is the sunny dry season. Ruili is lower and hotter.
notes: Tengchong days about 17°C, clear and dry, Rehai hot springs at their nicest

cn-yunnan-tengchong-nujiang.avoid: In the Jun–Sep rainy season landslides often cut the Nujiang Gorge road, making Bingzhongluo hard to reach. On ginkgo-season weekends Ginkgo Village is crowded and parking is hard. Rooms in Tengchong are pricey over Chinese New Year.
cn-yunnan-tengchong-nujiang.tips: Tengchong has an airport; Ginkgo Village, Heshun and Rehai can be linked by hired car. Bingzhongluo is near the border; carry your ID for border checks. Nujiang mountain roads are steep and risky; in the rainy season check road conditions first. Ruili is a border crossing city; follow the border rules. Big temperature swings between morning and evening; bring a jacket.

cn-tibet-lhasa-everest.places: Potala Palace, Jokhang Temple, Barkhor Street, Yamdrok Lake, Namtso Lake, Tashilhunpo Monastery in Shigatse, Gyantse, Everest Base Camp
cn-tibet-lhasa-everest.summary: Best: May and Sep–Oct, clear skies, good roads and a clear view of Everest
cn-tibet-lhasa-everest.climate: Plateau temperate semi-arid climate; Lhasa is about 3,650 m up and Everest Base Camp about 5,200 m, with very strong sun and big day-night swings. In the Jul–Aug rainy season it often rains at night, with the odd landslide; winter is dry, cold and clear, and Namtso freezes over.
notes: Lhasa days about 7°C, nights about -10°C; clear and dry, few visitors

cn-tibet-lhasa-everest.avoid: In the Jul–Aug rainy season some roads have landslides and Everest is often hidden by cloud. In winter Everest Base Camp is bitterly cold and Namtso is frozen. Flights and hotels are pricey over National Day and the summer holidays.
cn-tibet-lhasa-everest.tips: Take it slow for your first two days in Lhasa: shower less and don't drink alcohol; if altitude sickness is bad, see a doctor or go down quickly. The Potala Palace must be booked ahead with your real name. Going to Everest needs a border permit, and foreign visitors need permits such as the Tibet Travel Permit. UV is extremely strong; bring sunscreen and sunglasses. Respect religious customs and walk the kora clockwise.

cn-tibet-nyingchi.places: Yarlung Tsangpo Grand Canyon, Namcha Barwa, Suosong Village, Peach Blossom Valley, Gala Village, Lulang Forest, Basum Tso, Kading Valley, Bomi
cn-tibet-nyingchi.summary: Best: late Mar–Apr for peach blossom, Oct–Nov for autumn colours and snow peaks
cn-tibet-nyingchi.climate: Plateau temperate humid climate, about 2,900–3,300 m up, one of the milder, wetter parts of Tibet. Jun–Sep is the rainy season, and National Road 318 around Bomi and Tongmai is prone to landslides and mudslides; autumn and winter have many sunny days and a good chance of seeing Namcha Barwa.
notes: Days about 8°C; dry, cold and clear, good chance of seeing Namcha Barwa, few visitors
Days about 10°C; Tibetan New Year (the date changes every year), quite a few sunny days
Days about 13°C; Peach Blossom Festival opens in mid to late Mar, snow peaks and peach blossom in one view
Days about 16°C; peach blossom still lush in early to mid Apr, the odd spring snow
Days about 19°C; azaleas open on Sejila Mountain, plants turn green, more rain
Days about 21°C; rainy season starts, lots of cloud and mist, Namcha Barwa hard to see
Days about 22°C; peak rainy season, the Sichuan–Tibet road often cut by landslides
Days about 22°C; lots of rain, high mudslide risk, Lulang Forest at its greenest
Days about 19°C; rains ease, more sunny days in late Sep
Days about 16°C; golden autumn, snow peaks often in clear view; crowded over National Day
Days about 12°C; autumn colours ending, clear skies, fewer visitors
Days about 9°C; dry, cold and clear, sharp snow peak views, snow on some passes
highlights: Nyingchi Peach Blossom Festival, peach blossom at Gala Village
Alpine azaleas on Sejila Mountain
Autumn colours at Basum Tso and Lulang
Golden sunrise on Namcha Barwa
Kongpo New Year (1st day of the 10th Tibetan month, the date changes every year)
cn-tibet-nyingchi.avoid: In the Jun–Sep rainy season, landslides and mudslides are frequent on National Road 318 around Bomi and Tongmai, with frequent traffic controls. During the Peach Blossom Festival and National Day, rooms at Suosong Village and Lulang are hard to get.
cn-tibet-nyingchi.tips: Nyingchi is lower, a good first stop for getting used to the altitude in Tibet. To see Namcha Barwa, stay at Suosong or Zhibai village; sunrise is best. Nyingchi has an airport, and the Lhasa–Nyingchi railway is open. Foreign visitors need Tibet permits, and some border areas need a border permit. When self-driving in the rainy season, check road conditions every day.

cn-tibet-ngari.places: Mount Kailash, Lake Manasarovar, Lhanag Tso, Guge Kingdom ruins, Zanda Earth Forest, Pangong Lake, Shiquanhe, Purang
cn-tibet-ngari.summary: Best: Jun and Sep, settled roads and high clear skies
cn-tibet-ngari.climate: Plateau subarctic arid climate, over 4,500 m up on average, with thin air and very strong sun. Jul–Aug brings a short rainy season, with the odd landslide or river over the road on the Xinjiang–Tibet road; winter nights can drop below -25°C, and snow makes the kora path hard going.
notes: Days about -8°C, nights -25°C; bitter cold and strong wind, not a time to go
Days about -5°C; roads may close for ice and snow, the kora path blocked by snow
Days about 0°C; still bitterly cold and windy, snow on some Xinjiang–Tibet road passes
Days about 5°C; warming up, lakes start to thaw, still snow on the kora path
Days about 10°C; roads improve, kora season starts, still below zero at night
Days about 15°C; many sunny days, many pilgrims on the kora around Saga Dawa
Days about 17°C; short rainy season, grasslands turn green, some roads may have landslides
Days about 16°C; rainy season ending, rivers high, Pangong Lake looks great
Days about 12°C; rainy season over, deep blue skies, best for the kora and the loop road
Days about 6°C; still fine for the kora in early Oct, clearly colder after mid Oct
Days about -2°C; bitter cold arrives, passes ice up, very few visitors
Days about -6°C, nights around -25°C; not advised in winter
highlights: Mount Kailash kora at Saga Dawa (4th Tibetan month, the date changes every year)
Breeding season of bar-headed geese and brown-headed gulls on Bird Island, Pangong Lake
Mount Kailash kora season
Sacred lakes Manasarovar and Lhanag Tso with the holy mountain in one view
Clear light at Zanda Earth Forest and the Guge ruins
cn-tibet-ngari.avoid: Nov to Mar is bitterly cold with little oxygen and icy roads, not advised. The Jul–Aug rainy season has the odd landslide and river over the road. Around Saga Dawa the kora path and rooms are extremely crowded.
cn-tibet-ngari.tips: Over 4,500 m up: be sure to get fully used to the altitude in Lhasa first, and bring oxygen and medicine. You need a border permit; foreign visitors also need Tibet permits. Distances are long and fuel stations few; best to share a hired 4x4 with others. The Mount Kailash kora is about 52 km and usually takes 2–3 days. In the Tibetan Year of the Horse, pilgrim numbers rise sharply.

cn-hong-kong.places: Victoria Harbour, Victoria Peak, Central, Tsim Sha Tsui, Mong Kok, Ngong Ping on Lantau Island, Hong Kong Disneyland, Sai Kung
cn-hong-kong.summary: Best: Oct–Dec, dry, sunny autumn and winter with low humidity
cn-hong-kong.climate: Subtropical monsoon climate. Oct–Dec is clear and dry, about 18–26°C, the most pleasant; Jan–Feb has the odd cold snap; Mar–Apr is humid and foggy; May–Sep is hot and humid with many thunderstorms, and Jun–Sep is typhoon season: when Typhoon Signal No. 8 is up, most transport and shops stop.
notes: Days about 17 to 19°C, dry, the odd cold snap down to 10°C; good for hiking
About 16 to 20°C; Chinese New Year parade and fireworks (lunar calendar), crowded
About 19 to 22°C; humid and foggy, many arts events such as Art Basel
About 22 to 25°C; humid and warming up, Tin Hau Festival celebrated around the city (lunar calendar)
About 26 to 29°C; hot with many thunderstorms, Cheung Chau Bun Festival (lunar calendar)
About 28 to 31°C; peak rainy season, Dragon Boat Festival races, typhoon season starts
About 29 to 32°C; very hot and humid, frequent typhoons, strong air con indoors
About 29 to 32°C; peak typhoon time, transport stops when Signal No. 8 is up
About 28 to 31°C; typhoons still possible, Mid-Autumn lanterns at Victoria Park (lunar calendar)
About 25 to 28°C; turning dry, good for hiking and boat trips, one of the most pleasant months
About 21 to 25°C; clear and dry, low humidity, silvergrass on Tai Mo Shan
About 17 to 21°C; Christmas lights and New Year's Eve fireworks, peak hiking season
highlights: Chinese New Year parade and fireworks (lunar calendar, the date changes every year)
Art Basel Hong Kong
Cheung Chau Bun Festival and bun scrambling (lunar calendar, the date changes every year)
Dragon Boat Festival races (lunar calendar)
Mid-Autumn lantern fair at Victoria Park, Tai Hang Fire Dragon Dance (lunar calendar)
Silvergrass and hiking season at Tai Mo Shan and Sai Kung
Victoria Harbour Christmas lights and New Year countdown
cn-hong-kong.avoid: In the Jun–Sep typhoon season, when Signal No. 8 is up, some MTR lines stop, shops close and flights are cancelled. Jul–Aug is very hot and humid. Popular sights are crowded over Chinese New Year and the Golden Weeks.
cn-hong-kong.tips: Mainland residents need a Hong Kong and Macau travel permit with a valid endorsement. An Octopus card or e-payment is very handy. Under Signal No. 8 or a Black Rainstorm Warning, stay indoors if you can. Air con indoors is strong in summer; bring a thin jacket. The Peak Tram and Disneyland have long queues on holidays; set out early.

cn-macau.places: Ruins of St. Paul's, Senado Square, A-Ma Temple, Rua do Cunha in Taipa, Coloane, Macau Tower, Guia Lighthouse, Cotai Strip
cn-macau.summary: Best: Oct–Dec, dry autumn and winter, lots of festivals and food
cn-macau.climate: South subtropical monsoon climate, close to Hong Kong's. Oct–Dec is dry, about 18–26°C; Feb–Apr is humid and foggy; May–Sep is hot and rainy, and typhoons often hit in Jul–Sep: when Signal No. 8 is up, ferries stop and some transport is suspended.
notes: About 15 to 19°C, dry and coolish, good for walking the old town
About 15 to 20°C; Chinese New Year parade and fireworks, huge crowds
About 18 to 22°C; damp spells, humid and foggy, fewer visitors
About 22 to 25°C; humid and warming up, Tin Hau Festival at A-Ma Temple (lunar calendar)
About 26 to 29°C; hot with many thunderstorms, Drunken Dragon Festival (lunar calendar)

About 17 to 21°C; Christmas lights, Light Festival, Handover anniversary

Tin Hau Festival at A-Ma Temple (23rd day of the 3rd lunar month, the date changes every year)
Drunken Dragon Festival (8th day of the 4th lunar month, the date changes every year)
Macau International Fireworks Display Contest
Macau Grand Prix (usually mid Nov)
Macau Food Festival
Macau Light Festival and Christmas lights
cn-macau.via: From Hong Kong about 1 hour by ferry, or by bus over the Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macau Bridge
cn-macau.avoid: In the Jul–Sep typhoon season ferries and flights are often cancelled. Over Chinese New Year and National Day Golden Week, the area around the Ruins of St. Paul's is packed and hotel prices soar. Some roads close during the Grand Prix.
cn-macau.tips: Mainland residents need a Hong Kong and Macau travel permit and endorsement. The big hotels run free shuttle buses to the border crossings, very handy. You can come and go via the Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macau Bridge or the Gongbei crossing in Zhuhai. Macau patacas and Hong Kong dollars are both accepted, and yuan and mobile payment are also common. The area around the Ruins of St. Paul's is quieter in the morning.

jp-hokkaido.places: Sapporo, Otaru, Furano, Biei, Hakodate, Niseko, Shiretoko, Asahikawa
jp-hokkaido.summary: Best: Jun–Sep for cool summers and flower fields, Jan–Feb for the Snow Festival and powder skiing
jp-hokkaido.climate: Japan's northernmost island. Winters are long and very cold with heavy snow, and its powder snow is world famous; summers are cool and dry, with almost no rainy season and few typhoons, Japan's top choice to escape the heat. Spring and autumn are short, and the scenery in Apr and Nov is rather dull.
notes: Sapporo -7 to -1°C, best powder snow, peak ski season in Niseko, lovely snow scenes in Otaru and Asahikawa
-7 to 0°C, Sapporo Snow Festival and Otaru Snow Light Path in early Feb, drift ice on the Sea of Okhotsk in eastern Hokkaido
-3 to 4°C, end of the snow season but skiing still possible; snow melting in town, roads wet, slippery and muddy
1 to 11°C, low season as the snow melts and the land looks grey-brown; mountain roads open one by one from late Apr
6 to 17°C, cherry blossom at Hakodate's Goryokaku and in Sapporo in early May; after Golden Week, fewer people and fresh green
11 to 21°C, little rain, dry and the most comfortable; lupins in bloom, lavender starts to open in late Jun

About 26°C by day, the warmest month; Biei flower fields at their best, crowded around Obon
About 22°C by day, clear, crisp autumn; autumn colours start at Daisetsuzan in late Sep, autumn food harvest
5 to 16°C, autumn colours at Sounkyo and Jozankei in early to mid Oct, Sapporo ginkgos turn yellow in late Oct
0 to 8°C, between the end of the autumn colours and the first snow; grey and cold, bleak scenery, low season
