highlights: Sapporo Snow Festival (early Feb), Otaru Snow Light Path (early to mid Feb)
Drift ice at Abashiri and Shiretoko (late Jan–early Mar, best in Feb)
Powder ski season at Niseko and Rusutsu (mid Dec–Mar)
Cherry blossom at Hakodate's Goryokaku and Sapporo's Maruyama Park (early May)
Furano lavender (peaks mid-Jul)
Flower fields at Shikisai-no-oka and the Patchwork Road in Biei (Jun–Sep)
Autumn colours at Daisetsuzan and Sounkyo (late Sep–early Oct), the earliest in Japan
Sapporo White Illumination (late Nov–Dec)
jp-hokkaido.avoid: In Apr the snow melts, the scenery is dull and roads are muddy; Nov, between autumn and winter, is grey, cold and bleak. In winter, blizzards in eastern and northern Hokkaido can stop flights and JR trains; don't self-drive in winter without snow driving experience.
jp-hokkaido.tips: In winter wear shoes with non-slip soles; simple ice grips are sold at local convenience stores. Indoors is well heated, so dress in layers. For the Snow Festival and lavender season, book rooms in Sapporo and Furano 2–3 months ahead. Sights are spread out: self-drive is best in summer, in winter take JR or buses.

jp-tohoku.places: Aomori, Oirase Stream, Lake Towada, Hirosaki, Kakunodate in Akita, Sendai, Matsushima, Zao in Yamagata, Ginzan Onsen
jp-tohoku.summary: Best: late Apr cherry blossom, early Aug summer festivals, Oct autumn colours, Feb snow monsters (frost-covered trees)
jp-tohoku.climate: In winter the Sea of Japan side (Aomori, Akita, Yamagata) gets heavy snow, and Zao and Hakkoda are buried deep; Sendai on the Pacific side gets less snow. Summer is cooler than in Kanto; the rainy season runs from mid Jun to late Jul, and the early Aug festival season is still fairly muggy.
notes: -5 to 3°C, heavy snow on the Sea of Japan side, Ginzan Onsen loveliest on snowy nights, Zao snow monsters taking shape
-5 to 3°C, Zao snow monsters at their best, Hirosaki Castle Snow Lantern Festival, Yokote Kamakura (snow hut) Festival
-1 to 8°C, end of winter, melting snow and mud, dull scenery, an in-between low season
3 to 15°C, still cold in early Apr; cherry blossom peaks at Hirosaki Castle and Kakunodate in late Apr
9 to 20°C, last of the cherry blossom in early May, fresh green along Oirase Stream, crowded in Golden Week
14 to 23°C, fresh and pleasant in early Jun, rainy season from mid-month, fewer visitors
About 26°C by day, rainy season lasts to mid or late Jul, damp and wet, mountains often in cloud
About 29°C by day, Aomori Nebuta Festival, Akita Kanto Festival and Sendai Tanabata Festival in early Aug
About 25°C by day, late summer heat fading, sometimes leftover typhoon weather, early autumn in the high mountains in late Sep
8 to 19°C, autumn colours best at Hakkoda in early Oct, at Oirase Stream and Lake Towada in mid to late Oct
3 to 12°C, last autumn colours in the lowlands and at Hirosaki Castle in early Nov; colder in late Nov, maybe the first snow
-2 to 6°C, snow begins, good for hot springs; snow monster light-ups start one by one at the end of the year
highlights: Cherry blossom at Hirosaki Castle and the Kakunodate samurai houses (late Apr–early May)
Aomori Nebuta Festival (2–7 Aug)
Akita Kanto Festival (3–6 Aug), Sendai Tanabata Festival (6–8 Aug)
Autumn colours at Oirase Stream, Lake Towada and Hakkoda (early to late Oct)
Zao snow monsters (best late Jan–Feb, lit up at night)
Ginzan Onsen snow scenes and gas-lamp night views (Dec–Feb)
Yokote Kamakura Festival (mid Feb), Hirosaki Castle Snow Lantern Festival (early to mid Feb)
jp-tohoku.via: Shinkansen from Tokyo to Sendai about 1.5 hours, to Aomori about 3 hours
jp-tohoku.avoid: Mar is the snowmelt low season with flat scenery; rainy season from mid Jun through Jul; during the early Aug festivals, rooms in Aomori, Akita and Sendai are very scarce and prices soar; in winter, heavy snow on the Sea of Japan side can stop trains.
jp-tohoku.tips: The Tohoku, Akita and Yamagata Shinkansen reach the main cities, and the JR East pass is good value. For cherry blossom season and the summer festivals, book rooms more than 3 months ahead. Ginzan Onsen has few inns and rooms are very hard to get in winter; stay nearby and visit as a day trip. For Zao in winter bring snow boots and a windproof jacket.

jp-kanto.places: Tokyo, Yokohama, Kamakura, Enoshima, Nikko, Hakone
jp-kanto.summary: Best: late Mar–May for cherry blossom and fresh green, Oct–Nov for clear autumn days and autumn colours
jp-kanto.climate: Temperate climate on the Pacific coast. Winter is sunny and dry with little snow; summer is hot and humid, often over 35°C. The rainy season runs from early Jun to mid or late Jul, and Aug–Sep is peak typhoon time. Mountain areas such as Nikko, Hakone and Karuizawa are much cooler than Tokyo.
notes: 2 to 10°C, sunny and dry, crowds at New Year shrine visits, Mount Fuji often visible far off on winter days
3 to 11°C, dry, cold and sunny; plum blossom at Yushima Tenjin and Mito's Kairakuen in mid to late Feb
5 to 14°C, end of the Kawazu cherry blossom in mid Mar, Tokyo cherry blossom opens in late Mar, many spring break visitors
10 to 20°C, cherry blossom in full bloom at Ueno, Chidorigafuchi and Meguro River in early Apr, ending mid-month
14 to 23°C, fresh green and comfortable; sights crowded in Golden Week in early May, fewer people mid to late May
18 to 26°C, rainy season starts early Jun, grey, wet and muggy; hydrangeas in full bloom at Meigetsuin in Kamakura
About 30°C by day, hot and muggy once the rainy season ends mid to late Jul; Sumida River Fireworks in late Jul
About 31–35°C by day, very hot and humid, Obon homecoming rush; escape the heat in Karuizawa
About 27°C by day, summer heat lingers, peak of typhoons and autumn rain, transport easily disrupted
15 to 22°C, clear, crisp autumn; Nikko autumn colours mid to late Oct, lively Shibuya Halloween at month end
9 to 17°C, ginkgos and autumn colours at their best in Hakone in early to mid Nov and in Tokyo in late Nov
4 to 12°C, last autumn colours in Tokyo in early Dec, light shows everywhere, crowds and shop closures at year end
highlights: Tokyo cherry blossom (late Mar–early Apr): Ueno, Chidorigafuchi, Shinjuku Gyoen, Meguro River
Plum blossom at Mito's Kairakuen (mid Feb–mid Mar)
Kamakura hydrangeas (mid to late Jun, Meigetsuin and Hasedera)
Sumida River Fireworks (last Saturday of Jul)
Autumn colours on Nikko's Irohazaka road and at Lake Chuzenji (mid to late Oct)
Hakone autumn colours (early to mid Nov)
Ginkgo avenue at Meiji Jingu Gaien (late Nov–early Dec)
Winter light shows in Marunouchi, Roppongi and Omotesando
jp-kanto.avoid: The Jun–Jul rainy season is damp; late Jul–Aug is very hot; Aug–Sep typhoons can halt transport; Golden Week (end of Apr to early May), Obon (mid Aug) and the New Year period bring huge crowds and higher hotel prices.
jp-kanto.tips: Get around mainly by JR and subway; a Suica or PASMO card is easiest. Hotel prices rise clearly in cherry blossom season and Golden Week, so book 1–2 months ahead. In summer guard against the heat and drink water; in winter indoor and outdoor temperatures differ a lot, so wear layers that are easy to take off. Many restaurants and shops close around New Year's Day.

jp-chubu.places: Mount Fuji, Kawaguchiko, Nagano, Karuizawa, Tateyama Kurobe, Shirakawa-go, Takayama, Kanazawa, Nagoya, Kamikochi
jp-chubu.summary: Best: Apr–May for snow walls and cherry blossom, late Jul–Aug for hiking and cool air, Oct–Nov for autumn colours
jp-chubu.climate: A wide area: on the Sea of Japan side, Kanazawa and Shirakawa-go get a lot of snow in winter; in the inland mountains, Kamikochi and Tateyama are cool in summer and bitterly cold and closed in winter; Nagoya is muggy in summer. Rainy season Jun–Jul, many typhoons in Sep.
notes: Kanazawa 1 to 7°C, Takayama -5 to 4°C, snow scenes at Shirakawa-go, Mount Fuji clear from Kawaguchiko on sunny days
-5 to 5°C, winter light-up at Shirakawa-go's gassho village, snow monkeys bathing at Jigokudani in Nagano
0 to 10°C, end of winter, Tateyama and Kamikochi still closed, an in-between low season
5 to 16°C, Tateyama Kurobe opens mid-Apr, Takayama Spring Festival on the 14th–15th, cherry blossom at Kawaguchiko
10 to 21°C, Tateyama snow walls still high, fresh green at Kamikochi, Fuji Shibazakura (moss phlox) in full bloom
15 to 25°C, rainy season with lots of rain, Mount Fuji often hidden by cloud, mountain views poor
Mountains about 20°C, Nagoya about 31°C; Mount Fuji opens for climbing in early Jul, rainy season ends in late Jul
Mountains about 22°C by day, best for climbing Mount Fuji and hiking Kamikochi to escape the heat; lowlands very hot
About 26°C by day, Mount Fuji closes in early Sep, first autumn colours at Tateyama in late Sep, many typhoons
10 to 20°C, autumn colours at Kamikochi and Tateyama in early to mid Oct, Takayama Autumn Festival on the 9th–10th
5 to 15°C, Kawaguchiko Momiji Corridor and Korankei in early to mid Nov, snow ropes put on the trees at Kenrokuen in Kanazawa
-2 to 8°C, Tateyama and Kamikochi closed, Hokuriku crab season, Mount Fuji often clear and visible
highlights: Tateyama Kurobe 'Yuki-no-Otani' snow walls (mid Apr–mid Jun)
Fuji Shibazakura Festival (mid Apr–late May)
Takayama Spring Festival (14–15 Apr)
Mount Fuji climbing season (early Jul–early Sep)
Kamikochi autumn colours (early to mid Oct), Takayama Autumn Festival (9–10 Oct)
Kawaguchiko Momiji Corridor (early to mid Nov), Korankei near Nagoya (mid to late Nov)
Shirakawa-go gassho village snow scenes and winter light-up (set dates in Jan–Feb)
Snow monkeys bathing in hot springs at Jigokudani Monkey Park (Dec–Feb)
jp-chubu.via: Bus from Tokyo to Kawaguchiko about 2 hours; Shinkansen from Tokyo to Karuizawa about 1 hour, to Kanazawa about 2.5 hours; Shinkansen from Osaka to Nagoya about 50 minutes
jp-chubu.avoid: Rainy season from Jun to mid Jul, mountain views often hidden by cloud; many typhoons in Sep; Tateyama Kurobe and Kamikochi are closed from Dec to mid Apr; in winter, roads in Shirakawa-go and Takayama are snowy, so watch for transport problems.
jp-chubu.tips: The Hokuriku Shinkansen links Tokyo, Nagano and Kanazawa. Enter Tateyama Kurobe from Toyama or Shinano-Omachi; buy tickets ahead in peak season. For the Shirakawa-go winter light-up, book a bus or parking in advance. To climb Mount Fuji by the Yoshida Trail, register online and pay beforehand; nights at the summit are near 0°C, so bring warm clothes.

jp-kansai.places: Kyoto, Arashiyama, Osaka, Nara, Kobe, Himeji, Koyasan in Wakayama, Mount Yoshino
jp-kansai.summary: Best: cherry blossom in early Apr, autumn colours in mid to late Nov, when the old capital looks its best
jp-kansai.climate: Kyoto sits in a basin: summers are muggy and often over 35°C, winters damp and cold; Osaka and Kobe by the sea are milder. Rainy season Jun–Jul, typhoons Aug–Sep. Spring and autumn are pleasant but short, and are also when the cherry blossom and autumn leaf crowds are biggest.
notes: Kyoto 1 to 9°C, damp and cold with little snow, New Year crowds at Fushimi Inari, sometimes Kinkakuji in snow
1 to 10°C, still damp and cold, fewest visitors, plum blossom opens at Kitano Tenmangu in late Feb
4 to 14°C, plum blossom in early to mid Mar, first cherry blossom in late Mar, more spring break visitors
9 to 20°C, cherry blossom in full bloom in Kyoto and Osaka in early Apr, Mount Yoshino in early to mid Apr
14 to 25°C, pleasant fresh green, crowded in Golden Week in early May, Kyoto Aoi Festival on the 15th
19 to 28°C, muggy rainy season, hydrangeas in full bloom at Mimurotoji, fewer visitors
About 33°C by day, rainy season ends around mid-Jul, Gion Festival all month, very hot
About 34°C by day, Kyoto's hottest month, Gozan Okuribi bonfires on the 16th, typhoons becoming active
About 30°C by day, summer heat still strong, peak of typhoons, cooler in late Sep
14 to 24°C, cool and comfortable, Kyoto Jidai Festival on the 22nd, Koyasan autumn colours in late Oct
8 to 18°C, autumn colours peak at Tofukuji, Eikando and Arashiyama in mid to late Nov, biggest crowds
3 to 12°C, last autumn colours in early Dec, fewer visitors, temples and shrines get ready for New Year
highlights: Cherry blossom in Kyoto and Osaka (late Mar–early Apr): Philosopher's Path, Daigoji, Osaka Castle
Mount Yoshino's thousand cherry trees (early to mid Apr, blooming from the lower slopes upward)
Kyoto Aoi Festival (15 May)
Kyoto Gion Festival (all of Jul, float parades on the 17th and 24th), Osaka Tenjin Festival (24–25 Jul)
Kyoto Gozan Okuribi bonfires (16 Aug)
Kyoto Jidai Festival (22 Oct)
Koyasan autumn colours (late Oct–early Nov)
Kyoto autumn colours (mid Nov–early Dec): Tofukuji, Eikando, Kiyomizu-dera, Arashiyama
jp-kansai.avoid: In Jul–Aug the Kyoto basin is muggy and often over 35°C; rainy season Jun–Jul; typhoons Aug–Sep; popular temples are packed in early Apr and late Nov; hotel prices double in Golden Week, Obon and New Year.
jp-kansai.tips: Kyoto buses are often packed; combine subway, JR and walking where you can. Get to popular temples before 8 am. For cherry blossom and autumn leaf season, book Kyoto rooms 3 months ahead, or stay in Osaka and commute. Nara's deer will grab food, so don't tease them. Temple lodgings on Koyasan offer morning prayers and Buddhist vegetarian meals.

jp-chugoku-shikoku.places: Hiroshima, Miyajima, Okayama, Kurashiki, Naoshima, Dogo Onsen in Matsuyama, Kochi, Iya Valley, Tottori Sand Dunes
jp-chugoku-shikoku.summary: Best: Apr–May and Oct–Nov, mild weather good for island hopping and cycling
jp-chugoku-shikoku.climate: The Seto Inland Sea coast is mild, with little rain and lots of sun; on the Sea of Japan side, Tottori is snowy, grey and cold in winter; Kochi, on Shikoku's Pacific side, gets heavy rain and frequent typhoons. Rainy season Jun–Jul, summers are muggy.
notes: Hiroshima 2 to 10°C, many sunny, fairly dry days, Miyajima oysters in season, few visitors
2 to 11°C, cold low season, Miyajima Oyster Festival, possible snow in Tottori and the mountains
5 to 15°C, warming up, first cherry blossom in late Mar, Seto Inland Sea islands getting lively
10 to 20°C, cherry blossom at Matsuyama Castle, Okayama's Korakuen and Hiroshima in early Apr, comfortable island hopping
15 to 25°C, sunny and dry, best for cycling the Shimanami Kaido and art trips to Naoshima
19 to 27°C, rainy season with lots of rain, outdoor plans and ferry trips affected
About 31°C by day, very hot once the rainy season ends after mid-Jul, Miyajima Kangensai Festival (lunar calendar)
About 33°C by day, very hot with typhoons, Kochi Yosakoi Festival, Tokushima Awa Odori dance
About 29°C by day, peak typhoon season, strong wind and rain in Kochi and southern Shikoku
14 to 24°C, clear, crisp autumn, best for island hopping and cycling on the Seto Inland Sea
9 to 18°C, autumn colours at Miyajima's Momijidani, Iya Valley and Shodoshima's Kankakei in mid to late Nov
4 to 12°C, getting cold, low season, Tottori snow crab in season, Hiroshima Dreamination lights
highlights: Cherry blossom at Matsuyama Castle, Okayama's Korakuen and Hiroshima Peace Park (early Apr)
Cycling the Shimanami Kaido (best in spring and autumn)
Art island tours of Naoshima and Teshima (the Setouchi Triennale art festival is held every three years)
Miyajima Kangensai Festival (17th day of the 6th lunar month, the date changes every year)
Kochi Yosakoi Festival (9–12 Aug), Tokushima Awa Odori (12–15 Aug)
Autumn colours at Miyajima's Momijidani and Shodoshima's Kankakei (mid to late Nov)
Food season for Hiroshima oysters and Tottori snow crab (Nov–Feb)
jp-chugoku-shikoku.via: Shinkansen from Osaka to Okayama about 45 minutes, to Hiroshima about 1.5 hours; Shinkansen from Fukuoka to Hiroshima about 1 hour
jp-chugoku-shikoku.avoid: Rainy season Jun–Jul; Aug–Sep typhoons often hit Shikoku and the ferries, which may stop; Jul–Aug is muggy; most museums, such as Chichu Art Museum on Naoshima, close on Mondays, so plan around it.
jp-chugoku-shikoku.tips: At high tide Miyajima's great torii gate seems to float on the sea, and at low tide you can walk up to it, so check the tide table first. Visitors to Miyajima pay a visit tax. Book Chichu Art Museum on Naoshima online. Island ferries are few, so check timetables ahead. The JR Hiroshima-Yamaguchi or Setouchi area passes are good value.

jp-kyushu.places: Fukuoka, Dazaifu, Yufuin, Beppu, Kumamoto, Aso, Nagasaki, Kagoshima, Yakushima, Takachiho
jp-kyushu.summary: Best: late Mar–Apr and Oct–Nov; winter is also good for hot springs
jp-kyushu.climate: Winter is mild with little snow (colder in the Aso and Yufuin mountains), summer hot and humid; the rainy season from late May to mid Jul brings heavy rain and frequent downpours; Aug–Sep is the main typhoon path. Yakushima is rainy all year, with snow on the mountains in winter.
notes: Fukuoka 4 to 10°C, possible snow at Aso and Yufuin, hot springs in Beppu and Yufuin at their most comfortable
4 to 12°C, Nagasaki Lantern Festival (with Chinese New Year, the date changes every year), plum blossom at Dazaifu
7 to 16°C, cherry blossom opens at Fukuoka's Maizuru Park and Kumamoto Castle in late Mar, pleasant weather
11 to 21°C, last of the cherry blossom in early Apr, Aso grasslands turn green, Yakushima hiking season begins
15 to 25°C, Hakata Dontaku Port Festival on the 3rd–4th, rainy season begins in late May
19 to 27°C, heavy rainy season rain, prone to downpours and landslides
About 32°C by day, Hakata Gion Yamakasa on the 1st–15th, hot after the rainy season ends mid-month
About 33°C by day, very hot, typhoons more frequent, Nagasaki Shoro Nagashi spirit boat parade on the 15th
About 29°C by day, peak typhoon season, Kyushu is often where typhoons come ashore
15 to 24°C, clear, crisp autumn, Nagasaki Kunchi Festival on the 7th–9th, golden silver grass at Aso
9 to 18°C, autumn colours at Takachiho, Yabakei and Yufuin in mid to late Nov, good for hot spring trips
4 to 12°C, last autumn colours in early Dec, hot spring high season, Huis Ten Bosch lights
highlights: Nagasaki Lantern Festival (over Chinese New Year, the date changes every year)
Cherry blossom at Fukuoka's Maizuru Park and Kumamoto Castle (late Mar–early Apr)
Hakata Dontaku Port Festival (3–4 May)
Hakata Gion Yamakasa (1 Jul–15, the 'Oiyama' float race at dawn on the 15th)
Nagasaki Kunchi Festival (7–9 Oct)
Autumn colours at Takachiho Gorge, Yabakei and Yufuin (mid to late Nov)
Hiking to the Jomon Sugi cedar on Yakushima (best in spring and autumn)
Beppu's Hells hot springs and Yufuin hot springs, most enjoyable in winter
jp-kyushu.avoid: The rainy season from late May to mid Jul brings heavy rain and downpours; Aug–Sep typhoons often come ashore, and flights and ferries may stop; in winter Yakushima's mountains have snow, so hike with care; ash from the Sakurajima volcano sometimes affects Kagoshima.
jp-kyushu.tips: The All Kyushu JR Pass links Fukuoka, Kumamoto, Kagoshima and Nagasaki. Sightseeing trains such as the 'Yufuin no Mori' need seats booked ahead. Mountain hot spring towns are cold in winter, so bring warm clothes. The Jomon Sugi round trip on Yakushima takes about 10 hours; you need rain gear and hiking boots, and in peak season you must take the hikers' bus in and out.

jp-okinawa.places: Okinawa Main Island, Naha, Churaumi Aquarium, Kerama Islands, Ishigaki Island, Taketomi Island, Iriomote Island, Miyako Island
jp-okinawa.summary: Best: Apr and Oct; late Jun–Jul has the most beautiful sea, but watch for typhoons
jp-okinawa.climate: Subtropical oceanic climate, warm all year. Winter is about 15–20°C but windy and not good for swimming; rainy season from mid May to late Jun (earlier than Honshu); Jul–Sep is hot and the main typhoon season, and during a typhoon all flights and ferries stop.
notes: Naha 15 to 20°C, cool and windy, not for swimming; Okinawa cherry blossom opens and whale-watching season in late Jan
15 to 20°C, cherry blossom and whale-watching season, pro baseball spring training, low-season prices
17 to 22°C, warming up, beaches open one by one in late Mar, sea still on the cool side
20 to 25°C, sunny and comfortable, snorkelling and diving, few people and fair prices
About 27°C by day, crowded in Golden Week in early May, Naha Hari dragon boat race on the 3rd–5th, rainy season starts mid-month
About 29°C by day, rainy season showers, steady sunny weather after it ends in late Jun
About 31°C by day, strong sun and the most beautiful sea, peak beach season, watch for typhoons
About 31°C by day, peak typhoon season, flights and ferries easily stopped; Eisa drum dance at the old-calendar Obon
About 30°C by day, typhoons still frequent, the heat not yet gone
About 27°C by day, clear, crisp autumn, sea still warm for snorkelling, Naha Great Tug-of-War in early Oct
About 24°C by day, dry and comfortable, still good for swimming in early Nov, then the sea cools
16 to 21°C, northeast monsoon brings cloud and wind, not for swimming, good for culture and food trips
highlights: Okinawa cherry blossom (late Jan–early Feb), the earliest cherry blossom in Japan
Whale-watching season in the Kerama Islands (Jan–Mar)
Diving and snorkelling season at Kerama, Miyako Island and Ishigaki Island (Apr–Oct)
Naha Hari dragon boat race (3–5 May)
Eisa drum dance (Obon by the lunar calendar, the date changes every year)
Naha Great Tug-of-War (early to mid Oct)
jp-okinawa.avoid: Jul–Sep is typhoon season; when a typhoon hits, flights and ferries stop and you may be stuck for 2–3 days; rainy season from mid May to late Jun; in Dec–Feb the sea is cool and windy, not good for island beach fun.
jp-okinawa.tips: Public transport on the main island is poor, so most people rent a car (a mainland Chinese driving licence is not valid in Japan, so hire a car with driver or take buses). Ishigaki, Miyako and Kerama need a flight or ferry; book ahead in peak season. UV is very strong, so use sun protection. For summer trips, buy travel insurance that covers flight delays.

kr-seoul-gyeonggi.places: Seoul, Gyeongbokgung Palace and Bukchon Hanok Village, Myeongdong, Han River parks, Bukhansan, Hwaseong Fortress in Suwon, DMZ at Paju, Garden of Morning Calm in Gapyeong
kr-seoul-gyeonggi.summary: Best: Apr–May for cherry blossom and sunny spring days, Oct for clear autumn days and autumn colours
kr-seoul-gyeonggi.climate: Continental monsoon climate with four clear seasons. Winter is dry and cold, often below zero, down to -15°C in cold snaps; summer is hot and humid, and the rainy season (jangma) from late Jun to late Jul brings most of the heavy rain. Spring and autumn are sunny; spring sometimes has dust and smog.
notes: -6 to 2°C, bitterly cold and dry, sometimes cold snaps; good for skiing, jjimjilbang saunas and indoor sights
-4 to 5°C, still cold; some shops close over Seollal, the Lunar New Year (lunar calendar, the date changes every year)
1 to 12°C, warm days and cold snaps; forsythia and plum blossom open in late Mar, watch for dust and smog
7 to 18°C, cherry blossom at Yeouido and Seokchon Lake in early Apr, spring flowers all over the city mid to late Apr
13 to 24°C, sunny and comfortable, fresh green and rose season, best for outdoor activities
18 to 27°C, sunny and warming in early to mid Jun, rainy season starts in late Jun
About 29°C by day, rainy season with most of the heavy rain, muggy and humid
About 30°C by day, muggy and humid, sometimes typhoons; cool off at the Han River night markets
17 to 27°C, cooler mornings and evenings, heavy traffic over the Mid-Autumn Festival holiday (15th day of the 8th lunar month)
9 to 21°C, clear, crisp autumn, fireworks festival in early Oct, autumn colours at Bukhansan and the palaces in late Oct
2 to 12°C, autumn colours and ginkgos at their best in early Nov; leaves fall and it turns cold mid to late Nov
-4 to 5°C, cold and dry, lights at Myeongdong and Cheonggyecheon, a strong Christmas feel
highlights: Cherry blossom on Yeouido's Yunjung-ro and at Seokchon Lake (early Apr)
Lotus Lantern Festival (the weekend before Buddha's Birthday, 8th day of the 4th lunar month, the date changes every year)
Changdeokgung Moonlight Tour (night openings in spring and autumn, book ahead)
Seoul International Fireworks Festival (Yeouido Han River Park, early Oct)
Suwon Hwaseong Cultural Festival (early Oct)
Autumn colours and ginkgos at Gyeongbokgung, Changdeokgung's Secret Garden and Namsan (late Oct–early Nov)
Winter lights and Christmas markets at Myeongdong and Cheonggyecheon
kr-seoul-gyeonggi.avoid: Heavy rain in the Jul rainy season; Jul–Aug is muggy; Jan–Feb is bitterly cold; over the Seollal (Lunar New Year) and Mid-Autumn Festival holidays (lunar calendar, the date changes every year) some shops close and transport is packed; sometimes dust and smog in Mar–Apr.
kr-seoul-gyeonggi.tips: A T-money card is easiest for the subway and buses. Naver Map or KakaoMap gives more accurate directions than Google Maps. In spring bring masks for the dust; in winter you need a down jacket, hat and gloves. Wearing hanbok gets you into Gyeongbokgung and other old palaces free. To visit the DMZ you must join a tour and bring your passport.

kr-gangwon.places: Seoraksan, Sokcho, Pyeongchang, Chuncheon, Nami Island, Gangneung, Jeongdongjin, Odaesan
kr-gangwon.summary: Best: Oct for Seoraksan autumn colours, Jan–Feb for skiing in Pyeongchang; Aug for cool east coast beaches
kr-gangwon.climate: The Taebaek Mountains run through it; the mountains are very cold and snowy in winter, Korea's top ski area. On the east coast, Gangneung and Sokcho are milder in winter, with cool sea breezes in summer. In Jul–Aug the rainy season and typhoons can bring heavy rain to the mountains.
notes: Pyeongchang about -13 to -2°C, peak ski season, Hwacheon Sancheoneo (mountain trout) Ice Festival, grand snow scenes
-10 to 1°C, powder ski season goes on, sunrise on the east coast, crowded at Seollal (Lunar New Year)
-3 to 9°C, ski season ends, mountain snow melts into mud, rather dull scenery
Gangneung 5 to 17°C, cherry blossom at Gyeongpodae and in Chuncheon in early Apr, some snow still in the mountains
10 to 22°C, mountains all fresh green, Chuncheon and Nami Island fresh and pleasant
15 to 25°C, cool and clean, a good time to hike Seoraksan, rainy season starts in late Jun
About 28°C by day, rainy season downpours may close mountain roads, beaches open after mid-Jul
About 29°C by day, peak beach season in Gangneung and Sokcho, sometimes typhoons
14 to 25°C, cool mornings and evenings, Seoraksan's peaks start to change colour in late Sep
7 to 20°C, Seoraksan autumn colours at the top in early Oct and on the slopes mid to late Oct, biggest crowds
0 to 12°C, ginkgos and dawn redwoods turn gold on Nami Island in early Nov, colder after mid-Nov
-8 to 3°C, ski resorts open one by one, snow in the mountains, New Year sunrise at Jeongdongjin at month end
highlights: Ski season at Yongpyong and Phoenix in Pyeongchang (mid Dec–early Mar)
Hwacheon Sancheoneo Ice Festival (Jan)
Cherry blossom at Gyeongpodae in Gangneung and in Chuncheon (early Apr)
Gyeongpo Beach in Gangneung and Sokcho Beach (mid Jul–mid Aug)
Seoraksan autumn colours (early to late Oct)
Ginkgo and dawn redwood avenues on Nami Island (late Oct–early Nov)
New Year sunrise by the sea at Jeongdongjin and Gangneung
kr-gangwon.via: KTX from Seoul to Gangneung about 2 hours, bus to Sokcho about 2.5 hours
kr-gangwon.avoid: In the Jul rainy season, mountain downpours often close roads; Seoraksan is extremely crowded on mid-Oct weekends, with bad traffic jams; the Mar snowmelt scenery is dull; in winter mountain roads are icy, so drivers need snow tyres.
kr-gangwon.tips: The KTX from Seoul reaches Gangneung and Pyeongchang in about 2 hours. Reach Nami Island by boat or zipline from Gapyeong pier. In Seoraksan autumn leaf season, go on a weekday and enter the park early. In ski season there are shuttle buses straight from Seoul to the resorts. In winter you need full cold-weather gear.

kr-busan-gyeongsang.places: Busan, Haeundae, Gamcheon Culture Village, Gyeongju, Bulguksa Temple, Jinhae, Tongyeong, Daegu
kr-busan-gyeongsang.summary: Best: Apr cherry blossom and May spring days, Oct–Nov for clear autumn days and autumn colours
kr-busan-gyeongsang.climate: In southeast Korea. Winter is warmer than Seoul with little snow, sunny and dry; summer is muggy, and Daegu is one of Korea's hottest cities. Rainy season from late Jun to Jul; Aug–Sep typhoons often strike, and the Busan coast is hit first.
notes: Busan -1 to 8°C, dry, cold and sunny, few visitors, winter sea views at Haeundae
0 to 10°C, cold low season, first plum blossom in late Feb, crowded at Seollal, the Lunar New Year (the date changes every year)
4 to 14°C, warming up, plum blossom mid-Mar, cherry blossom opens in Jinhae and Gyeongju in late Mar
9 to 19°C, Jinhae Gunhangje Festival and Gyeongju's Bomun Lake cherry blossom in early Apr, spring at its best
14 to 23°C, sunny and comfortable, Buddha's Birthday lanterns, lovely Tongyeong sea views and Gyeongju at night
18 to 25°C, comfortable in early to mid Jun, rainy season starts in late Jun
About 29°C by day, rainy and wet, muggy after the rainy season ends in late Jul, Daegu can top 35°C
About 30°C by day, peak beach season at Haeundae and Gwangalli, watch for typhoons
About 27°C by day, peak typhoon season, heavy traffic over the Mid-Autumn Festival holiday
13 to 23°C, clear, crisp autumn, Busan International Film Festival in early Oct, Gyeongju autumn colours in late Oct
7 to 17°C, autumn colours at Bulguksa in early Nov; recently the Busan Fireworks Festival is mostly held this month
1 to 10°C, sunny, cold and dry, Nampo-dong Christmas Tree Festival, few visitors
highlights: Cherry blossom at the Jinhae Gunhangje Festival (late Mar–early Apr)
Cherry blossom at Bomun Lake and Daereungwon in Gyeongju (early Apr)
Buddha's Birthday lanterns in Gyeongju (8th day of the 4th lunar month, the date changes every year)
Beach season at Haeundae and Gwangalli (Jul–Aug)
Busan International Film Festival (early Oct)
Autumn colours at Bulguksa and Tohamsan in Gyeongju (late Oct–early Nov)
Busan Fireworks Festival (Gwangan Bridge, recently mostly in early Nov)
kr-busan-gyeongsang.via: KTX from Seoul to Busan about 2.5 hours, to Gyeongju about 2 hours
kr-busan-gyeongsang.avoid: Rainy season late Jun–Jul; Aug–Sep typhoons often hit Busan head-on, and seaside facilities and flights may shut down; Daegu is very hot in Jul–Aug; traffic is extremely jammed during the Jinhae Gunhangje Festival, so use public transport.
kr-busan-gyeongsang.tips: The KTX from Seoul reaches Busan in about 2.5 hours. Busan's subway covers the main sights. Gyeongju's historic sites are spread out, so rent a bike or take buses. Visit Jinhae in cherry blossom season on a weekday if you can. In summer, book sea-view rooms and fireworks viewing spots early. Winter sea winds are strong, so bring a windproof jacket.

kr-jeju.places: Jeju City, Seongsan Ilchulbong, Hallasan, Udo Island, Seopjikoji, Jungmun Resort, Hyeopjae Beach, Manjanggul Cave
kr-jeju.summary: Best: late Mar–May for canola flowers and cherry blossom, Oct for silver grass and autumn scenery
kr-jeju.climate: Korea's southernmost island, a volcanic one. Winter is warmer than the mainland but sea winds are strong, and Hallasan has snow; summer is muggy and humid, rainy season from late Jun to Jul, and typhoons often hit in Jul–Sep, when many flights are cancelled.
notes: 3 to 9°C, strong sea wind makes it feel cold, snowy Hallasan hikes, winter camellias in full bloom
3 to 10°C, grey, cold and windy low season, first plum blossom in late Feb
6 to 14°C, still cool in early Mar; canola flowers open and first cherry blossom in late Mar
10 to 19°C, cherry blossom and canola together on Jeonnong-ro in early Apr, best for spring trips
14 to 23°C, sunny and comfortable, Udo sea views and fresh green, a good time to climb Hallasan
18 to 25°C, hydrangeas in full bloom mid-Jun, rainy season starts in late Jun
About 29°C by day, rainy season lasts to mid or late Jul, muggy and humid, typhoons begin
About 30°C by day, peak beach season, the warmest sea, watch for typhoons
About 27°C by day, peak typhoon season, flights often affected
15 to 23°C, clear, crisp autumn, silver grass sways at Saebyeol Oreum, Hallasan autumn colours in late Oct
10 to 18°C, tangerine picking season begins, silver grass still lovely, sea winds getting stronger
5 to 12°C, seas of winter camellias, tangerines in season, first snow on Hallasan
highlights: Canola flower fields (late Mar–mid Apr), most famous below Seongsan Ilchulbong
Cherry blossom on Jeonnong-ro and at Jeju National University (late Mar–early Apr)
Hydrangeas (around mid Jun)
Hyeopjae and Hamdeok beaches (Jul–Aug)
Silver grass at Saebyeol Oreum and Sangumburi (Oct–Nov)
Tangerine picking and winter camellias (Nov–Jan)
Snowy Hallasan hikes (ice grips needed)
kr-jeju.avoid: Jul–Sep is typhoon season, and flights and ferries are often cancelled; rainy season late Jun–Jul; very strong sea winds make winter feel cold; rental car and room prices soar in the Korean summer holidays and over the Mid-Autumn Festival holiday.
kr-jeju.tips: Chinese passport holders flying direct into Jeju can stay 30 days visa-free. Island buses are infrequent; with an international driving permit you can rent a car, but a mainland Chinese licence cannot be used in Korea, so hire a car with driver or take buses. To reach Hallasan's summit (Seongpanak or Gwaneumsa trail), book online ahead. Bring a windproof jacket in every season.

tw-taipei-north.places: Taipei, Beitou Hot Springs, Yangmingshan, Tamsui, Jiufen, Pingxi in New Taipei, Yehliu, Yilan
tw-taipei-north.summary: Best: Oct–Nov and Mar–Apr, comfortable weather with less rain and few typhoons
tw-taipei-north.climate: Subtropical climate. Summer is hot and humid, often reaching 35°C, with many afternoon thunderstorms; plum rain season in May–Jun, typhoon season Jul–Sep. In winter the northeast monsoon brings damp, cold, rainy weather, and Keelung, Jiufen and Yilan are especially rainy in winter.
notes: Taipei 13 to 19°C, damp, cold and often rainy, the best time for Beitou hot springs, Jiufen often foggy
14 to 20°C, Yangmingshan cherry blossom, Pingxi sky lanterns at the Lantern Festival (the date changes every year)
16 to 23°C, warming up and comfortable, Yangmingshan flower season, calla lily season starts at Zhuzihu
19 to 26°C, spring flowers, calla lilies in full bloom at Zhuzihu, tung blossom starts in late Apr
22 to 29°C, tung blossom in full bloom in early May, plum rain season from mid-month
About 32°C by day, lots of plum rain and afternoon thunderstorms, muggy and humid
About 34°C by day, very hot, typhoon season starts, Yilan International Children's Folklore and Folkgame Festival
About 34°C by day, hot with many thunderstorms, frequent typhoons, Ghost Festival in the 7th lunar month
About 31°C by day, still many typhoons, lingering muggy heat
22 to 27°C, clear, crisp autumn, less rain, best for outdoor trips and hiking
19 to 24°C, dry and comfortable, silver grass on Yangmingshan, northeast monsoon builds in late Nov
15 to 21°C, damp and cold northeast monsoon, Jiufen and Yilan rainy, Taipei 101 New Year's Eve fireworks
highlights: Pingxi Sky Lantern Festival (Lantern Festival, 15th day of the 1st lunar month, the date changes every year)
Yangmingshan Flower Festival cherry blossom and azaleas (Feb–Mar)
Zhuzihu calla lily season (Mar–Apr)
Northern Taiwan tung blossom season (late Apr–early May)
Yilan International Children's Folklore and Folkgame Festival (Jul–Aug)
Keelung Ghost Festival (7th lunar month, the date changes every year)
Silver grass on Yangmingshan's Datun Mountain (late Oct–Nov)
Taipei 101 New Year's Eve fireworks (31 Dec)
tw-taipei-north.avoid: May–Jun plum rain; Jul–Sep is typhoon season, and when a typhoon comes, work and school stop and transport halts; Jiufen, Keelung and Yilan are rainy, damp and cold in winter; Jiufen and Pingxi are packed over Chinese New Year and long weekends.
tw-taipei-north.tips: An EasyCard is easiest for the MRT and buses. Jiufen Old Street is extremely crowded on weekend evenings, so a weekday is better. In winter bring a windproof, waterproof jacket; in summer carry an umbrella against sun and thunderstorms. Beitou and Wulai have hot springs. On typhoon days, watch for official work and school closure notices.

tw-central-south.places: Taichung, Sun Moon Lake, Cingjing Farm, Hehuanshan, Alishan, Tainan, Kaohsiung, Kenting
tw-central-south.summary: Best: the Nov–Apr dry season with clear skies, Alishan cherry blossom in Mar
tw-central-south.climate: Winter and spring are the dry season, sunny with little rain, and even in winter Tainan and Kaohsiung reach over 20°C by day; May–Sep is the wet season, bringing most of the plum rain, afternoon thunderstorms, southwest-flow downpours and typhoons. The high mountains of Alishan and Hehuanshan are cold, and Hehuanshan may get snow in winter cold snaps.
notes: Kaohsiung 16 to 24°C, sunny dry season, possible snow on Hehuanshan in cold snaps
Tainan 15 to 24°C, sunny, crowds over the Chinese New Year holiday, Yanshui Beehive Fireworks at the Lantern Festival
17 to 27°C, Alishan cherry blossom season from mid-Mar, pleasant weather at Sun Moon Lake
21 to 29°C, comfortable late spring, firefly season in the mountains, Kenting sea warming up
24 to 31°C, tung blossom and fireflies in early May, plum rain season after mid-May
About 32°C by day, lots of plum rain and southwest-flow downpours, falling rocks and landslides in the mountains
About 33°C by day, hot, typhoon season starts, peak beach season in Kenting
About 33°C by day, peak of typhoons and downpours, the Alishan road is often cut
About 32°C by day, still many typhoons, muggy and humid
22 to 30°C, sometimes typhoons in early Oct, dry season from mid-Oct, clear and crisp
19 to 28°C, sunny and dry, one of the best times for the Alishan sea of clouds and sunrise
16 to 25°C, sunny dry season, Tainan and Kaohsiung warm and comfortable, possible snow on Hehuanshan
highlights: Alishan cherry blossom season (mid Mar–early Apr)
Firefly season in the mountains (Apr–May, Alishan, Xitou and more)
Dajia Mazu Pilgrimage (3rd lunar month, the date changes every year)
Yanshui Beehive Fireworks in Tainan (Lantern Festival, the date changes every year)
Alishan sunrise and sea of clouds (best in the autumn and winter dry season)
Snow on Hehuanshan in cold snaps (depends on the cold air mass)
Snorkelling and water sports in Kenting (Apr–Oct)
tw-central-south.via: High-speed rail from Taoyuan Airport to Taichung about 40 minutes, to Kaohsiung about 1.5 hours
tw-central-south.avoid: Jun–Sep brings most of the plum rain, downpours and typhoons, and mountain roads to Alishan and Hehuanshan often collapse and close; strong winds blow down from the mountains in Kenting in Oct–Mar; Sun Moon Lake and Alishan are packed over Chinese New Year and long weekends.
tw-central-south.tips: High-speed rail is the easiest way between Taichung, Chiayi, Tainan and Kaohsiung. Book the Alishan forest train and rooms ahead; for the sunrise you get up soon after 4 am. Wuling on Hehuanshan is about 3,275 m up; in winter you need snow chains, and watch for altitude sickness. In Kenting, rent a car or scooter (licence needed).

tw-east-islands.places: Hualien, Taroko, Taitung, Chishang, Green Island, Orchid Island, Penghu, Kinmen
tw-east-islands.summary: Best: Apr–Jun for sea views on the outlying islands, Oct for clear, crisp days in Hualien, Taitung and Kinmen
tw-east-islands.climate: The east faces the Pacific and is where typhoons most often come ashore; in winter the northeast monsoon makes Hualien rainy. Penghu, Green Island and Orchid Island have very rough seas in winter and ferries often stop, while summer is the island high season; Kinmen is dry and cold in winter and foggy in spring.
notes: Hualien 14 to 21°C, northeast monsoon brings rain, rough seas at Penghu and Orchid Island, ferries often stop
15 to 21°C, damp, cold, windy low season, Kinmen rather cold, most island businesses closed
17 to 23°C, Hualien and Taitung warm up, Kinmen spring fog often delays flights, island winds easing
20 to 26°C, Penghu Fireworks Festival opens, flying fish season on Orchid Island, island travel season begins
23 to 29°C, calm seas, Penghu Fireworks Festival, best for snorkelling at Green Island and sea views on Orchid Island
About 31°C by day, clear after the plum rain, high season for water sports, watch for afternoon thunderstorms
About 33°C by day, high season on the islands and for the Taitung balloon festival, watch for typhoons
About 33°C by day, peak typhoon season, ferries and flights easily stopped, you may get stuck on an island
About 31°C by day, frequent typhoons, strong wind and rain in the east, the Suhua Highway often cut
22 to 28°C, clear and crisp, good for Taroko and the East Rift Valley, Kinmen at its most comfortable
20 to 26°C, northeast monsoon getting stronger, more rain in Hualien, rougher seas around the islands
17 to 23°C, Hualien grey, damp and cold; Penghu, Green Island and Orchid Island enter the no-ferry low season
highlights: Penghu International Fireworks Festival (Apr–Jun, set nights each week)
Tao people's flying fish season on Orchid Island (spring and summer)
Diving, snorkelling and the Zhaori undersea hot spring on Green Island
Taiwan International Balloon Festival at Luye, Taitung (Jul–Aug)
Golden rice fields in Chishang and the East Rift Valley, and the autumn harvest Rice Art Festival (Oct–Nov)
Taroko Gorge, Qingshui Cliffs and Kinmen's old houses and wartime sites (most comfortable in autumn)
tw-east-islands.via: Train from Taipei to Hualien about 2 hours, to Taitung about 3.5 hours; Penghu, Kinmen and Orchid Island need a further flight or boat
tw-east-islands.avoid: Jul–Sep typhoons often come ashore in the east, and island ferries and flights stop; in Nov–Mar the northeast monsoon makes seas rough at Penghu, Green Island and Orchid Island and most ferries stop; Kinmen's spring fog often grounds flights; since the earthquake some Taroko trails are closed.
tw-east-islands.tips: Book Green Island and Orchid Island boat tickets and rooms early in summer; bring medicine if you get seasick. On Orchid Island respect Tao culture and ask before photographing people. Check which Taroko trails are open before you go. Hualien–Taitung train tickets are tight over long weekends, so book early. Renting a scooter is the usual way to get around Penghu and Green Island.

mn-mongolia.places: Ulaanbaatar, Terelj National Park, Kharkhorin, Erdene Zuu Monastery, Lake Khuvsgul, Gobi Desert, Khongoryn Els sand dunes
mn-mongolia.summary: Best: Jul–Aug when the grasslands are greenest, Naadam Festival in mid Jul
mn-mongolia.climate: A classic continental climate. Winter is long and bitterly cold; Ulaanbaatar is one of the world's coldest capitals, down to -30°C in Jan. Summer is short and mild with big day–night temperature swings; Jul–Aug gets most of the rain, mostly in short showers. Spring is windy and dusty.
notes: Ulaanbaatar about -28 to -15°C, extreme cold and heavy coal smoke pollution, outdoor travel is hard
-25 to -10°C, bitterly cold, Tsagaan Sar (Mongolian New Year, the date changes every year)
-15 to 0°C, still cold, Khuvsgul Ice Festival in early Mar, activities on the frozen lake
-5 to 8°C, warming but windy and dusty, grasslands brown and dry, low season
3 to 17°C, windy and dry, grasslands start to turn green, Gobi trips possible from late May
10 to 22°C, grasslands turn green, more visitors, about 30°C by day in the Gobi
11 to 23°C, grasslands at their best, Naadam Festival on the 11th–13th, short afternoon showers
10 to 21°C, lush green grasslands, tail end of high season, cooler mornings and evenings in late Aug
2 to 15°C, golden autumn colours, fewer visitors, frost starts at night
-6 to 7°C, Bayan-Ulgii Golden Eagle Festival in early Oct, then the cold sets in
-18 to -4°C, bitter cold arrives, most tourist camps close
-25 to -13°C, extreme cold, ger camps closed, only special winter tours
highlights: Naadam Festival (11 Jul–13, wrestling, horse racing, archery)
Ger stays, horse riding and Terelj National Park on the central grasslands (Jun–Aug)
Lake and mountain scenery at Lake Khuvsgul (Jun–Sep)
Gobi Desert and Khongoryn Els dunes (most comfortable May–Jun and Sep, avoiding the midsummer heat)
Bayan-Ulgii Golden Eagle Festival (early Oct)
Khuvsgul Ice Festival (early Mar)
Tsagaan Sar (Mongolian New Year, the date changes every year)
mn-mongolia.avoid: Nov–Feb is extremely cold, Ulaanbaatar has heavy coal smoke pollution and most camps are closed; Apr–May has frequent dust storms; flight and room prices soar during Naadam, so book early.
mn-mongolia.tips: Sights are spread out and roads are rough, so most people travel by hired car with a driver and guide. Summer days and nights differ a lot in temperature, so bring fleece and a windproof jacket. Most ger camps have pit toilets and limited hot water. For Naadam, book flights and rooms more than 3 months ahead. Visa rules often change, so check before you go.

my-kuala-lumpur.region: Kuala Lumpur and the West Coast
my-kuala-lumpur.places: Kuala Lumpur, Batu Caves, Putrajaya, Melaka, Ipoh, Kuala Selangor fireflies, Klang
my-kuala-lumpur.summary: Good all year; Jan–Feb and Jun–Jul are drier, Apr and Oct–Nov have the most thunderstorms
my-kuala-lumpur.climate: Tropical rainforest climate, hot and humid all year, 31–33°C by day and about 24°C at night. No real dry season; thunderstorms are most frequent in the monsoon changeovers of Mar–Apr and Oct–Nov, Jun–Jul is drier, and Aug–Sep sometimes has haze.
notes: About 32°C by day, fairly dry, malls and Chinatown brightly decorated before Chinese New Year
About 33°C by day, less rain; hotels and long-distance bus tickets are tight over the Chinese New Year holiday
About 33°C by day, muggy, monsoon changeover begins, more afternoon thunderstorms
About 33°C by day, one of the stormiest months, strong thunderstorms often in the evening
About 33°C by day, thunderstorms easing, Wesak Day Buddhist float procession
About 32°C by day, fairly dry, good for strolling the old towns of Melaka and Ipoh
About 32°C by day, drier with many sunny days, good for fireflies and old-town walks
About 32°C by day, National Day celebrations on Aug 31, watch for haze
About 32°C by day, haze still possible, Malaysia Day holiday on 16 Sep
About 32°C by day, monsoon changeover, frequent afternoon downpours, sometimes local flash floods
About 31°C by day, one of the wettest months, heavy rain can cause brief flash floods
About 31°C by day, still rainy, Christmas and year-end shopping season with many mall sales
highlights: Chinese New Year (the date changes every year, late Jan to mid Feb): Petaling Street and Melaka's Jonker Street hung with lanterns
Thaipusam (Tamil calendar, the date changes every year, usually late Jan to Feb): huge crowds of pilgrims at Batu Caves
Eid al-Fitr (Islamic calendar, about 11 days earlier each year): about a week of homecoming travel around it
National Day on 31 Aug: celebrations and parades at Merdeka Square and Putrajaya
Deepavali (Festival of Lights, Hindu calendar, the date changes every year, usually Oct–Nov): lights and markets in Little India
Kuala Selangor fireflies all year, best on moonless, dry nights
Haze season from forest burning in Sumatra, how bad it gets changes every year
my-kuala-lumpur.avoid: Apr and Oct–Nov have the most thunderstorms; if haze comes in Aug–Sep, outdoor plans suffer; during the Eid al-Fitr and Chinese New Year homecoming rush, highways are jammed and bus and train tickets are tight.
my-kuala-lumpur.tips: Malls and trains are strongly air-conditioned, so bring a light jacket. During Ramadan Muslims fast by day; non-Muslims eat as normal but should be discreet, and the evening Ramadan bazaars are worth a visit. Go firefly watching on a moonless night; trips may be cancelled in heavy rain. Melaka is busy at weekends, so go on a weekday if you can.

my-penang.places: George Town, Penang Hill, Kek Lok Si Temple, Clan Jetties, Batu Ferringhi, Penang National Park, Balik Pulau
my-penang.summary: Best: Dec–Mar is drier, Jan–Feb the sunniest; Sep–Nov is the peak of the rainy season
my-penang.climate: Tropical rainforest climate, about 24–32°C all year. Dec–Mar is drier and sunny; thunderstorms build in Apr–May, Aug–Nov is the rainy season, wettest in Sep–Oct, with frequent downpours from afternoon into the night.
notes: About 32°C by day, dry season, sunny with little rain, the most comfortable time for walking George Town's streets
About 32°C by day, dry; Chinese New Year and the Lantern Festival are lively in George Town
About 33°C by day, muggy with little rain, go up Penang Hill early in the morning
About 33°C by day, more thunderstorms, mostly afternoon showers
About 32°C by day, hot, Wesak Day Buddhist events, more thunderstorms
About 31°C by day, southwest monsoon, many breaks between showers, still fine to travel
About 31°C by day, George Town World Heritage Day on Jul 7, cultural events in the old town
About 31°C by day, rain increasing, sometimes haze, getai stage shows for the Hungry Ghost Festival
About 31°C by day, peak rainy season begins, frequent downpours from afternoon into the night
About 31°C by day, one of the wettest months, beach activities limited
About 31°C by day, still rainy, slowly easing in the second half of the month
About 31°C by day, less rain, more visitors over the year-end holidays
highlights: Chinese New Year (the date changes every year): Kek Lok Si lit up; the Jade Emperor's birthday prayers at the Clan Jetties on the 9th day are the liveliest
Thaipusam (the date changes every year, usually Jan–Feb): pilgrimage to the hilltop Hindu temple on Waterfall Road, coconuts smashed along the way
George Town World Heritage Day on Jul 7, with cultural shows and guided walks in the old town
Durian season (about Jun–Aug), tree-ripened durians at Balik Pulau orchards
Hungry Ghost Festival (7th lunar month, the date changes every year): street stages for Chinese opera and getai shows
Drier months: clear views from Penang Hill, good for coastal hikes in the national park
my-penang.avoid: Sep–Nov is the peak rainy season, with frequent afternoon downpours and local flash floods; over Chinese New Year room prices double and there are long queues for the Penang Hill funicular.
my-penang.tips: George Town's heritage area is best on foot or by bike; the midday sun is strong, so go out in the morning and evening. Penang Hill has long queues at weekends and holidays; go in the morning or buy a fast-lane ticket. Penang is famous for street food, and many stalls have a fixed weekly day off. The national park requires registration to enter, and trails are slippery after rain.

my-langkawi.places: Pantai Cenang, Sky Bridge and cable car, Kilim mangroves, Tanjung Rhu beach, Seven Wells Waterfall, Kuah, Pulau Payar Marine Park, Black Sand Beach
my-langkawi.summary: Best: Dec–Mar dry season, calm seas; May–Oct has more rain and big waves
my-langkawi.climate: Tropical monsoon climate, about 24–33°C all year. Nov–Apr is the dry season, sunny with little rain and calm seas; in May–Oct the southwest monsoon brings more rain, Aug–Sep is wettest, sometimes with big waves.
notes: About 32°C by day, dry season, calm seas, best for beaches and island hopping
About 33°C by day, sunny with little rain, good for the cable car to the Sky Bridge
About 34°C by day, hot and dry, fairly clear water
About 34°C by day, afternoon thunderstorms begin, still good for trips
About 33°C by day, rainy season begins, more showers, fewer visitors
About 32°C by day, rainy season, mostly showers, lower hotel prices
About 32°C by day, many rainy days, average sea conditions, try a mangrove boat trip
About 32°C by day, lots of rain and big waves, island hopping and snorkelling sometimes cancelled
About 31°C by day, the wettest month, the cable car stops during thunderstorms
About 31°C by day, still rainy, slowly drying out at month end
About 31°C by day, less rain, good value just before high season
About 31°C by day, dry season begins, room prices rise clearly over Christmas and New Year
highlights: Dry season: calm seas, good for island hopping, sunset cruises and beaches
Snorkelling at Pulau Payar Marine Park, with baby sharks and coral, clearer water in the dry season
Mangrove boat trips in Kilim Geoforest Park, with eagles, macaques and karst landscapes
Duty-free island: tax-free shopping for alcohol, chocolate and more all year
LIMA, the Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (late May in odd-numbered years), hotels tight then
my-langkawi.avoid: Aug–Oct has the most rain; when waves are big, island hopping and snorkelling may be cancelled, and the cable car stops for thunderstorms; room prices are highest from Christmas to Chinese New Year.
my-langkawi.tips: There is little public transport on the island; most visitors rent a car or use ride-hailing apps, and traffic drives on the left. The cable car closes for regular maintenance or bad weather, so check before going. Pantai Cenang has the most places to eat; for quiet, stay around Tanjung Rhu. Book rooms early for the Dec–Feb high season.

my-highlands.places: Cameron Highlands, Tanah Rata, BOH tea plantation, Mossy Forest, strawberry farms, Genting Highlands, Genting cable car, Fraser's Hill
my-highlands.summary: Cool all year, an escape from the heat; Jan–Feb and Jun–Jul have less rain and are most comfortable, Oct–Nov has lots of rain and fog
my-highlands.climate: About 1,300–2,000 m above sea level (Cameron Highlands about 1,500 m), 18–25°C by day and 12–16°C at night. Rainy and foggy all year; Apr and Oct–Dec are wettest, Jan–Feb and Jun–Jul fairly dry.
notes: About 22°C by day, about 14°C at night, drier, clear views of the tea plantations
About 23°C by day, little rain, but huge crowds and traffic jams over Chinese New Year
About 24°C by day, more sunny days, sometimes afternoon thunderstorms
About 24°C by day, more thunderstorms, watch for falling rocks and thick fog on mountain roads
About 24°C by day, showers, still many self-drive visitors at weekends
About 23°C by day, fairly dry, crowded at weekends in the school holidays
About 23°C by day, drier and fresh, good for the Mossy Forest and jungle trails
About 23°C by day, occasional showers, crowded going up on the National Day long weekend
About 23°C by day, more rain, often foggy in the afternoon
About 22°C by day, rainy season, landslides on mountain roads, slippery trails
About 22°C by day, the wettest month, often cloud and fog all day, poor views
About 22°C by day, lots of rain, year-end school holiday crowds pour in
highlights: Drier months, good for Cameron tea plantations, the Mossy Forest and jungle trails
Migratory bird season at Fraser's Hill, when birdwatchers gather; birding is best early in the morning
Cameron strawberry farms, fruit, vegetable and flower markets and night markets, open all year
Genting cable car and indoor and outdoor theme parks; the hilltop is often below 18°C at night
Genting and Cameron packed at Chinese New Year, bad traffic jams on the roads up
my-highlands.via: Drive from Kuala Lumpur to Genting about 1 hour, to Cameron Highlands about 3.5 hours
my-highlands.avoid: Oct–Dec has the most rain, with landslides on mountain roads and frequent thick fog; at Chinese New Year and on public holidays the roads up are badly jammed, and room prices rise at weekends.
my-highlands.tips: Mornings and evenings are cool, so bring a long-sleeved jacket and rain gear. The road up has many bends, so bring medicine if you get carsick; fog is thick at night, so drive with care. Some Cameron jungle trails need a guide or have been closed for safety, so check locally before you go. Go up on weekdays if you can, avoiding weekends and holidays.

my-east-coast.places: Perhentian Islands, Redang Island, Lang Tengah Island, Tioman Island, Kuantan, Cherating, Kuala Terengganu, Kota Bharu
my-east-coast.summary: Best: Apr–Aug island season; Nov–Feb northeast monsoon, most island resorts closed
my-east-coast.climate: Tropical monsoon climate, 28–33°C by day. From Nov to Feb the northeast monsoon brings downpours, big waves and floods, and the islands basically close; Mar–Oct is fairly sunny with clear water, the island season.
notes: About 28°C by day, northeast monsoon in full force, downpours and big waves, most island resorts closed
About 29°C by day, end of the monsoon but still big waves, most of Perhentian and Redang not yet open
About 30°C by day, monsoon over, resorts reopen one by one from about mid to late Mar
About 31°C by day, sea conditions improving, water starting to clear, good for snorkelling
About 32°C by day, sunny and hot, good visibility, peak diving season begins
About 32°C by day, calm seas, turtle nesting season, good for island hopping
About 32°C by day, high season, book island rooms ahead
About 32°C by day, good sea conditions, still a great time for diving and island hopping
About 32°C by day, still fine for boat trips, fewer visitors
About 31°C by day, change-over before the monsoon, more showers, some resorts close in late Oct
About 29°C by day, northeast monsoon arrives, islands basically closed, floods common on the coast
About 28°C by day, peak time for heavy rain and floods, most ferries stopped
highlights: Diving and snorkelling season at Perhentian and Redang, turtles and blacktip reef sharks often seen
Green turtle nesting season (about May–Sep), turtle conservation projects on Redang and elsewhere
Best diving on Tioman (about Mar–Oct), a few places to stay are open on the island all year
Northeast monsoon: most island resorts close, ferries stop, floods common on the coast
Surfing at Cherating near Kuantan in the monsoon, good for beginners
Crystal Mosque in Kuala Terengganu, Kota Bharu Central Market and traditional Kelantan culture
my-east-coast.avoid: From Nov to Feb the northeast monsoon closes most island resorts and stops ferries, and floods are common on land; Mar and Oct are change-over months, when some facilities are not fully open.
my-east-coast.tips: Perhentian is usually reached by speedboat from Kuala Besut jetty, Redang mostly from jetties around Kuala Terengganu; boats stop in rough seas. The islands have few ATMs, so bring enough cash. Kelantan and Terengganu are conservative, so dress modestly away from the beach. Book rooms ahead for Jul–Aug and public holidays.

my-sabah.places: Kota Kinabalu, Mount Kinabalu, Tunku Abdul Rahman Marine Park, Semporna, Sipadan, Mabul Island, Sandakan, Kinabatangan River
my-sabah.summary: Best: Feb–May is dry and fresh, good for both diving and climbing; Oct–Dec has lots of rain
my-sabah.climate: Tropical rainforest climate, 30–32°C by day on the coast, near 0°C at night on the summit of Mount Kinabalu. The west coast is wettest in Oct–Nov, the east gets lots of rain in the Dec–Feb northeast monsoon; it lies south of the typhoon belt and is rarely hit directly by typhoons.
notes: About 31°C by day, rainy season in the east, the Kinabatangan River floods easily; Kota Kinabalu is OK
About 31°C by day, turning dry, good summit views on Mount Kinabalu, island trips getting comfortable
About 32°C by day, dry season, good for climbing Mount Kinabalu and island hopping at Tunku Abdul Rahman
About 32°C by day, sunny, clear water at Semporna, a great time for diving
About 32°C by day, good diving season, Harvest Festival celebrations (30–31 May)
About 32°C by day, sometimes showers, high visibility at Sipadan, permits in short supply
About 32°C by day, good sea conditions, more afternoon thunderstorms on the west coast
About 32°C by day, more rain but mostly showers, wildlife easy to see along the river
About 31°C by day, lots of rain in Kota Kinabalu, still good diving at Semporna
About 31°C by day, the wettest month on the west coast, climbers often meet rain and fog
About 31°C by day, lots of rain, the east coast starts its rainy season
About 31°C by day, northeast monsoon brings heavy rain, Sandakan's rivers rise easily
highlights: Best time to dive Sipadan: turtles and barracuda tornadoes, limited daily dive permits
Climbing Mount Kinabalu, better views in the dry season, book mountain huts and permits ahead
Kaamatan Harvest Festival (30–31 May), a traditional Kadazan-Dusun celebration
Kinabatangan River boat trips: proboscis monkeys, hornbills, and with luck Borneo pygmy elephants
Green turtle nesting peak at Turtle Islands Park near Sandakan (about Jul–Oct), overnight stay must be booked
Sepilok Orangutan Rehabilitation Centre and Sun Bear Conservation Centre open all year
my-sabah.avoid: Oct to Jan has the most rain, eastern rivers flood easily and west coast climbs meet lots of rain and fog; in Sipadan's high season (about Apr–Aug) permits are very hard to get without booking ahead.
my-sabah.tips: To climb Mount Kinabalu, book mountain huts and climbing permits months ahead; a guide is required. Sipadan has limited daily permits, and you usually must stay several nights with a dive shop around Mabul or Kapalai to get one. Sabah's east coast (Semporna and around) has controls such as a night-time sea curfew, so check the latest safety advice before going.

my-sarawak.places: Kuching, Sarawak Cultural Village, Bako National Park, Semenggoh Wildlife Centre, Mulu National Park, Niah National Park, Miri, Sibu
my-sarawak.summary: Best: May–Aug is drier, and Jun has the Gawai Dayak harvest festival and the Rainforest Music Festival
my-sarawak.climate: Tropical rainforest climate, rainy all year, 30–32°C by day. Rain is heaviest in the Nov–Feb northeast monsoon, often in downpours; Jun–Aug is fairly dry, but rainforest showers can come at any time of year.
notes: About 30°C by day, peak of the northeast monsoon rains, frequent downpours, sometimes floods
