About 31°C by day, less rain, rainforest hikes slippery but doable
About 32°C by day, less rain, good for proboscis monkeys at Bako National Park
About 32°C by day, fairly dry; from month end longhouses get ready for Gawai Dayak
About 32°C by day, Gawai Dayak (1–2 Jun), Rainforest Music Festival usually in late Jun
About 32°C by day, dry season, good for longhouse visits and rainforest hikes
About 32°C by day, fairly dry, a good time for the Mulu caves and watching the bats fly out
About 32°C by day, more showers, fewer visitors, rainforest still fine
About 31°C by day, more rain, still good for Kuching city trips and caves
About 31°C by day, rainy season begins, heavy rain often from afternoon into the night
About 30°C by day, northeast monsoon arrives, lots of rain and big waves, Bako boat trips may be cancelled
highlights: Gawai Dayak harvest festival (1–2 Jun): longhouse celebrations of the Iban, Bidayuh and other peoples
Rainforest World Music Festival (usually late Jun, sometimes Jul), held at Sarawak Cultural Village
Bats flying out of Deer Cave at Mulu at dusk, most amazing on clear days
Bako National Park: proboscis monkeys, bearded pigs, trails easier in the dry season
Semenggoh orangutans: seen at the two daily feeding times, fewer show up when wild fruit is plentiful
Rafflesia at Gunung Gading National Park, no fixed flowering season, ask the park before going
my-sarawak.avoid: Dec to Feb has the most rain, rivers rise, and Bako National Park boat trips may be cancelled due to big waves; Mulu is reached by plane, and flights are sometimes delayed in rain.
my-sarawak.tips: Most visitors fly to Mulu National Park from Miri on a small plane; book flights and park rooms ahead in high season. Bako boat trips depend on the tide, and at low tide you may have to wade ashore. For the rainforest, bring dry bags and leech socks. Visit longhouses through a proper travel agency; you can bring small gifts.

sg-singapore.places: Marina Bay, Gardens by the Bay, Sentosa, Chinatown, Little India, Kampong Glam, Singapore Botanic Gardens, Singapore Zoo and Night Safari, Pulau Ubin
sg-singapore.summary: Good all year; Feb–Mar is driest, Nov–Dec has the most rain
sg-singapore.climate: Equatorial climate, about 25–32°C all year, very humid, no real dry season. In Dec–Jan the northeast monsoon brings lots of rain, Feb–Mar is driest; in the monsoon changeovers of Apr–May and Oct–Nov afternoon thunderstorms are frequent; Aug–Oct sometimes has haze.
notes: About 30°C by day, wet northeast monsoon, sometimes days of grey rain, Chinese New Year approaching
About 31°C by day, the driest month, breezier, feels the most comfortable
About 32°C by day, fairly dry and sunny, good for outdoor sights such as Marina Bay
About 32°C by day, monsoon changeover, frequent but short afternoon thunderstorms
About 32°C by day, one of the hottest months, muggy, afternoon thunderstorms
About 31°C by day, southwest monsoon, sometimes early-morning 'Sumatra squall' storms
About 31°C by day, fairly steady weather, many food and mid-year shopping events
About 31°C by day, National Day celebrations and fireworks on Aug 9, watch for haze
About 31°C by day, hotels expensive during the F1 night race (Sep or Oct), watch for haze
About 31°C by day, monsoon changeover, more thunderstorms, Little India lit up for Deepavali
About 31°C by day, one of the rainiest months, heavy rain from afternoon to evening
About 30°C by day, monsoon rainy season, Orchard Road Christmas lights and year-end holidays
highlights: Chinese New Year (the date changes every year): Chinatown lights and River Hongbao at Marina Bay
Geylang Serai Ramadan bazaar (Islamic calendar, about 11 days earlier each year)
National Day on 9 Aug: celebrations and fireworks at Marina Bay (parade tickets by ballot)
Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix night race (Sep or Oct), hotel prices soar
Deepavali (Festival of Lights, Hindu calendar, the date changes every year, usually Oct–Nov): Little India lights
Orchard Road Christmas lights (about mid Nov to early Jan)
Haze risk season, air quality affected by burning in Indonesia (how bad changes every year)
Gardens by the Bay light show and Night Safari open every night all year
sg-singapore.avoid: Nov–Dec has the most rain; Aug–Oct may bring haze; hotel prices rise clearly during the F1 race and Chinese New Year, and some hawker centres and shops close for the first two days of Chinese New Year.
sg-singapore.tips: Indoor air-conditioning is strong, so bring a light jacket; carry an umbrella for afternoon thunderstorms. No eating or drinking on the MRT, chewing gum may not be sold, and fines for littering and smoking in the wrong place are strict. Hotels are expensive, so book ahead; hawker centres are the cheap, authentic way to eat.

th-bangkok-central.places: Bangkok, Grand Palace and Wat Phra Kaew, Wat Arun, Ayutthaya, Pattaya, Hua Hin, Bridge on the River Kwai in Kanchanaburi, Maeklong Railway Market, Damnoen Saduak Floating Market
th-bangkok-central.summary: Best: Nov–Feb cool season; Apr is very hot, with Songkran; Aug–Oct is rainy
th-bangkok-central.climate: Tropical savanna climate with three clear seasons: Nov–Feb is the cool, dry season (about 22–32°C), Mar–May the hot season, often over 35°C, and Jun–Oct the rainy season, wettest in Sep, with frequent downpours from afternoon to evening.
notes: About 32°C by day, cool season, dry and sunny, the most comfortable time for temples and palaces
About 33°C by day, dry season; Chinese New Year is lively on Yaowarat Road in Chinatown
About 34°C by day, getting hot, fierce midday sun, go out early and late
About 36°C by day, the hottest month; Songkran on 13–15 Apr
About 35°C by day, very hot and humid, rainy season begins in late May with showers
About 34°C by day, early rainy season, mostly afternoon showers, cheaper hotels
About 33°C by day, mostly showers, more summer holiday visitors
About 33°C by day, more rain, afternoon downpours often flood roads
About 32°C by day, the wettest month, flooded streets, high water on the Chao Phraya River
About 32°C by day, end of the rainy season but still rainy, sometimes a flood risk
About 31°C by day, cool season begins, Loy Krathong nights with floating lanterns on the river
About 31°C by day, dry and pleasant, year-end high season, many countdown events
highlights: Songkran (fixed on 13–15 Apr), water fights liveliest on Khao San Road and Silom Road
Loy Krathong (full moon of the 12th Thai lunar month, the date changes every year, usually Nov), floating lanterns on the Chao Phraya River
River Kwai Bridge light and sound show in Kanchanaburi (about late Nov to early Dec)
Ayutthaya World Heritage celebrations (about mid Dec), light shows at the ruins and traditional performances
Chinese New Year (the date changes every year), lion dances and food on Yaowarat Road in Chinatown
Cool, dry season, good for cycling around Ayutthaya's ruins and visiting floating markets
Peak rainy season, flood risk in low-lying parts of Bangkok and around Ayutthaya
th-bangkok-central.avoid: Apr–May is very hot, often over 35°C; Sep–Oct has the most rain, with flooded streets and sometimes floods around Ayutthaya; during Songkran transport and hotels are tight, and if you don't want to get wet, stay off the streets.
th-bangkok-central.tips: To enter the Grand Palace and temples, cover shoulders and knees, and don't wear flip-flops or shorts. Bangkok traffic is very bad, so use the BTS, MRT and Chao Phraya boats. Keep your phone in a waterproof pouch at Songkran. Alcohol sales are banned at some times on Buddhist holidays. Watch for 'it's closed today' scams near the Grand Palace. Pattaya and Hua Hin have many local visitors at weekends.

th-chiang-mai-north.places: Chiang Mai Old City, Wat Phra That Doi Suthep, Doi Inthanon, Chiang Dao, Pai, Mae Hong Son, White Temple in Chiang Rai, Golden Triangle
th-chiang-mai-north.summary: Best: Nov–Jan cool season; late Feb to Apr has heavy smoke haze from burning
th-chiang-mai-north.climate: Mountain tropical monsoon climate. Nov–Feb is cool and dry, 13–18°C in the mornings and evenings and colder in the mountains; Mar–Apr is hot and affected by smoke haze from burning; May–Oct is the rainy season, wettest in Aug–Sep.
notes: About 29°C by day, about 14°C at night, cool and dry, seas of clouds in the mountains at dawn
About 31°C by day, sunny and dry; Flower Festival in early Feb, haze starts building in late Feb
About 35°C by day, the worst smoke haze from burning, PM2.5 often over safe limits, not recommended
About 37°C by day, very hot with haze still around; Songkran (13–15 Apr) at its liveliest
About 35°C by day, haze clears once the rainy season starts, still muggy
About 32°C by day, green season, rice fields turn green, afternoon showers
About 31°C by day, rainy season, bright green rice terraces in the mountains, some mountain roads slippery
About 31°C by day, heavy rain, landslide risk in the mountains, trekking limited
About 31°C by day, peak rainfall, rivers rise, Chiang Mai sometimes floods
About 31°C by day, less rain, rice fields turn golden, cooler weather
About 29°C by day, cool season begins; Loy Krathong and the Yi Peng lantern festival
About 28°C by day, about 13°C at night, mountain tops can drop below 5°C, high season
highlights: Chiang Mai Flower Festival (first weekend of Feb), flower float parade and flower shows
Yi Peng lantern festival, held with Loy Krathong (full moon of the 12th Thai lunar month, the date changes every year, usually Nov); release lanterns only at permitted sites
Songkran (fixed on 13–15 Apr), water fights liveliest along Chiang Mai's moat
Burning and haze season (about late Feb to Apr), poor air and hazy distant views
Thai sakura (wild Himalayan cherry) blooms about late Dec to Jan, best at Doi Ang Khang and other spots
Wild sunflowers (Mexican sunflowers) turn the Mae Hong Son hills gold (about Nov)
Bright green mountain rice terraces in the green season, rice turns yellow around Oct
th-chiang-mai-north.avoid: Smoke haze is worst from about late Feb to Apr, especially in Mar, so people with breathing problems should not go; Aug–Sep has heavy rain, with slippery roads and landslides in the mountains; rooms are very scarce during Loy Krathong.
th-chiang-mai-north.tips: In the cool season mornings and evenings are much colder than midday, so bring a warm jacket for the mountains. For Loy Krathong and Yi Peng, book rooms months ahead; lanterns may only be released at permitted sites, and rules are strict near the airport. The mountain road to Pai has about 762 bends, so bring medicine if you get carsick. In haze season wear an N95 mask and check the air quality index.

th-phuket-andaman.places: Phuket, Ao Nang in Krabi, Railay Beach, Phi Phi Islands, Phang Nga Bay, Similan Islands, Surin Islands, Koh Lanta
th-phuket-andaman.summary: Best: Nov–Apr dry season, clear water and small waves
th-phuket-andaman.climate: Tropical monsoon climate, about 25–33°C all year. Nov–Apr is the dry season, sunny with little rain and calm seas; in May–Oct the southwest monsoon brings heavy rain and big waves, wettest in Sep, and west coast beaches often fly red flags.
notes: About 32°C by day, peak dry season, clear water and small waves, best for boat trips
About 33°C by day, sunny with little rain, great visibility for Similan diving
About 33°C by day, hot and dry, sea conditions still good, slightly fewer visitors
About 34°C by day, the hottest month, Songkran (13–15 Apr) lively in Phuket too
About 32°C by day, southwest monsoon begins, the Similans close about mid-May
About 31°C by day, rainy season, west coast beaches often fly red flags banning swimming
About 31°C by day, many showers and big waves, island-hopping boats may be cancelled
About 31°C by day, strong wind and waves, Maya Bay closed in Aug–Sep to recover
About 30°C by day, the wettest month, downpours and big waves, sea activities very limited
About 31°C by day, less rain, the Similans open about mid-Oct, the Vegetarian Festival is often at this time
About 31°C by day, dry season returns, seas calming, high season begins
About 31°C by day, dry high season, hotel prices highest at Christmas and New Year
highlights: Open season for the Similan and Surin Islands national parks (about mid Oct to mid May)
Better chance of meeting whale sharks around Richelieu Rock (about Feb–Apr)
Maya Bay on Phi Phi closes about Aug–Sep every year to let nature recover
Phuket Vegetarian Festival (1st to 9th day of the 9th lunar month, the date changes every year), street processions
Songkran (fixed on 13–15 Apr), water fights around Patong Beach
Best season for sea kayaking in Phang Nga Bay and rock climbing at Railay Beach
Rainy season surfing: Kata and Karon beaches have waves good for beginners
th-phuket-andaman.avoid: In May–Oct the southwest monsoon brings big waves, beaches often fly red flags and island boats are cancelled, worst in Sep; the Similans close from about mid May to mid Oct; room prices double from Christmas to New Year.
th-phuket-andaman.tips: When beaches fly red flags in the rainy season, never go in the water; tourists drown every year. For island hopping choose a licensed boat company and wear a life jacket. Book rooms and boats ahead for the Dec–Jan high season. Phuket taxis are expensive, so use ride-hailing apps. National parks charge a separate entry fee, and some islands limit daily visitors.

th-samui-gulf.region: Koh Samui and the Gulf of Thailand
th-samui-gulf.places: Koh Samui, Chaweng Beach, Fisherman's Village, Koh Phangan, Koh Tao, Koh Nang Yuan, Ang Thong National Marine Park
th-samui-gulf.summary: Best: Feb–Aug dry season; Oct–Dec northeast monsoon brings lots of rain and big waves
th-samui-gulf.climate: Tropical climate, about 25–33°C all year, with a rain pattern opposite to the Andaman Sea: about Jan–Sep is fairly dry, and Oct–Dec gets lots of rain from the northeast monsoon, wettest in Nov.
notes: About 29°C by day, end of the monsoon, sometimes showers, getting sunnier mid to late Jan
About 30°C by day, turning to the dry season, calm seas, good for island hopping
About 31°C by day, sunny and dry, good diving visibility at Koh Tao
About 32°C by day, hot with little rain, Songkran (13–15 Apr) is lively
About 33°C by day, the hottest month, warm sea, sometimes showers
About 32°C by day, fairly dry, a good alternative when the Andaman Sea has its rainy season
About 32°C by day, steady weather, more summer holiday visitors, good for diving
About 32°C by day, many sunny days, good sea conditions, high-season room prices rise
About 31°C by day, more showers, still fine for boat trips, fewer visitors
About 30°C by day, northeast monsoon arrives, rain clearly increases
About 29°C by day, the wettest month, downpours and big waves, boats often cancelled
About 29°C by day, still rainy, easing from late Dec, crowded at Christmas
highlights: Koh Phangan Full Moon Party, held around each full moon on Haad Rin Sunrise Beach
Better chance of whale sharks around Koh Tao and Sail Rock (about Mar–May and Sep–Oct)
Kayaking and viewpoint hikes in Ang Thong National Marine Park, good sea conditions
Koh Tao dive course season, good visibility and lower prices
Songkran (fixed on 13–15 Apr), water fights on Chaweng's streets
Northeast monsoon rainy season, island trips to Ang Thong Marine Park and elsewhere often stopped by wind and waves
th-samui-gulf.avoid: Oct–Dec northeast monsoon, worst in Nov, with downpours and big waves, and ferries and island trips often cancelled; around the Full Moon Party, Koh Phangan rooms and boat tickets are tight.
th-samui-gulf.tips: Samui airport has few flights and high fares; you can fly to Surat Thani and then take a boat. At the Full Moon Party, watch your safety and belongings, and stay away from drugs; Thailand's drug penalties are very severe. Koh Nang Yuan charges a landing fee and bans plastic bottles. For Koh Tao dive courses choose a well-reviewed dive shop. In the rainy season check the sea forecast before boat trips.

vn-north.places: Hanoi, Ha Long Bay, Lan Ha Bay, Trang An and Tam Coc in Ninh Binh, Sa Pa, Fansipan, Ha Giang, Moc Chau
vn-north.summary: Best: Mar–Apr and Oct–Nov; summer is hot and humid with typhoons, winter is grey and cold
vn-north.climate: Subtropical monsoon climate with four clear seasons. In winter (Dec–Feb) Hanoi is about 14–20°C, grey, cold and foggy; summer (May–Sep) is hot and humid at 33–35°C, with heavy rain and typhoons; spring and autumn are the most pleasant.
notes: Hanoi daytime about 19°C, grey, cold and damp; Ha Long Bay often foggy, Sa Pa may freeze
Daytime about 20°C, lots of drizzle; most shops close around Tết
Daytime about 23°C, warming up, some light mist and drizzle; pleasant for Ninh Binh and Ha Long Bay
Daytime about 28°C, pleasant late spring; calm seas in Ha Long Bay, good for cruises
Daytime about 32°C, getting hot; Ninh Binh rice fields turn gold around late May, Sa Pa terraces filled with water
Daytime about 33°C, very hot and humid, frequent afternoon thunderstorms
Daytime about 33°C, peak rainy season; typhoons may stop Ha Long Bay cruises
Daytime about 32°C, frequent heavy rain and typhoons, landslides in the mountains
Daytime about 31°C, rice terraces at Sa Pa and Mu Cang Chai turn gold; typhoons still possible
Daytime about 29°C, clear, crisp autumn; buckwheat flowers in Ha Giang, one of the best months
Daytime about 26°C, dry with little rain; Ha Long Bay and Hanoi at their most comfortable
Daytime about 21°C, turning cold; mountain nights near 0°C, more fog
highlights: Tết (Lunar New Year, the date changes every year, usually late Jan to mid Feb); shops and transport stop for about a week around it
Plum and peach blossom season on the Moc Chau plateau (about Jan–Feb), best around Tết
Rice fields turn gold at Tam Coc, Ninh Binh (about late May to early Jun); Sa Pa terraces filled with water like mirrors
Rice ripens gold on the Sa Pa and Mu Cang Chai terraces (about mid Sep to early Oct)
Buckwheat flower season in Ha Giang (about mid Oct to Nov), seas of pink and white flowers
Typhoon season; Ha Long Bay cruises may be stopped at short notice
In cold snaps Sa Pa sometimes gets snow, and rime ice forms on top of Fansipan
vn-north.avoid: Jul–Sep is rainy with typhoons, and Ha Long Bay cruises may be stopped; for a week around Tết businesses close and tickets are hard to get; Dec–Feb is damp, cold and foggy in the mountains, often spoiling the views.
vn-north.tips: When a typhoon comes, the authorities stop all Ha Long Bay cruises, so keep your plans flexible. The Ha Giang Loop mountain roads are dangerous; riding a motorbike needs experience and a valid licence, so hiring a local rider is advised. Hanoi has little indoor heating in winter, bring warm clothes. Book tickets and rooms early around Tết.

vn-central.places: Da Nang, My Khe Beach, Ba Na Hills, Hoi An Ancient Town, My Son Sanctuary, Hue, Phong Nha-Ke Bang National Park, Son Doong Cave
vn-central.summary: Best: Feb–May, dry; Sep–Dec is typhoon and flood season
vn-central.climate: Tropical monsoon climate. Feb–Aug is the dry season, often over 35°C in Jun–Aug; Sep–Dec is the rainy season, with typhoons and floods mostly in Oct–Nov, and low-lying parts of Hoi An and Hue flood easily.
notes: Daytime about 25°C, end of the rainy season, many cloudy days and light rain, sea is cool
Daytime about 26°C, drying out; Hoi An decorated with lanterns for Tết, pleasant weather
Daytime about 28°C, sunny and dry, good for old-town walks and beaches
Daytime about 30°C, settled weather, sea warming up, one of the best months
Daytime about 33°C, getting hot; beach season, good time for caving
Daytime about 35°C, very hot; the Da Nang International Fireworks Festival often falls around now
Daytime about 35°C, the hottest time; avoid being outdoors at noon, beaches crowded
Daytime about 34°C, hot, some thunderstorms; the rainy season nears by month's end
Daytime about 31°C, rainy season begins, typhoon risk rises, some caves close
Daytime about 29°C, peak of heavy rain and typhoons; Hoi An Ancient Town often floods
Daytime about 27°C, frequent floods, transport often disrupted, not for beach trips
Daytime about 25°C, still rainy, some cold snaps, rough seas
highlights: Hoi An lantern night on the 14th of every lunar month: the old town turns off its lights and floats lanterns on the river
Da Nang International Fireworks Festival (mostly on weekends in Jun–Jul, dates announced each year)
Phong Nha-Ke Bang cave season; Son Doong expeditions run about Feb–Aug and must be booked far ahead
My Khe Beach swimming season, calm seas
Tết (Lunar New Year, the date changes every year): traditional New Year decorations in Hue and Hoi An
Peak of typhoons and floods; low-lying parts of Hoi An Ancient Town often flood
vn-central.avoid: Sep–Dec is the rainy season, with typhoons and floods worst in Oct–Nov; low parts of Hoi An and Hue often flood and caves close. In Jun–Aug days are often over 35°C.
vn-central.tips: In the rainy season watch typhoon forecasts and keep plans flexible. Son Doong places are very few and must be booked far ahead through the official licensed operator. The top of Ba Na Hills is about 8–10°C cooler than the city, bring a jacket. Hoi An Ancient Town needs a ticket; it is crowded at night, so watch your belongings.

vn-south-central.places: Nha Trang, Da Lat, Mui Ne, Phan Thiet, Quy Nhon, Phu Yen, Phan Rang
vn-south-central.summary: Best: Feb–Apr; Da Lat is cool all year, Oct–Dec is the coastal rainy season with many typhoons
vn-south-central.climate: Tropical coastal climate: about Jan–Aug is dry, Sep–Dec is rainy with many typhoons. Da Lat is about 1,500 m up, 15–25°C all year, with frequent afternoon rain in May–Oct. Mui Ne is one of the driest coasts in Vietnam.
notes: Nha Trang daytime about 27°C, end of the rains and clearing up; Da Lat dry, nights about 12°C

Daytime about 30°C, sunny with little rain; kitesurfing still busy in Mui Ne
Daytime about 31°C, best sea conditions; good visibility for diving in Nha Trang
Daytime about 32°C, hot on the coast; afternoon showers start in Da Lat

Daytime about 29°C, rain rises sharply, typhoon and flood risk goes up

Daytime about 27°C, rain easing but unsettled; wild sunflowers in bloom in Da Lat

Kitesurfing and windsurfing season in Mui Ne (about Nov to Apr), strong winds

Wild sunflower (Mexican sunflower) season in Da Lat
Tết (the date changes every year): busy flower market in Da Lat, peak for local tourists
Rainy season typhoons and floods; sea activities in Nha Trang and Quy Nhon often stop
vn-south-central.avoid: Oct–Dec is the rainy season, with typhoons and floods worst in Nov, affecting beaches and boat trips; over Tết hotels in Da Lat and Nha Trang are full and prices jump.
vn-south-central.tips: Da Lat is about 1,500 m up and cool in the mornings and evenings, bring a jacket. In Mui Ne's windy season the waves are big, not good for ordinary swimming but good for kitesurfing. The mountain road from Nha Trang to Da Lat has many bends; bring medicine if you get carsick. Around Tết there are huge numbers of local tourists, so book transport and rooms early.

vn-south.places: Ho Chi Minh City, Cu Chi Tunnels, My Tho, Can Tho, Phu Quoc, Con Dao, Vung Tau
vn-south.summary: Best: Dec–Mar dry season; afternoon thunderstorms May–Oct, big waves at Phu Quoc Jun–Sep
vn-south.climate: Tropical savanna climate, 26–35°C all year. Dec–Apr is the dry season, hottest in Mar–Apr; May–Nov is the rainy season, mostly short afternoon downpours. Phu Quoc has big waves in Jun–Sep with the southwest monsoon.
notes: Daytime about 32°C, dry season; clear water at Phu Quoc, the best time

Con Dao turtle nesting season (about May–Oct), with national park turtle-watching trips

vn-south.tips: Ho Chi Minh City has many motorbikes: cross the road at a steady pace, and watch out for phone snatchers on bikes. Phu Quoc has visa-free entry for foreign visitors (check the latest rules). Mekong floating markets need an early-morning start. Con Dao has few flights, book early; much of the island is managed as a national park.

kh-cambodia.places: Angkor Wat in Siem Reap, Bayon, Ta Prohm, Banteay Srei, Tonle Sap Lake, Phnom Penh, Sihanoukville, Koh Rong, Kampot, Kep
kh-cambodia.summary: Best: Nov–Feb, cool and dry; Apr–May very hot, Aug–Oct rainy
kh-cambodia.climate: Tropical monsoon climate. Nov–Feb is cool and dry (about 21–32°C); Mar–May is very hot, often over 35°C; May–Oct is the rainy season, wettest in Sep–Oct, when Tonle Sap Lake rises sharply.
notes: Daytime about 31°C, cool and dry; Angkor sunrises most reliable, most visitors
Daytime about 33°C, dry and sunny, comfortable sightseeing, slowly getting hotter
Daytime about 35°C, hot and dry; visit early morning and late afternoon
Daytime about 36°C, hottest of the year; many go home for Khmer New Year (mid Apr)
Daytime about 35°C, very hot; rainy season begins late in the month

Daytime about 30°C, cool and dry, high season; crowds at Angkor sunrise
highlights: Khmer New Year (mid Apr, three days from about the 13th or 14th); many people go home
Pchum Ben (Khmer calendar, the date changes every year, usually late Sep to Oct), about three days of national holiday
Water Festival (full moon in the Khmer calendar, the date changes every year, usually Nov): boat races on the Tonle Sap River in Phnom Penh
Around the spring equinox (about 20 Mar) and autumn equinox (about 22 Sep), the sun rises over Angkor Wat's central tower
Tonle Sap high-water season, best for boat trips to floating villages and flooded forest
Kampot and Kep dry season: pepper farms, crab market, calm seas at Koh Rong
kh-cambodia.avoid: Apr–May is very hot, often over 36°C; Sep–Oct is the peak of the rainy season, with muddy country roads; during Khmer New Year and Pchum Ben transport is crowded and many shops close.
kh-cambodia.tips: Angkor passes come as 1-day, 3-day and 7-day; your photo is taken on site for the named pass. Temples require covered shoulders and knees, and some high towers have an extra dress check. Angkor Wat sunrise is packed in the cool season; you can watch sunrise at another temple instead. US dollars are widely used, small change often comes in riel. For a beach break, take a boat from Sihanoukville to Koh Rong.

la-laos.places: Luang Prabang, Kuang Si Falls, Vang Vieng, Vientiane, Pakse, Wat Phou, Four Thousand Islands (Si Phan Don), Plain of Jars
la-laos.summary: Best: Nov–Feb cool season; Mar–Apr smoke haze in the north, Aug–Sep heavy rain
la-laos.climate: Tropical monsoon climate. Nov–Feb is cool and dry, with northern mountain nights below 10°C; Mar–May is hot, with smoke haze from field burning in the north; May–Oct is the rainy season, heaviest in Aug–Sep.
notes: Luang Prabang daytime about 27°C, mornings and evenings about 12°C, dry with morning mist
Daytime about 30°C, sunny and dry; Kuang Si Falls bright blue
Daytime about 33°C, field-burning haze starts in the north, distant views blurred
Daytime about 35°C, hottest month with heavy haze; water splashing for Lao New Year (mid Apr)

Daytime about 30°C, Boun Ok Phansa: boat lanterns and boat races; weather turning dry
Daytime about 29°C, cool season begins; That Luang Festival in Vientiane
Daytime about 27°C, dry; northern nights can drop below 10°C, high season

Boun Ok Phansa (full moon of the 11th Buddhist month, the date changes every year, usually Oct): boat lanterns in Luang Prabang, boat races in Vientiane
That Luang Festival (full moon of the 12th Buddhist month, the date changes every year, usually Nov): pilgrims at Pha That Luang in Vientiane
Morning alms giving in Luang Prabang, every day around 6 am
Cool season: low water at the Four Thousand Islands shows sandbars, good for cycling round the islands (Irrawaddy dolphins are now gone from Laos)
Northern burning-haze season; poor air in Luang Prabang, flights sometimes affected
la-laos.avoid: Mar–Apr brings heavy field-burning haze in the north and high heat; Aug–Sep has heavy rain, landslides on mountain roads and muddy Kuang Si Falls; transport is busy around Lao New Year.
la-laos.tips: At the Luang Prabang alms giving keep your distance and use no flash; don't join in unless you know the customs. Don't go in the river at Vang Vieng after drinking. The Laos–China Railway links Vientiane, Vang Vieng and Luang Prabang; tickets are often tight, so buy early. Laos still has unexploded bombs from the war; in remote areas don't leave the road.

mm-myanmar.places: Yangon, Shwedagon Pagoda, Bagan, Mandalay, U Bein Bridge, Inle Lake, Golden Rock (Kyaiktiyo), Ngapali Beach
mm-myanmar.summary: Best: Nov–Feb cool season; Mar–May very hot, Jun–Sep coastal rainy season
mm-myanmar.climate: Tropical monsoon climate. Nov–Feb is cool and dry; Mar–May is very hot, up to 40°C in the central dry zone; Jun–Sep brings the southwest monsoon, with heavy rain in Yangon and on the Rakhine coast, while the dry zone around Bagan gets less rain.
notes: Bagan daytime about 30°C, cool mornings and evenings; cool, dry season, the traditional hot-air balloon season
Daytime about 33°C, dry and sunny; Inle Lake about 10°C in the early morning
Daytime about 36°C, getting hot; Bagan hot at noon, fewer visitors
Daytime about 38°C, hottest of the year; national holiday for the Thingyan water festival (mid Apr)
Daytime about 37°C, very hot; the southwest monsoon arrives late in the month
Daytime about 32°C, rainy season, heavy rain in Yangon and on the coast; most Ngapali hotels close

Daytime about 31°C, heavy rain in Yangon, Inle Lake water rising

Daytime about 31°C, rain stopping; lights everywhere for Thadingyut, the festival of lights
Daytime about 30°C, cool season begins; Taunggyi fire balloon festival, Ngapali reopens
Daytime about 29°C, dry and comfortable, high season, good for travel everywhere
highlights: Thingyan water festival (about 13–16 Apr), national holiday, transport and shops affected
Bagan hot-air balloon season (traditionally about Oct to Mar; check how it has run recently before you go)
Phaung Daw Oo festival at Inle Lake (Burmese calendar, the date changes every year): a golden bird-shaped barge tours the lake
Thadingyut festival of lights (full moon in the Burmese calendar, the date changes every year, usually Oct): pagodas and homes lit up
Taunggyi fire balloon festival (Tazaungdaing festival of lights, full moon in the Burmese calendar, the date changes every year, usually Nov)
Ngapali Beach season, calm sea, good for a beach holiday
mm-myanmar.avoid: Mar–May is very hot, Bagan often reaches 40°C; Jun–Sep is the coastal rainy season and most of Ngapali closes; during Thingyan most shops and offices close.
mm-myanmar.tips: Before going, check the latest safety situation and visa rules; some areas are closed to foreign visitors, and routes and transport may change at short notice. Take off shoes and socks to enter pagodas, and dress modestly. For changing money, flat, crease-free new US dollar notes work best. Climbing the Bagan pagodas is now banned.

ph-manila-luzon.places: Manila, Intramuros, Baguio, Banaue Rice Terraces, Sagada, Vigan, Taal Volcano, Anilao in Batangas
ph-manila-luzon.summary: Best: Dec–Mar dry season; Jul–Oct lots of rain from typhoons and the southwest monsoon
ph-manila-luzon.climate: Tropical monsoon climate. Dec–May is the dry season (cooler Dec–Feb, hot Mar–May); Jun–Nov is the rainy season, with typhoons and the southwest monsoon bringing heavy rain and floods in Jul–Oct. Baguio is about 1,500 m up and cool all year.
notes: Manila daytime about 30°C, cool and dry; Baguio nights about 12°C
Daytime about 31°C, dry season, Baguio flower festival parade, clear skies

Daytime about 31°C, rain easing, fewer typhoons but still possible
Daytime about 30°C, dry season begins; Christmas decorations make malls and churches lively

Baguio flower festival, Panagbenga (Feb, float parades mostly on a late-month weekend)
Holy Week (the week before Easter, the date changes every year), sights and transport packed
Banaue terraces at their greenest; Sagada caves and hiking trails in better shape
Rice turns gold and is harvested on the Banaue and Batad terraces (about Jun–Jul)
Macro diving at Anilao, Batangas, best sea conditions in the dry season

Typhoon season, frequent flight cancellations and landslides on mountain roads
ph-manila-luzon.avoid: Jul–Oct brings typhoons and the southwest monsoon; Aug is wettest, low parts of Manila often flood and mountain roads slide easily. Transport and rooms are tight around Holy Week and Christmas.
ph-manila-luzon.tips: Manila traffic is terrible, allow plenty of time, and avoid walking alone in quiet areas at night. Most people take the overnight bus to Banaue, 9 hours or more. When a typhoon comes, follow warnings from PAGASA, the Philippine weather bureau; ferries and flights often stop. Sagada caves need a local guide.

ph-boracay.places: White Beach, Puka Beach, Friday's Beach, Bulabog Beach, Mount Luho, Crocodile Island, Kalibo
ph-boracay.summary: Best: Dec–Apr, the northeast wind season, when White Beach is calm
ph-boracay.climate: Tropical climate, about 25–32°C all year. Nov–Apr has the northeast wind (Amihan), and the White Beach side is calm; Jun–Oct has the southwest monsoon (Habagat), with big waves and lots of rain on White Beach, and sometimes typhoons.
notes: Daytime about 29°C, northeast wind, White Beach calm, high season
Daytime about 30°C, dry and sunny, clear water, sailboat sunsets at their best
Daytime about 31°C, sunny with little rain, kitesurfing still busy on Bulabog Beach

Daytime about 30°C, strong southwest monsoon; typhoons sometimes affect flights and ferries

Daytime about 30°C, typhoons still possible; the monsoon changes at month's end
Daytime about 30°C, northeast wind returns, sea calming, high season begins
Daytime about 29°C, dry season; Christmas and New Year room prices highest, book ahead
highlights: Northeast wind season (Amihan): White Beach calm, good for swimming and sailing
Kitesurfing season on Bulabog Beach (about Nov to Mar)
In the southwest monsoon White Beach has big waves, but Bulabog Beach on the east side is calmer
Ati-Atihan Festival in Kalibo (around the third Sunday of Jan); Kalibo is about 1.5–2 hours by road from Caticlan port
Holy Week (the date changes every year), huge numbers of local tourists
Evening paraw sailboat sunset trips on White Beach
ph-boracay.avoid: Jun–Oct brings the southwest monsoon: big waves and lots of seaweed on White Beach, and flights and ferries cancelled in typhoons. Crowds and high prices over Holy Week, Christmas–New Year and Chinese New Year.
ph-boracay.tips: To go over to the island you pay an environmental fee and terminal fee at Caticlan port and show your hotel booking. Smoking, drinking and building sandcastles on White Beach are banned (check current rules). Kalibo airport is about 1.5–2 hours by road from the port; Caticlan airport is closer but has fewer flights and higher fares.

ph-cebu-bohol.places: Cebu City, Mactan Island, Moalboal, Oslob, Chocolate Hills, Tarsier Sanctuary, Panglao Island, Balicasag Island
ph-cebu-bohol.summary: Best: Jan–Apr dry season; Oct–Dec higher typhoon risk
ph-cebu-bohol.climate: Tropical climate, about 24–32°C all year. About Jan–May is the dry season with calm seas; Jun–Dec is wetter, and typhoons cross the Visayas more often in Oct–Dec.
notes: Daytime about 30°C, dry season begins; Sinulog festival in Cebu (third Sunday of Jan)
Daytime about 30°C, sunny and dry, good seas for island-hopping and diving
Daytime about 31°C, dry; great snorkelling visibility at Balicasag Island
Daytime about 32°C, hot; many local tourists over Holy Week

Moalboal sardine run, seen all year, even by snorkelling
Oslob whale shark watching open all year (feeding-based, with ecological concerns)

ph-cebu-bohol.avoid: Oct–Dec has higher typhoon risk and ferries often stop; rooms in Cebu are tight and pricey during Sinulog and Holy Week; Oslob is crowded early in the morning.
ph-cebu-bohol.tips: Oslob whale shark watching uses feeding, which raises ecological concerns; if that bothers you, choose another trip. See tarsiers only at proper sanctuaries, not places that offer holding photos. The fast ferry from Cebu to Bohol takes about 2 hours and stops under typhoon warnings. When snorkelling in Moalboal, watch for passing boats.

ph-palawan.summary: Best: Dec–Apr dry season for island-hopping; Jun–Oct rough seas often stop boats
ph-palawan.climate: Tropical climate, about 25–33°C all year. Dec–May is the dry season with calm seas; in Jun–Oct the southwest monsoon brings rain, wind and waves; Coron in the north is sometimes hit by typhoons, the south less so.
notes: Daytime about 30°C, dry season, calm sea, best for El Nido island-hopping

Daytime about 30°C, peak rainy season, Coron routes affected; low-season prices

ph-palawan.avoid: Jun–Oct brings the southwest monsoon; island-hopping and ferries are often cancelled because of the sea, and the Coron area also gets typhoons. Rooms are tight and pricey over Christmas–New Year and Holy Week.
ph-palawan.tips: El Nido charges an eco-tourism fee, and some lagoons have daily limits, so book through a licensed agency. The Underground River needs an entry permit booked ahead. ATMs on the islands are few and often run out of cash; bring plenty of cash. Kayangan Lake in Coron is busy at weekends, go early.

ph-siargao-mindanao.summary: Best: Apr–May for island-hopping, Sep–Oct for surfing; Dec–Feb rainy season
ph-siargao-mindanao.climate: Tropical climate on the Pacific side, about 25–32°C all year. Nov–Feb, the northeast monsoon period, is rainy; Mar–Oct is fairly dry, and Aug–Nov brings bigger Pacific swells. Most of Mindanao lies south of the main typhoon track.
notes: Daytime about 29°C, northeast monsoon rainy season, lots of rain and wind, island-hopping often cancelled

Northeast monsoon rainy season: rough seas at Siargao, flights and ferries sometimes affected
ph-siargao-mindanao.avoid: Dec–Feb is the rainy season, with strong wind and waves and island-hopping often cancelled; beginner surfers should avoid the big waves of Sep–Oct, or pick a beginner break.
ph-siargao-mindanao.tips: Parts of Mindanao carry government travel warnings; check the latest safety situation before going. Siargao and Camiguin are popular tourist areas; check even more carefully before going anywhere else. Getting around Siargao is mostly by motorbike, ride safely. ATMs on the island are few and often run out of cash; bring plenty of cash.

id-bali.places: Ubud, Tegallalang Rice Terraces, Seminyak, Canggu, Uluwatu, Nusa Dua, Tanah Lot, Nusa Penida
id-bali.summary: Best: May–Sep dry season; Dec–Feb rainy season, the whole island shuts for Nyepi in Mar
id-bali.climate: Tropical monsoon climate, about 24–31°C all year. Apr–Oct is the dry season, coolest and driest in Jul–Aug; Nov–Mar is the rainy season, hot and humid with frequent afternoon and night downpours. Inland hills such as Ubud are cooler and wetter.
notes: Daytime about 30°C, peak rainy season, afternoon or night downpours, lots of rubbish on Kuta Beach

Bali Arts Festival (about mid Jun to mid Jul), traditional dance and music in Denpasar

id-bali.avoid: Dec–Feb is the peak of the rainy season, with lots of rubbish on west coast beaches; on Nyepi you can't go out and there are no flights; Jul–Aug and Christmas–New Year have the most visitors and highest room prices.
id-bali.tips: On Nyepi the whole island closes; even in hotels you must keep quiet with lights off, so avoid that day or check in beforehand. Foreign visitors pay a tourist levy on arrival (check the latest rules). Nusa Penida has poor roads and big waves; don't swim at some beaches. Wear a sarong to enter temples. Drink bottled water and watch out for stomach upsets.

id-lombok-gili.places: Gili Trawangan, Gili Meno, Gili Air, Mount Rinjani, Kuta (Lombok), Selong Belanak Beach, Sendang Gile Waterfall
id-lombok-gili.summary: Best: May–Sep dry season, Rinjani open; Jan–Mar rainy season, the mountain is closed
id-lombok-gili.climate: Tropical climate, about 24–32°C all year. May–Oct is the dry season, sunny; Nov–Mar is the rainy season with rougher seas, and Mount Rinjani closes about Jan–Mar. The top of Rinjani can be near 0°C before dawn.
notes: Daytime about 30°C, rainy season; Rinjani trekking closed, rough seas for ferries

id-lombok-gili.avoid: Jan–Mar is the rainy season: Rinjani closes and Bali–Gili fast boats are often cancelled for big waves; in the Jul–Aug high season rooms on the Gilis are tight.
id-lombok-gili.tips: The Gili Islands have no motor vehicles; get around on foot or by bicycle. Rinjani treks must go with a licensed guide; the 2–3 day trip is physically hard. Lombok is fairly conservative, so dress modestly away from the beach. Fast boat safety varies; choose a well-reviewed company and don't risk going out in big waves.

id-java.places: Yogyakarta, Borobudur, Prambanan, Mount Bromo, Ijen Crater, Jakarta, Bandung, Malang
id-java.summary: Best: May–Sep dry season, a good chance of volcano sunrises
id-java.climate: Tropical monsoon climate; lowlands about 24–32°C all year. May–Oct is the dry season, Nov–Apr the rainy season (wettest Jan–Feb). Highlands such as Bromo and Ijen can drop below 5°C before dawn.
notes: Yogyakarta daytime about 30°C, peak rainy season; Jakarta floods easily

id-java.avoid: Dec–Feb is the peak rainy season and volcano sunrises are often clouded over; for a week around Eid al-Fitr people travel home, trains and flights are hard to book and sights are packed; sites close at short notice when volcanoes are active.
id-java.tips: Climbing Borobudur has limited places; buy the special ticket and book online ahead. Bromo and Ijen need a pre-dawn start; bring a thick jacket and a head torch. Ijen's sulphur gas stings, bring a gas mask. Follow official Indonesian warnings on volcano status. During Ramadan, eat and drink discreetly in front of Muslims in the daytime.

id-komodo-flores.places: Labuan Bajo, Komodo Island, Rinca Island, Padar Island, Pink Beach, Manta Point (Makassar Reef), Kelimutu's three coloured lakes, Wae Rebo village
id-komodo-flores.summary: Best: May–Sep dry season for island-hopping and diving; Jan–Feb rainy season, rough seas
id-komodo-flores.climate: One of the driest parts of Indonesia, about 24–33°C all year. Apr–Nov is the dry season, when the hills slowly turn gold; Dec–Mar is the rainy season, with rougher seas. Highlands such as Kelimutu are cool in the early morning.
notes: Daytime about 31°C, rainy season, rough seas, some liveaboard trips stopped

id-komodo-flores.tips: Komodo National Park fees and entry rules have changed several times recently; check the latest rules before going. Seeing Komodo dragons on the islands requires a ranger; women on their period should tell the ranger. Choose a liveaboard with safety gear and a licence. For sunrise at Kelimutu, leave Moni village before dawn.

id-sumatra.places: Lake Toba, Samosir Island, Medan, Bukit Lawang, Bukittinggi, Mentawai Islands, Bintan, Batam
id-sumatra.summary: Best: Apr–Jul; Mentawai surf season about Apr–Oct, watch for haze in Aug–Oct
id-sumatra.climate: Equatorial rainforest climate with rain spread through the year. The north (Medan, Lake Toba) is fairly dry about Feb–Jul and wettest in Sep–Dec. Lake Toba is about 900 m up and cooler. Aug–Oct often brings haze from forest burning.

id-sumatra.tips: Bukit Lawang treks need a licensed guide; don't feed or touch the orangutans. Mentawai surf boat trips need booking months ahead and suit intermediate to advanced surfers. Bintan and Batam are about 1 hour by boat from Singapore, busy at weekends and in Singapore holidays. Sumatra is in an earthquake zone; note the tsunami evacuation signs.

id-raja-ampat-papua.places: Sorong, Waisai, Waigeo Island, Piaynemo, Kri Island, Arborek, Misool, Baliem Valley
id-raja-ampat-papua.summary: Best: Oct–Mar liveaboard diving season; Jun–Aug big waves with the southeast monsoon
id-raja-ampat-papua.climate: Equatorial climate, about 25–32°C all year, with rain spread through the year and no clear dry season. Oct–Apr has calm seas, best for liveaboard diving; in Jun–Sep the southeast monsoon makes the sea rough. The Baliem Valley is about 1,600 m up and cooler.

id-raja-ampat-papua.tips: Entering Raja Ampat requires a marine park entry card (fee per current rules). The ferry from Sorong to Waisai takes about 2 hours. Island stays are mostly simple homestays with limited power and internet; bring plenty of cash. Parts of the Papua highlands carry safety warnings; check the latest situation before going to the Baliem Valley.

bn-brunei.places: Bandar Seri Begawan, Omar Ali Saifuddien Mosque, Jame' Asr Hassanil Bolkiah Mosque, Water Village (Kampong Ayer), Istana Nurul Iman, Brunei River mangroves, Ulu Temburong National Park
bn-brunei.summary: Best: Feb–Apr, drier; Oct–Jan rainy, some services limited in Ramadan
bn-brunei.climate: Equatorial rainforest climate, hot and humid all year, about 24–33°C. Feb–Apr is fairly dry; Oct–Jan has the most rain. Sometimes hit by regional forest-burning haze.

bn-brunei.tips: Brunei bans the sale of alcohol, and drinking in public is not allowed. Wear long sleeves and trousers to enter mosques; women need a robe, usually lent on site. Many shops close for Friday prayers, about 12 to 2 pm. During Ramadan don't eat or drink in public in the daytime. Since the Temburong Bridge opened, you can drive to the national park.

in-north-plains.places: Delhi, Taj Mahal in Agra, Jaipur, Varanasi, Jodhpur, Udaipur, Jaisalmer desert, Pushkar
in-north-plains.summary: Best: Nov–Feb cool dry season; Oct and Mar also good
in-north-plains.climate: Continental monsoon climate. Apr–Jun is very hot, often over 40°C in Delhi and Rajasthan; Jul–Sep brings monsoon rain and muggy heat; Oct–Mar is dry and sunny, with frequent morning fog and cold nights in Dec–Jan.

in-north-plains.tips: The Taj Mahal is closed on Fridays. Trains and hotels are tight during Diwali and Holi, so book ahead. Winter mornings and evenings are much colder than the daytime, bring a jacket. At Holi, protect your eyes and camera from coloured powder; women travelling alone should take care. Drink only bottled water and be careful with food hygiene.

in-ladakh-himachal.places: Leh, Pangong Lake, Nubra Valley, Manali, Shimla, Dharamshala, Spiti Valley, Rohtang Pass
in-ladakh-himachal.summary: Best: Jun–Sep for the Ladakh plateau, Apr–Jun for the Himachal hill towns
in-ladakh-himachal.climate: Ladakh is a cold high desert: summer days about 25°C with cool nights, winter down to -20°C. The Himachal mountains have four clear seasons, with monsoon rain and landslides in Jul–Aug and snow up high in winter.

highlights: Pangong Lake and Nubra Valley plateau road-trip season
Hemis Festival, on the 10th day of the 5th Tibetan month, usually Jun–Jul

Apple blossom in Himachal
Kullu Dussehra, lasting about a week, the date changes every year

Snow scenes in Shimla and Manali
in-ladakh-himachal.avoid: Nov–Mar Ladakh is bitterly cold and the roads are closed, so you can only fly in; Jul–Aug brings monsoon rain to Himachal, with landslides cutting mountain roads.
in-ladakh-himachal.tips: Leh is about 3,500 m up; rest at least 1–2 days after flying in before doing much, to prevent altitude sickness. Foreign visitors need a Protected Area Permit (PAP) for Pangong Lake and Nubra Valley, which an agency can arrange. Mountain roads are steep and often cut, so allow spare days. Big temperature swings between day and night: bring a down jacket and use sun protection.

in-goa.places: Panaji, churches of Old Goa, Baga Beach, Anjuna, Palolem Beach, Arambol, Dudhsagar Falls
in-goa.summary: Best: Nov–Feb dry season for beaches, liveliest in Dec
in-goa.climate: Tropical monsoon climate, about 24–33°C all year. In Jun–Sep the southwest monsoon brings heavy rain and big waves; it turns dry from Oct, Nov–Feb is sunny with little rain, and Mar–May gets more and more muggy.

in-goa.avoid: Jun–Aug brings monsoon downpours and dangerous waves, and most beach shacks and water sports close. From Christmas to New Year's Day room prices double and it is packed.
in-goa.tips: For late Dec to early Jan, book rooms months ahead. In the monsoon red flags often ban swimming; always obey them. Renting a motorbike needs an international driving permit; ride carefully at night. North Goa is lively for parties, South Goa is quiet for relaxing. Use sun protection and mosquito repellent.

in-kerala-south.places: Kochi, Alleppey backwaters, Munnar tea estates, Varkala, Periyar, Mysore, Hampi, Madurai
in-kerala-south.summary: Best: Dec–Feb, dry and pleasant, good for houseboats on the backwaters and the Hampi ruins
in-kerala-south.climate: Tropical climate, coast about 25–33°C all year. Kerala has heavy southwest monsoon rain in Jun–Aug and northeast monsoon showers in Oct–Nov; hill areas like Munnar are about 15–25°C; inland Hampi nears 40°C in Apr–May.

Onam, Kerala's harvest festival, set by the Malayalam calendar, the date changes every year

Pongal harvest festival (Tamil, mid Jan)
Monsoon Ayurveda treatment season
in-kerala-south.avoid: Jun–Jul brings monsoon downpours to Kerala, and the beaches are unsafe for swimming; in Apr–May inland Hampi and Mysore are very hot, often near 40°C.
in-kerala-south.tips: Book houseboats early for the high season (Dec–Jan), and choose a licensed operator. Take off shoes and cover shoulders and knees in temples; some temples don't admit non-Hindus. Varkala's clifftop path has no railings, take care at night. In the rainy season guard against mosquitoes and damp.

in-darjeeling-sikkim.places: Darjeeling, Gangtok, Pelling, Lachung, Yumthang Valley, Tsomgo Lake, Shillong, Kaziranga National Park
in-darjeeling-sikkim.summary: Best: Oct–Nov for views of Kangchenjunga, Apr for rhododendrons
in-darjeeling-sikkim.climate: Eastern Himalayan mountain climate. Darjeeling and Gangtok are about 1,600–2,100 m up, about 10–20°C in spring and autumn; the Jun–Sep monsoon is very wet with frequent landslides; winter is cold and dry, with snow up high.

in-darjeeling-sikkim.avoid: Jul–Aug has monsoon downpours, landslides often close roads and the mountains can hardly be seen; Kaziranga closes for the rains about May–Oct; some North Sikkim roads close in winter.
in-darjeeling-sikkim.tips: Foreign visitors need a Restricted Area Permit (RAP) for Sikkim, available at the border or online; North Sikkim and Tsomgo Lake need an extra permit and a group tour through a local agency. Indian visitors surge during Durga Puja and Diwali, book rooms early. Mountain roads have many bends that cause carsickness; allow spare days in the rainy season.

np-nepal.places: Kathmandu, Bhaktapur, Pokhara, Chitwan National Park, Lumbini, Nagarkot, Annapurna trek, Everest Base Camp trek
np-nepal.summary: Best: Oct–Nov autumn trekking, Mar–Apr rhododendron season
np-nepal.climate: Huge differences from south to north: the Terai plains can reach 38°C in summer, while the Kathmandu Valley is about 1,400 m up and mild all year. The Jun–Sep monsoon is rainy, with muddy trails and leeches; skies are clearest in Oct–Nov, and the high mountains are cold in winter.
notes: Kathmandu daytime about 18°C, nights near 2°C; good for low-altitude treks
About 20°C, sunny and dry; still cold up high, passes may have snow
About 25°C, rhododendrons blooming, spring trekking season begins

np-nepal.avoid: The Jun–Aug monsoon is rainy: mountains hidden by cloud, muddy trails, frequent landslides and flight cancellations. During Dashain some shops and transport stop.
np-nepal.tips: Treks need the right permits and park entry tickets; most national parks now require trekkers to hire a licensed guide. Above 3,000 m, climb no more than about 500 m a day to prevent altitude sickness. Lukla flights are often delayed by weather; allow 2–3 spare days. Book tickets early for the autumn high season and Dashain.

bt-bhutan.places: Thimphu, Paro, Tiger's Nest (Paro Taktsang), Punakha Dzong, Dochula Pass, Phobjikha Valley, Bumthang, Haa Valley
bt-bhutan.summary: Best: Mar–Apr for spring flowers and the Paro Tshechu, Oct–Nov for clear, crisp autumn
bt-bhutan.climate: Mountain climate. Paro and Thimphu are about 2,200–2,400 m up, about 15–25°C in spring and autumn; Punakha is lower and warmer. The Jun–Aug monsoon brings lots of rain and fog; winter is sunny and cold, with nights often below 0°C.

bt-bhutan.avoid: The Jun–Aug monsoon is rainy, mountain roads slide easily and the snow peaks are mostly hidden by cloud; during tshechu festivals flights and hotels are tight and pricey.
bt-bhutan.tips: Visitors must pay a Sustainable Development Fee per person per night (check the latest official rate); touring outside Thimphu and Paro usually needs a licensed guide, generally arranged through an agency. Wear long sleeves and long trousers to visit dzongs. The Tiger's Nest round trip takes about 4–5 hours, start early. Paro has few flights, book early.

lk-southwest-coast.places: Colombo, Bentota, Hikkaduwa, Galle Fort, Unawatuna, Mirissa, Tangalle, Yala National Park
lk-southwest-coast.summary: Best: Dec–Mar dry season, good for beaches, whale watching and the old town
lk-southwest-coast.climate: Tropical climate, about 27–31°C all year. In May–Sep the southwest monsoon brings lots of rain and big waves to the southwest coast; Dec–Mar is the dry season, sunny with little rain and a calm sea; Oct–Nov is the monsoon changeover, with many showers.

lk-southwest-coast.avoid: May–Jun has the strongest southwest monsoon, with dangerous waves and whale watching stopped; Oct–Nov has many showers; Yala National Park closes about Sep to mid Oct.
lk-southwest-coast.tips: In the monsoon there are often rip currents; watch for red flag warnings and don't swim where there is no lifeguard. Christmas to Jan is high season, book sea-view hotels early. On every full moon day (Poya) alcohol sales are banned nationwide. Take off shoes and cover shoulders and knees at Buddhist temples, and don't take selfies with your back to a Buddha statue.

lk-hill-country.summary: Best: Jan–Mar, sunny and dry; Kandy Esala Perahera in Aug
lk-hill-country.climate: The Cultural Triangle is in the dry zone, about 27–33°C all year, with its main rains in Oct–Dec. The central hills are cool, Nuwara Eliya about 15–22°C; in May–Sep the western slopes get monsoon rain and fog.

lk-hill-country.avoid: The Oct–Nov northeast monsoon is rainy and mountain roads slide easily; in May–Sep the western hill slopes are foggy and rainy, with poor views at Horton Plains and Adam's Peak.
lk-hill-country.tips: Book seats on popular mountain trains ahead, online or at the station. Climb Lion Rock early in the morning to avoid the heat and crowds. At the Temple of the Tooth wear light-coloured clothes and cover shoulders and knees. The hills are cool mornings and evenings, bring a light jacket. Rooms are tight over the April New Year and the Esala Perahera, book ahead.

lk-east-north.summary: Best: May–Sep, the east coast dry season, for beaches, surfing and snorkelling
lk-east-north.climate: The east coast is in the southwest monsoon's rain shadow: May–Sep is sunny and dry with a calm sea, about 30–34°C; in Oct–Jan the northeast monsoon brings heavy rain, wind and waves. Jaffna in the north is hot and dry, with its rains mostly in Oct–Dec.

lk-east-north.avoid: Nov–Dec brings northeast monsoon downpours, strong wind and waves, sometimes cyclones, and many beach resorts close; Jan is still often rainy.
lk-east-north.tips: The east and west coasts have opposite seasons; in May–Sep you can link the east coast with the hills and the Cultural Triangle in a loop. The north is a Tamil cultural area; some Hindu temples require men to remove their shirts to enter. Rooms in Jaffna are tight at festival times, and Arugam Bay also needs early booking in the surf high season.

mv-maldives.places: Malé, Maafushi, North Malé Atoll, South Malé Atoll, Ari Atoll, Hanifaru Bay in Baa Atoll, Raa Atoll, Vaavu Atoll
mv-maldives.summary: Best: Dec–Apr, the dry northeast monsoon season: sunny, little rain, clear water
mv-maldives.climate: Equatorial tropical ocean climate, about 27–31°C all year, water about 28–29°C. The Dec–Apr northeast monsoon is dry and sunny with high visibility; the May–Oct southwest monsoon brings more showers, wind and waves, but the rain is mostly short.

mv-maldives.tips: Resort islands are reached by speedboat or seaplane; seaplanes fly only in daylight, so if you arrive late you stay overnight in Malé. Local islands ban alcohol and need modest dress; bikinis only on designated beaches. Ramadan moves about 11 days earlier each year by the Islamic calendar (see the season highlights for this year's dates); food and drink are limited in the daytime on local islands. Don't step on coral.

pk-north.places: Hunza, Karimabad, Attabad Lake, Khunjerab Pass border crossing, Skardu, Deosai Plateau, Fairy Meadows, Karakoram Highway
pk-north.summary: Best: Apr for apricot blossom; Jun and Sep–Oct for high mountain lakes and autumn colours
pk-north.climate: Karakoram high mountain climate. The Hunza Valley is about 2,400 m up, with summer days about 25–30°C and cool mornings and evenings; winter can drop to -10°C, with snow closing high roads; summer sometimes has rainstorms and glacier meltwater causing mudslides.

pk-north.tips: Before going, check the latest safety situation and official travel warnings. Foreigners must register or get permits for some areas, and high mountain treks such as K2 must go through a licensed agency. Roads are often cut by landslides, allow spare days. Local customs are conservative: cover shoulders and knees, and women should bring a headscarf. Ramadan moves every year by the Islamic calendar; food and drink are limited in the daytime.

bd-bangladesh.places: Dhaka, Old Dhaka, Sundarbans, Khulna, Mosque City of Bagerhat, Cox's Bazar, St. Martin's Island, Sreemangal tea gardens
bd-bangladesh.summary: Best: Dec–Feb, the cool dry season, good for the Sundarbans and beaches
bd-bangladesh.climate: Tropical monsoon climate. Nov–Feb is cool and dry, about 25°C by day; Mar–May is hot and humid with many thunderstorms; Jun–Oct brings heavy monsoon rain and floods easily; Apr–May and Oct–Nov are peak cyclone seasons in the Bay of Bengal.

bd-bangladesh.tips: Check the latest safety situation before you go and avoid rallies and protests. Dhaka traffic is extremely jammed, so allow plenty of time. Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha follow the Islamic calendar and come about 11 days earlier each year; tickets are scarce and shops close. Dress modestly; women cover shoulders and knees. Drink only bottled water and take care with food hygiene.

kz-kazakhstan.summary: Best: May–Jun and Sep in the Almaty mountains; skiing in winter
kz-kazakhstan.climate: Typical continental climate, cold winters and hot summers. Almaty is about 30°C in summer and about -5°C in winter; Astana often drops below -20°C in winter, with much wind and snow; the mountains are cool Jun–Sep, and spring and autumn are short and pleasant.

kz-kazakhstan.avoid: Dec–Feb Astana is bitterly cold, often below -20°C; Jul–Aug the plains and Charyn Canyon are hot; Nov is gloomy and cold with rain and snow, and mountain roads start to close.
kz-kazakhstan.tips: Chinese passports can currently stay short-term visa-free (check the latest rules). Roads to Kolsai and Kaindy lakes are rough, so hire a car with driver or join a tour. Mountain days and nights differ a lot in temperature, bring a jacket even in summer. Almaty and Astana are far apart, better to fly. Ramadan has little effect; most restaurants open as usual.

kg-kyrgyzstan.climate: Alpine continental climate. Bishkek is about 30°C in summer and about -5°C in winter; Issyk-Kul is about 25°C in summer, the water a little cool; Song-Kul lies about 3,000 m up, thaws only in Jun, gets snow from late Sep, and winter is severe.

Song-Kul is about 3,000 m up, watch for altitude sickness. Agree on taxi fares first, and download offline maps in advance. Cash rules in the mountains, carry enough local currency.

Ramadan follows the Islamic calendar and comes about 11 days earlier each year; it has little effect, but some restaurants close by day.

tj-tajikistan.climate: Mountain continental climate; over 90% of the country is mountains. Dushanbe often reaches 35–40°C in summer; the Pamir plateau sits 3,500–4,600 m up, about 15–20°C by day in summer and near 0°C at night, and can drop to -30°C in winter.

tj-tajikistan.tips: Check the latest safety situation before you go, especially along the Afghan border. Entering Gorno-Badakhshan (the Pamirs) needs a GBAO permit, which you can apply for with the e-visa. Acclimatise step by step to prevent altitude sickness. Roads are poor and supplies few; hire a 4WD and carry enough cash.

tm-turkmenistan.climate: Extremely dry continental desert climate; the Karakum Desert covers about 80% of the country. Summer often tops 40°C, winter is about 0°C with occasional cold snaps; spring and autumn are mild, about 20–28°C by day.

The Door to Hell is reached by 4WD.

Winery stays are in demand in Sep–Oct. Check the latest safety situation before you go, and don't visit disputed areas such as Abkhazia and South Ossetia.

Damask rose picking and rosewater making on Jebel Akhdar
Green turtles nesting at Ras al Jinz, seen all year, most in summer
Camping in Wahiba Sands and wadi hikes
Muscat Festival, usually Jan–Feb, the date changes every year
National Day celebrations, usually mid to late Nov
Ramadan (Islamic calendar, about 11 days earlier each year): most restaurants close by day and sights open shorter hours; iftar meals and night markets are lively after sunset
om-oman.avoid: May–Sep the north is very hot, often over 40°C, making desert trips and wadi hikes dangerous; in Salalah's monsoon season thick fog cuts visibility on some mountain roads.
om-oman.tips: Ramadan follows the Islamic calendar and comes about 11 days earlier each year (see the season highlights for this year's dates); don't eat or drink in public by day. The Grand Mosque is usually open to non-Muslims only in the morning and closed on Fridays; wear long clothes, and women wear a headscarf. You need a 4WD for the desert. Rain can cause flash floods in wadis, watch the weather.

sa-saudi-arabia.places: Riyadh, Diriyah, Edge of the World, AlUla, Hegra, Jeddah Old Town, Red Sea coast, Abha
sa-saudi-arabia.summary: Best: Nov–Feb, cool, best for outdoors in AlUla and Riyadh
sa-saudi-arabia.climate: Tropical desert climate. Riyadh and AlUla often top 43°C in summer; winter is about 20°C by day and can drop below 5°C at night; coastal Jeddah is hot and humid all year; the Abha mountains in the southwest are about 2,200 m up and cool in summer.

sa-saudi-arabia.avoid: Jun–Sep inland is very hot, often over 43°C; in the last ten days of Ramadan and during Hajj (Islamic calendar, the date changes every year), crowds and room prices soar in Mecca, Medina and Jeddah.
sa-saudi-arabia.tips: Check the latest safety situation before you go and stay away from the Yemen border area. Non-Muslims may not enter Mecca, and the central holy area of Medina is also restricted. E-visas are available (check the latest rules). Dress modestly; women don't need a headscarf but should cover shoulders and knees. Don't eat or drink in public by day during Ramadan. Sights are far apart, so drive or hire a car with driver, and carry plenty of water.

jo-jordan.places: Petra, Wadi Rum, Dead Sea, Aqaba, Amman Citadel, Jerash, Dana Nature Reserve, Wadi Mujib
jo-jordan.summary: Best: Apr–May and Oct–Nov, Petra and Wadi Rum are most comfortable
jo-jordan.climate: The western highlands have a Mediterranean climate: Amman is about 10°C in winter with occasional snow, and about 32°C in summer; the Dead Sea and Aqaba can top 40°C in summer; the Wadi Rum desert has big day-night swings. Spring and autumn are clear and mild.

jo-jordan.tips: Check the latest safety situation before you go and keep an eye on the wider region. The Jordan Pass covers the visa fee and Petra entry; stay at least 3 nights and the visa fee is waived. Give Petra at least 1–2 days and go in at opening time. At the Dead Sea keep the water out of your eyes, and don't go in after shaving. Ramadan follows the Islamic calendar and comes about 11 days earlier each year.

il-israel.places: Jerusalem Old City, Western Wall, Church of the Holy Sepulchre, Tel Aviv, Dead Sea, Masada, Sea of Galilee, Nazareth, Eilat
il-israel.summary: Best: Apr–May and Oct, mild and pleasant
il-israel.climate: Mediterranean climate. Winter is mild and rainy, Jerusalem about 12°C with occasional snow; summer is dry and hot, Tel Aviv humid at about 30°C, the Dead Sea and Eilat often over 40°C; spring and autumn are clear and mild.
notes: Jerusalem about 12°C, rainy, occasional snow, Dead Sea warm

il-israel.tips: Check the latest safety situation before you go, follow official travel warnings, and avoid tense areas. On the Sabbath most shops and public transport stop, so plan ahead. Cover shoulders and knees at religious sites. Hotels raise prices over Jewish holidays. Security checks on entry and exit are strict, allow plenty of time.

ir-iran.places: Tehran, Naqsh-e Jahan (Imam) Square in Isfahan, Pink Mosque in Shiraz, Persepolis, Yazd, Kashan, Tabriz, Lut Desert
ir-iran.summary: Best: Apr–May and Oct, mild and sunny in spring and autumn
ir-iran.climate: Highland continental climate that varies a lot by region. Tehran and Isfahan are about 35–38°C in summer and about 0–5°C in winter; Yazd and the desert top 40°C in summer; spring and autumn are about 20–28°C by day, clear and dry, the best time to travel.

ir-iran.tips: Check the latest safety situation before you go and follow official travel warnings. International bank cards don't work, so bring enough US dollars or euros in cash to exchange. Women must wear a headscarf and a long top that covers the hips. Ramadan follows the Islamic calendar and comes about 11 days earlier each year; don't eat or drink in public by day. Check the latest visa rules.

bh-bahrain.summary: Best: Dec–Mar, mild and dry; the F1 Grand Prix in spring
bh-bahrain.climate: Tropical desert climate; surrounded by sea, so humidity is high. Nov–Mar is about 20–25°C by day, pleasant; May–Sep is very hot and humid, often over 38°C by day with very high humidity; very little rain all year.

bh-bahrain.tips: Bahrain is fairly open, but still dress decently; in mosques cover shoulders and knees, and women wear a headscarf. Ramadan follows the Islamic calendar and comes about 11 days earlier each year (see the season highlights for this year's dates); don't eat or drink in public by day. You can cross to and from Saudi Arabia on the King Fahd Causeway, which jams at weekends. Check the latest safety situation before you go.

lb-lebanon.summary: Best: Apr–May and Sep, good for both coast and mountains
lb-lebanon.climate: Mediterranean climate. The coast is mild and rainy in winter at about 15°C, and hot and humid in summer at about 30°C; the Mount Lebanon range has snow for skiing in winter and is cool in summer; the Bekaa Valley is dry and hot in summer and cold in winter.

lb-lebanon.tips: Check the latest safety situation before you go, follow official travel warnings, and avoid the southern border area and protests. Currency and banking conditions are unusual; most places mainly take cash (US dollars), check before you go. Cover shoulders and knees at religious sites. Israeli entry or exit stamps in your passport may get you refused entry.

Friday is the main prayer day; some places open only in the afternoon. Check the latest safety situation before you go.

gb-england.places: London, Windsor, Oxford, Cambridge, Bath, Cotswolds, Lake District, York
gb-england.summary: Best: May–Jul and Sep for long days and flowers; Dec has a strong Christmas feel
gb-england.climate: Temperate maritime climate, mild and often rainy all year but rarely with heavy storms. Winter is gloomy and cold with little sun, dark by 4 pm; summer is 20–25°C by day, with occasional heatwaves over 30°C; the weather changes fast, four seasons in one day.
notes: About 7°C by day, gloomy, cold and damp, dark by 4 pm, winter sales

gb-england.tips: The UK is not in the Schengen Area, so you need a separate UK visa (visa-free nationalities need an ETA, Electronic Travel Authorisation). London rooms are expensive, book early; the weather changes fast, so carry an umbrella and a light jacket. National museums such as the British Museum are free; tap a contactless bank card on the Tube and buses, with a daily cap.

gb-scotland.tips: Rooms on Skye are very tight in summer, book months ahead; Highland driving is often on single-track roads, so use the passing places. Always carry a waterproof jacket and layers. For Edinburgh in Aug, book rooms about six months ahead. Scotland is part of the UK, so use a UK visa.

Countryside sights need a car; drive on the left, roads are narrow and winding. Always carry a waterproof jacket; Dublin rooms are expensive, book early.
