Provençal santon fairs and the traditional thirteen desserts
fr-provence.via: High-speed train from Charles de Gaulle Airport to Avignon about 3 hours, to Marseille about 3.5 hours
fr-provence.avoid: Late Jul to Aug is hottest and most crowded, seaside rooms double in price and roads jam; hotels in Cannes and Monaco are very expensive during the film festival and F1; Nov is rainy and some places close.
fr-provence.tips: Lavender bloom depends on the weather and can be 1–2 weeks earlier or later each year; harvesting starts from mid to late Jul. Drive to the inland villages. In summer use sun protection, drink plenty, and avoid going out at midday. Monaco is not in the EU but you can enter with a Schengen visa. Village shops are mostly closed on Sundays.

fr-alps-east.places: Chamonix, Mont Blanc, Annecy, Strasbourg, Colmar, Alsace Wine Route, Lyon, Beaune, Dijon
fr-alps-east.summary: Best: Jun–Sep for mountain hiking, Dec for Alsace Christmas markets, Jan–Mar for skiing
fr-alps-east.climate: A mix of continental and mountain climates: Alsace and Lyon are 26–28°C by day in summer and near 0°C in winter; Chamonix is about 22°C by day in summer with cool mornings and evenings, snowy in winter, and the high mountains are cold all year.
notes: Chamonix about 0°C by day, peak ski season; Alsace gloomy and cold at about 4°C
About 2–7°C by day, great skiing, French school winter holidays bring crowds and high prices
About 11°C by day, high-mountain snow still good, chilly spring in the cities, few visitors
About 15°C by day, ski season ends mid to late Apr, in-between season in the mountains, many cable cars stop
About 19°C by day, lovely spring at Lake Annecy and in Burgundy, snow still on high trails
About 23°C by day, high trails open one by one, Alsace vineyards lush and green
About 26°C by day, peak hiking season in Chamonix, long queues for the Aiguille du Midi cable car
About 26°C by day, holiday peak, Lake Annecy crowded, afternoon thunderstorms in the mountains
About 22°C by day, settled hiking weather, grape harvest begins
About 16°C by day, golden vineyards, high cable cars close one by one for maintenance
About 9°C by day, gloomy and cold; Christmas markets open in late Nov; Beaune wine auction
About 5°C by day, Strasbourg and Colmar Christmas markets, Lyon Festival of Lights
highlights: Strasbourg and Colmar Christmas markets (late Nov to late Dec)
Lyon Festival of Lights (about 4 days around 8 Dec)
Ski season in Chamonix and the French Alps (mid Dec to mid Apr)
Mont Blanc hiking, the Aiguille du Midi cable car and the Tour du Mont Blanc
Annecy International Animation Film Festival (mid Jun)
Grape harvest in Alsace and Burgundy
Hospices de Beaune charity wine auction (third weekend of Nov)
fr-alps-east.via: High-speed train from Paris to Strasbourg or Lyon about 2 hours, to Annecy about 4 hours
fr-alps-east.avoid: Apr–May and Oct–Nov are in-between seasons in the mountains, with many cable cars and huts closed; Christmas market weekends in Dec are packed and rooms pricey; in Aug traffic jams in Annecy and Chamonix.
fr-alps-east.tips: During the Christmas markets, book Strasbourg and Colmar hotels months ahead, or stay in nearby towns and take the train. Mountain weather changes fast; bring a warm jacket up the Aiguille du Midi, and check the official site for cable car opening. Book huts early for the Tour du Mont Blanc. France is in the Schengen Area.

be-belgium.places: Brussels, Bruges, Ghent, Antwerp, Leuven, Dinant, Hallerbos
be-belgium.summary: Best: May–Jun and Sep; Christmas markets in Dec, the Flower Carpet in Aug of even-numbered years
be-belgium.climate: Temperate maritime climate, rainy and cloudy all year. Summer is about 22–23°C by day, winter about 6°C by day, gloomy, cold and damp, rarely with heavy snow; spring and autumn are changeable, so carry an umbrella in every season.
notes: About 6°C by day, gloomy, cold and damp, short days, few visitors, good for museums and beer cafés
About 7°C by day, damp and cold; Carnival in Binche and other towns (the date changes every year)
About 10°C by day, many showers and unsettled weather, sights quiet
About 14°C by day, bluebells in Hallerbos, busy over the Easter holidays
About 18°C by day, spring flowers in bloom, long days, pleasant canal boats in Bruges
About 21°C by day, sunset near 10 pm, fairly settled weather, lots of outdoor events
About 23°C by day, many summer holiday visitors; National Day celebrations in Brussels on 21 Jul
About 22°C by day, Flower Carpet on the Grand-Place in even-numbered years, Bruges crowded with day-trippers
About 19°C by day, fewer people and still fine weather, Belgian Beer Weekend in early Sep
About 15°C by day, more rain, autumn leaf season, few visitors
About 10°C by day, grey, rainy, short days; Christmas markets open in late Nov
About 7°C by day, Brussels Winter Wonders and the Bruges Christmas market
highlights: Bluebells in Hallerbos (mid to late Apr)
Royal Greenhouses of Laeken, open for a short time (about 3 weeks, late Apr to early May)
Brussels Grand-Place Flower Carpet (mid Aug in even-numbered years)
Belgian Beer Weekend (early Sep, Grand-Place in Brussels)
Belgian National Day (21 Jul)
Brussels Winter Wonders Christmas market (late Nov to early Jan)
Binche Carnival (before Lent, the date changes every year)
be-belgium.via: Train to Brussels from Paris about 1.5 hours, from Amsterdam about 2 hours
be-belgium.avoid: Nov–Mar is grey and rainy with short days, so outdoor time is so-so; on summer weekends and in the Christmas season Bruges is packed with day-trippers; popular sights are crowded over the Easter holidays.
be-belgium.tips: Belgium is in the Schengen Area, and trains between cities are fast; Ghent, Bruges and Antwerp are all easy day trips from Brussels. Stay a night in Bruges to dodge the day-tripper crowds in the morning and evening. Carry rain gear all year. Many museums close on Mondays.

nl-netherlands.places: Amsterdam, Keukenhof, Lisse flower fields, Giethoorn, Zaanse Schans, Kinderdijk, Rotterdam, Delft, The Hague
nl-netherlands.summary: Best: mid to late Apr for tulips, May–Jun and Sep; King's Day on 27 Apr
nl-netherlands.climate: Temperate maritime climate; low, flat and windy, rainy all year. Summer is about 22°C by day, winter about 6°C by day, and canals freeze in very cold years; spring mornings and evenings are cool, so bring a windproof jacket.
notes: About 6°C by day, gloomy, cold and windy, Amsterdam Light Festival nearing its end
About 7°C by day, damp and cold, fewest visitors, Carnival in southern towns
About 10°C by day, Keukenhof opens, early flowers mainly crocuses and daffodils
About 14°C by day, tulips at their peak; King's Day on 27 Apr, a nationwide orange party
About 18°C by day, Keukenhof closes early to mid May, pleasant weather, long days
About 20°C by day, long days, Giethoorn and Zaanse Schans at their best
About 22°C by day, summer holiday peak, Amsterdam rooms at their most expensive
About 22°C by day, Pride Canal Parade in early Aug, many visitors
About 19°C by day, fewer people and still fine weather, good for Rotterdam's architecture and harbour
About 14°C by day, more autumn rain, summer time ends in late Oct and days get shorter
About 10°C by day, grey, rainy and windy; Sinterklaas arrives by boat in mid Nov
About 7°C by day, Amsterdam Light Festival; Sinterklaas on 5 Dec
highlights: Keukenhof gardens (late Mar to early May, best mid to late Apr)
Tulip fields around Lisse (mid to late Apr, earlier or later with the temperature)
King's Day (27 Apr, a day earlier if it falls on a Sunday)
Bulb Region flower parade (late Apr, Noordwijk to Haarlem)
National Mill Day (second weekend of May, many windmills open to visit)
Amsterdam Pride Canal Parade (early Aug)
Amsterdam Light Festival (late Nov to mid Jan)
nl-netherlands.avoid: Rooms soar in the Apr tulip season and on King's Day, so book early; Jul–Aug Amsterdam is overrun; Nov–Feb is gloomy, cold, rainy and windy, with short days.
nl-netherlands.tips: Buy Keukenhof tickets on the official site in advance; bloom time shifts 1–2 weeks each year with the temperature. Book the Van Gogh Museum and Anne Frank House online in advance; Anne Frank House tickets often sell out in seconds. Amsterdam rooms are expensive, so you can stay in Haarlem or Leiden and take the train. Don't walk in bike lanes. In the Schengen Area.

lu-luxembourg.places: Luxembourg City Old Town, Grand Ducal Palace, Bock Casemates, Adolphe Bridge, Vianden Castle, Müllerthal, Moselle Valley, Clervaux
lu-luxembourg.summary: Best: May–Jul and Sep, good to combine with Belgium, Germany and France; Christmas markets in Dec
lu-luxembourg.climate: Mild climate, partly maritime and partly continental. Summer is about 22–24°C by day, winter about 3–4°C by day with occasional snow; rain is spread fairly evenly through the year, and the northern Ardennes are cooler.
notes: About 3°C by day, gloomy and cold, occasional snow, very few visitors, country castles on shorter hours
About 5°C by day, cold and damp, Carnival parades in many places
About 9°C by day, chilly spring, rainy, castles gradually reopen
About 13°C by day, spring flowers; Éimaischen market in the Old Town on Easter Monday
About 17°C by day, Müllerthal trails lush and green, great for hiking
About 21°C by day; National Day on 23 Jun with fireworks the night before; comfortable weather
About 23°C by day, long days, lots going on at Vianden Castle and outdoors
About 23°C by day, European holiday season; Schueberfouer fair opens in late Aug
About 19°C by day, grape harvest and wine festivals in the Moselle Valley
About 13°C by day, lovely autumn colours in the Ardennes forest, more rain
About 7°C by day, gloomy and cold; Christmas markets open in late Nov
About 4°C by day, Luxembourg City Christmas markets, short cold days
highlights: National Day (23 Jun, fireworks over the Old Town on the evening of 22 Jun)
Schueberfouer fair (late Aug to early Sep)
Grape harvest and wine festivals in the Moselle Valley
Luxembourg City winter Christmas markets (late Nov to late Dec)
Hiking the sandstone gorges of Müllerthal, "Little Switzerland"
Éimaischen clay whistle market (Easter Monday, the date changes every year)
lu-luxembourg.via: High-speed train from Paris to Luxembourg about 2 hours; from Frankfurt by road about 2.5 hours
lu-luxembourg.avoid: Nov–Mar is gloomy and cold with short days, and country castles and sights open shorter hours; most shops close on Sundays and public holidays.
lu-luxembourg.tips: Public transport across Luxembourg is free (except first class on trains), very handy. The country is small, 1–2 days is enough, and it pairs well with Belgium, Trier in Germany and Metz in France. Rooms are rather pricey, so you can stay in nearby cities. In the Schengen Area. Vianden Castle has shorter winter hours, check the official site before you go.

es-madrid-central.places: Madrid, Toledo, Segovia, Ávila, Salamanca, Cuenca, El Escorial
es-madrid-central.summary: Best: Apr–May and Sep–Oct; Jul–Aug is scorching and locals leave on holiday
es-madrid-central.climate: Continental plateau climate, dry with little rain and big swings between day and night. Summer days often reach 33–38°C; winter days are about 10°C and nights can drop to around 0°C; many sunny days and plenty of sunshine.
notes: About 10°C by day, near 0°C at night, sunny, cold and dry; Three Kings parade on the evening of the 5th
About 12°C by day, sunny and cold, few tourists, comfortable for Madrid's museums
About 16°C by day, spring warmth and flowers; Holy Week may fall late in the month
About 19°C by day, pleasant; crowds for the Holy Week processions (the date changes every year)

About 29°C by day, getting hot late in the month; sunset near 10 pm, lively terraces

About 27°C by day, the heat eases, fewer tourists, good for strolling the old towns
About 20°C by day, clear, crisp autumn, one of the best months
About 14°C by day, sunny and cool, few tourists, a good time for museums

highlights: Holy Week processions (the week before Easter, the date changes every year; grandest in Toledo and Salamanca)
San Isidro festival in Madrid (around 15 May)
Corpus Christi procession in Toledo (about 60 days after Easter, the date changes every year)
Madrid Pride (late Jun to early Jul)
Salamanca fiestas (early to mid Sep)
Eating 12 grapes at Puerta del Sol on New Year's Eve; Three Kings parade on the evening of 5 Jan
es-madrid-central.avoid: In Jul–Aug days are often over 35°C, so stay out of the afternoon sun, and in Aug some local restaurants close. During Holy Week, old towns like Toledo are crowded and rooms are expensive.
es-madrid-central.tips: Spain keeps late hours: lunch about 2–4 pm, dinner after 9 pm. The Prado has free hours in the early evening (check the official website). In summer, sightsee in the morning and rest in the afternoon. Toledo and Segovia are easy day trips by high-speed train. Schengen area; watch for pickpockets at Puerta del Sol and on the metro.

es-barcelona-north.places: Barcelona, Montserrat, Girona, Costa Brava, Bilbao, San Sebastián, Pamplona, Santiago de Compostela
es-barcelona-north.summary: Best: May–Jun and Sep; the north is cool in summer, Barcelona is humid and crowded in Aug
es-barcelona-north.climate: Barcelona has a Mediterranean climate: hot and humid in summer, days about 28–30°C, about 14°C in winter. The northern Atlantic coast (Basque Country, Galicia) is mild and rainy, with summer days about 24°C.
notes: Barcelona about 14°C by day, sunny and cold; the north grey and rainy at about 11°C; few tourists

Sant Joan (night of Jun 23, bonfires and beach fireworks)
Running of the Bulls in Pamplona (6–14 Jul)
Feast of St James (Jul 25, fireworks in front of the cathedral in Santiago on the night of the 24th)
Semana Grande in San Sebastián (mid Aug, international fireworks contest)
La Mercè in Barcelona (around 24 Sep) and San Sebastián Film Festival (late Sep)
Best season for walking the Camino de Santiago
es-barcelona-north.avoid: In Jul–Aug Barcelona is muggy, and sights like the Sagrada Família and the beaches are packed. During the Running of the Bulls, room prices in Pamplona soar. Nov–Mar the north has grey, rainy days on end.
es-barcelona-north.tips: Book the Sagrada Família, Park Güell and Casa Batlló ahead on their official websites. Barcelona has many pickpockets, so watch your phone and wallet. In the Basque Country, try pintxos in the snack bars. Camino hostels fill up in summer. Schengen area; Barcelona also charges a tourist tax.

es-andalusia.places: Seville, Granada, Córdoba, Málaga, Ronda, Cádiz, Jerez, Nerja, Mijas
es-andalusia.summary: Best: Mar–May and Oct; Holy Week and the April Fair are the liveliest, Jul–Aug is scorching inland
es-andalusia.climate: Mediterranean climate, one of the hottest areas in southern Europe. Summer days in Seville and Córdoba often reach 36–40°C or more; winter is mild and sunny, days about 16–18°C. The Costa del Sol is cooler, and sunny even in winter.
notes: Seville about 16°C by day, sunny with little rain, a good winter escape; cool mornings and evenings
About 18°C by day, almond blossom; Cádiz Carnival (the date changes every year)

About 32°C by day, the heat eases; Jerez grape harvest festival

highlights: Holy Week processions (the week before Easter, the date changes every year; grandest in Seville)
Seville April Fair (about two weeks after Easter, the date changes every year)

Christmas light show on Calle Larios, Málaga (late Nov to early Jan)
es-andalusia.avoid: In Jul–Aug, days in Seville and Córdoba are often over 40°C, with a risk of heatstroke outdoors at midday. During Holy Week and the April Fair, rooms in Seville cost several times more and must be booked far ahead.
es-andalusia.tips: Alhambra tickets are limited: in high season book 1–2 months ahead on the official website and pick a time slot for the Nasrid Palaces. In summer sightsee early morning and evening; many small shops close in the afternoon. Indoor heating is often missing in winter, so bring warm clothes. Schengen area.

es-balearic.places: Mallorca, Palma, Serra de Tramuntana, Sóller, Caves of Drach, Menorca, Ciutadella, Ibiza, Formentera
es-balearic.summary: Best: May–Jun and Sep, warm sea and fewer people; Jul–Aug is the most crowded, and many seaside places close in winter
es-balearic.climate: Mediterranean climate: hot and dry in summer, days about 29–31°C, sea about 25–26°C in Aug–Sep; winter is mild and cloudy, days about 15°C, with the odd strong wind and rain. Spring and autumn are sunny, good for hiking and cycling.

es-balearic.avoid: Jul–Aug is packed, with the highest prices for rooms, car hire and ferries, and parking at popular coves is hard. Nov–Mar most seaside hotels and restaurants close, and there are fewer ferries and flights.
es-balearic.tips: The islands are linked by ferries and short flights, and budget flights within Europe are cheap; Formentera is reached by boat from Ibiza. Driving yourself is easiest on the islands; in high season book car and room well ahead. Each island charges a nightly sustainable tourism tax. Palma Cathedral and the old Sóller train are worth it. Schengen area.

es-canary.places: Tenerife, Teide National Park, Santa Cruz de Tenerife, Gran Canaria, Maspalomas Dunes, Lanzarote, Timanfaya National Park, Fuerteventura, La Palma
es-canary.summary: Mild all year, best Mar–May and Oct–Nov; Europe's top winter escape
es-canary.climate: Subtropical oceanic climate, softened by the trade winds and the cold Canary Current; days about 21–29°C all year, known as the 'eternal spring'. The south coast is dry and sunny, the north cloudy and damp; Mount Teide can have snow in winter, and Saharan dust sometimes blows in.
notes: South about 21°C by day and sunny, sea cool at about 19°C; peak winter-escape season for Europeans
About 21°C by day; Carnival in Santa Cruz and Las Palmas (the date changes every year)

About 24°C by day, few tourists and low prices; red tajinaste flowers on Teide

Towers of red tajinaste flowers in full bloom in Teide National Park (about May–Jun)
Corpus Christi volcanic sand pictures and flower carpets in La Orotava (late May to Jun, the date changes every year)
Windsurfing and kitesurfing on Fuerteventura and Lanzarote (trade winds strongest in summer)

Winter-escape season: south coast days about 21–24°C, mostly sunny
es-canary.avoid: Aug has the most mainland Spanish visitors and high prices, with the odd Saharan dust storm and heatwave. Late Dec to early Jan, Christmas and New Year rooms are the most expensive. In winter the north and the mountains are cloudy and rainy, and the summit of Teide may close for ice and snow.
es-canary.tips: The Canary Islands are part of Spain and the Schengen area but outside the EU VAT area, so some goods are cheaper. They are far from mainland Europe, about 2.5–3 hours' flight from Madrid. To climb to Teide's summit you need a free permit, applied for in advance; the cable car stops in strong wind. The south is sunny and the north cloudy, so choose where to stay by area. In winter the sea is cool, about 19°C.

pt-lisbon-porto.places: Lisbon, Sintra, Cascais, Cabo da Roca, Óbidos, Coimbra, Porto, Douro Valley
pt-lisbon-porto.summary: Best: Apr–Jun and Sep; saints' festivals in Jun, Douro Valley harvest in Sep–Oct
pt-lisbon-porto.climate: Mediterranean climate softened by the Atlantic. Lisbon summer days are about 28°C with the odd heatwave; winter is about 15°C and rainy. Porto is cooler and wetter, rainy in winter, with sea fog on many summer mornings.
notes: Lisbon about 15°C by day, rainy, few tourists, lowest hotel prices

About 15°C by day, rainy, Christmas lights; New Year's Eve at Praça do Comércio in Lisbon

São João in Porto (night of Jun 23, toy-hammer fun and fireworks)
Jacarandas in bloom in Lisbon (late May to mid Jun)
Coimbra student festival (early May)
Douro Valley grape harvest (mid Sep to early Oct)
St Martin's Day roast chestnuts and new wine (11 Nov)
pt-lisbon-porto.avoid: Jul–Aug Lisbon and Sintra are packed and rooms cost the most. Nov–Feb is rainy, Porto especially damp and cold. Weekend morning queues in Sintra are very long.
pt-lisbon-porto.tips: Lisbon and Porto have steep hills and slippery stone pavements, so wear comfortable shoes with good grip. Book an early slot at Pena Palace in Sintra on the official website. Tram 28 has many pickpockets. The Atlantic is cold in summer; surfers need a wetsuit. Schengen area; city transport cards are good value.

pt-algarve-islands.places: Lagos, Benagil Cave, Sagres, Albufeira, Funchal (Madeira), Madeira levada walks, Ponta Delgada (Azores), Sete Cidades
pt-algarve-islands.summary: Algarve: best May–Jun and Sep; Madeira is mild all year; the Azores are best Jun–Sep
pt-algarve-islands.climate: The Algarve has a Mediterranean climate: summer days about 29°C, sunny all year, winter about 16°C. Madeira's days are about 19–26°C all year. The Azores have a mild, rainy oceanic climate with changeable weather.
notes: Algarve about 16°C by day, sunny, cold sea; many beach bars closed

Madeira Flower Festival (after Easter, the date changes every year)
Almond blossom in the Algarve (late Jan to Feb)
Hydrangeas in the Azores (late Jun to Aug)
Whale-watching season in the Azores (about Apr–Oct, blue whales in spring)
Kayaking to Benagil Cave and the Seven Hanging Valleys coastal trail
Madeira Wine Festival (late Aug to early Sep)
pt-algarve-islands.avoid: Jul–Aug Algarve beaches are packed, rooms cost the most and sea cave boat trips are crowded. Nov–Feb the Azores are rainy and windy, and flights are often affected. In winter many Algarve restaurants close.
pt-algarve-islands.tips: Under recent rules you may not land on the beach inside Benagil Cave; you can only see it by boat or kayak, from outside or on the water inside, and trips stop in rough seas. Madeira's airport often has delays from crosswinds. Azores weather changes many times a day; check the clouds before going to see the crater lakes. Schengen area.

it-north.places: Milan, Venice, Verona, Lake Como, Lake Garda, the Dolomites, Cinque Terre, Turin, Bologna
it-north.summary: Best: May–Jun and Sep; hiking in the Dolomites Jul–Sep, skiing Dec–Mar
it-north.climate: The Po Valley is muggy in summer, days about 30°C, and grey, cold and foggy in winter, about 5–7°C. The lakes are milder; the Dolomites are cool in summer and snowy in winter; Cinque Terre has a Mediterranean climate.

highlights: Venice Carnival (about 2 weeks, ending in Feb or early Mar, the date changes every year)
Verona Arena Opera Festival (mid to late Jun to early Sep)
Hiking in the Dolomites (cable cars and mountain huts open late Jun to mid Sep)
Dolomites ski season (Dec to late Mar)

it-north.avoid: Aug on the plain is scorching and muggy; around the 15th many city shops close, and the lakes and Cinque Terre are packed. Nov brings frequent high water and thick fog to Venice. During Carnival, room prices in Venice soar.
it-north.tips: On some high-season days Venice charges day-trippers an entry fee; register online ahead (check official rules). Some stretches of the Cinque Terre coastal path need a trail card and often close after rain. Book The Last Supper in Milan months ahead. Schengen area; validate paper train tickets before boarding.

it-central.places: Rome, Vatican City, Florence, Pisa, Siena, San Gimignano, Val d'Orcia, Assisi, Orvieto
it-central.summary: Best: Apr–May and Sep–Oct; Jul–Aug is scorching, and Rome is mobbed at Easter
it-central.climate: Mediterranean climate: hot and dry in summer, with days in Rome and Florence often 32–35°C; winter is mild and rainy, days about 12°C. Florence sits in a basin, so its cold winters and hot summers are more marked.
notes: Rome about 12°C by day, few tourists, winter sales, short queues at the Vatican
About 13°C by day, quite a few rainy days, low-season prices, the odd cold snap
About 16°C by day, spring warmth; Easter may fall late in the month, many school groups

Poppies and green wheat fields in Val d'Orcia (May)
Calcio Storico final in Florence (Jun 24, Feast of St John)
Feast of Sts Peter and Paul in Rome (29 Jun)
Palio in Siena (Jul 2, 16 Aug)
Tuscan grape harvest (mid to late Sep into Oct)
San Miniato White Truffle Fair (weekends in Nov)
Christmas at the Vatican and the nativity scene in St Peter's Square
it-central.avoid: Jul–Aug Rome and Florence are scorching, with long queues at the Vatican and the Uffizi. At Easter and during big religious events, rooms in Rome are hard to find. In mid Aug small local shops close.
it-central.tips: Book the Vatican Museums, the Uffizi, the Accademia and the Borghese Gallery ahead on their official websites. Cover shoulders and knees in churches. You can fill your bottle at Rome's street drinking fountains. The Tuscan countryside is best by car, but watch for the ZTL limited-traffic zones in towns: entering by mistake means a fine. Schengen area.

it-south-islands.places: Naples, Pompeii, Amalfi Coast, Positano, Capri, Matera, Alberobello, Sicily, Taormina, Sardinia
it-south-islands.summary: Best: May–Jun and Sep; Jul–Aug the coast is hottest and most crowded, and many places close in winter
it-south-islands.climate: Classic Mediterranean climate: dry heat in summer, days about 30–33°C, and inland Sicily can top 38°C; winter is mild, days about 14–16°C, and boats to Amalfi and Capri are much reduced in winter.
notes: Naples about 13°C by day; many Amalfi Coast hotels closed, few tourists
About 14°C by day, almond blossom in Sicily; Almond Blossom Festival in Agrigento
About 16°C by day, spring warmth in Sicily; coastal sights open around Easter

highlights: Hiking the Path of the Gods on the Amalfi Coast
Almond Blossom Festival in Agrigento (Feb or early Mar)
Holy Week processions in Sicily (Trapani and other towns, the date changes every year)

Ferragosto (Aug 15, festivals and fireworks everywhere)
Feast of San Gennaro in Naples (19 Sep)
Nativity scenes on Via San Gregorio Armeno, Naples (about mid Nov to Jan)
it-south-islands.avoid: In Aug seaside rooms are the most expensive and crowded, and traffic on the Amalfi road is very bad. Nov–Mar most hotels and restaurants on Amalfi and Capri close and there are fewer ferries. Jul–Aug inland Sicily is scorching.
it-south-islands.tips: On the Amalfi Coast, take ferries instead of buses to skip the traffic, and book rooms ahead in high season. Pompeii has little shade, so bring water and sun protection, and book tickets on the official website. In Naples watch for pickpockets and bag snatchers on scooters. Sicily and Puglia are best by car. Schengen area.

mt-malta.places: Valletta, Mdina, the Three Cities, St Julian's, Blue Grotto, Marsaxlokk, Gozo, Blue Lagoon on Comino
mt-malta.summary: Best: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; winter is mild but windy, Jul–Aug is hot and crowded
mt-malta.climate: Mediterranean climate with plenty of sunshine all year. Summer days are about 31°C, hot, humid and dry; winter days are about 15–16°C with the odd strong wind and shower; the sea drops to about 15°C at its coldest.
notes: About 16°C by day, windy with some rain, few tourists; good for the cities and historic sites
About 16°C by day, cold sea; Carnival (Feb or Mar, the date varies)

mt-malta.avoid: Jul–Aug is hot and humid, the Blue Lagoon and beaches are packed and rooms are expensive. In winter, strong winds now and then stop the Gozo ferry or boat trips. In Jan–Feb indoor heating is often missing, so it feels cold and gloomy.
mt-malta.tips: Malta is in the Schengen area; English is widely spoken, cars drive on the left and plugs are the British three-pin type. The Blue Lagoon may need booking to limit numbers in high season (check local rules). Buses are slow and often full; ride-hailing apps help. The limestone ground has little shade, so use sun protection and drink water in summer.

gr-athens-mainland.places: Athens, Acropolis, Cape Sounion, Delphi, Meteora, Nafplio, Mycenae, Epidaurus, Olympia
gr-athens-mainland.summary: Best: Apr–May and Sep–Oct; Jul–Aug Athens is scorching, and the Acropolis closes at midday in heatwaves
gr-athens-mainland.climate: Mediterranean climate: hot and dry in summer, with Athens days often 33–38°C and heatwaves; winter is mild and rainy, days about 13–14°C. Meteora in the north and the mountains are cold in winter and can get snow.

gr-athens-mainland.avoid: In Jul–Aug Athens days are often over 35°C, and in heatwaves the Acropolis and other sites may close at midday. Over Orthodox Easter some sights and shops close. Mountain roads are poor in winter.
gr-athens-mainland.tips: Book a time slot for the Acropolis on the official website, and go in right at opening. From Nov to Mar some sites are free on the first Sunday of each month (check official info). Carry plenty of water and a hat in summer. Each Meteora monastery has its own closing day; cover shoulders and knees. Schengen area.

gr-islands.places: Santorini, Mykonos, Naxos, Paros, Crete, Rhodes, Zakynthos, Corfu
gr-islands.summary: Best: May–Jun and Sep; Jul–Aug is hottest and most crowded, and most small islands shut down Nov–Mar
gr-islands.climate: Mediterranean climate: hot, dry and sunny in summer, days about 28–32°C; the Cyclades often get the strong meltemi north wind in Jul–Aug. Winter is mild and rainy, about 15°C, with fewer ferries.
notes: About 15°C by day; most small-island hotels and restaurants closed, few ferries

gr-islands.avoid: Jul–Aug Santorini and Mykonos are packed and rooms cost a fortune; the meltemi often delays ferries. Nov–Mar most small-island hotels, restaurants and direct flights stop.
gr-islands.tips: Book ferries ahead for island hopping; boats often stop in strong wind, so leave spare time in your plan. Santorini is very crowded on cruise ship days; get to the Oia sunset viewpoints early for a spot. Crete is big, so a car is best. Book island rooms months ahead in high season. Schengen area.

cy-cyprus.places: Limassol, Paphos, Larnaca, Ayia Napa, Nicosia, Troodos Mountains, Aphrodite's Rock, Akamas Peninsula
cy-cyprus.summary: Best: Apr–May and Oct; summer is scorching, winter is mild and good for escaping the cold
cy-cyprus.climate: Eastern Mediterranean climate with plenty of sunshine all year. Summer is long, hot and dry: coastal days about 32°C, and inland Nicosia can top 40°C. Winter is mild, coastal days about 17°C; the Troodos Mountains get snow in winter.

cy-cyprus.tips: Cyprus is in the EU but not in the Schengen area, so it needs its own visa; with a valid multiple-entry Schengen visa you may enter under certain conditions (check official rules). Cars drive on the left. The island is divided; bring your passport to cross to the north. Use sun protection and drink water in summer.

de-north.places: Brandenburg Gate in Berlin, Museum Island in Berlin, Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, Lübeck Old Town, Cologne Cathedral, Frauenkirche in Dresden, Leipzig, Middle Rhine Valley
de-north.summary: Best: May–Sep for the cities and the Rhine Valley, Dec for Christmas markets
de-north.climate: Between temperate oceanic and continental: summer is mild with the odd heatwave (20–30°C), winter is grey, cold and damp (-3 to 5°C). The northern coast is windy; winter days are short and summer days long.
notes: -3 to 3°C, grey, cold and cloudy, about 8 hours of daylight; good for museums and concerts

de-north.tips: Use Deutsche Bahn ICE trains between cities; tickets bought early are cheaper, but trains are often late, so leave plenty of time to change. Most shops close on Sundays. Bring a warm, waterproof coat in winter. During big trade fairs, hotel prices in Cologne, Hamburg and other cities shoot up, so book early. Schengen visa applies.

de-south.tips: Book timed tickets for Neuschwanstein ahead on the official website, weeks ahead in high season. The Bayern-Ticket is good for several towns in one day. Mountain weather changes fast, so bring a rain jacket. Driving in winter needs snow tyres. Shops close on Sundays and public holidays. Schengen visa applies.

at-austria.tips: Visit Hallstatt early morning or in the evening, ideally staying a night to miss the tour groups. The Vienna State Opera sells cheap standing tickets. Motorways need a digital vignette. The Grossglockner High Alpine Road is usually open only from early May to early Nov. Driving in winter needs snow tyres. Schengen visa applies.

ch-switzerland.places: Interlaken, Jungfrau, Grindelwald, Lauterbrunnen, Zermatt and the Matterhorn, Lucerne, Zurich, Geneva, Glacier Express

School holidays in Feb and Christmas–New Year are the most expensive at ski resorts. On rainy, foggy days you may see nothing at all from the Jungfrau.
ch-switzerland.tips: Switzerland is expensive; compare the Swiss Travel Pass and the Half Fare Card for your plan. Check the live summit webcams for visibility before going up. Bring a warm jacket at high altitude even in summer. The Glacier Express needs a seat reservation. The currency is the Swiss franc. Schengen visa applies.

cz-czechia.avoid: Jul–Aug Prague's Old Town is packed with tourists and rooms are expensive. Nov and Jan–Feb are grey and cold with short days. On New Year's Eve Old Town Square is crowded and noisy.
cz-czechia.tips: The currency is the Czech koruna; avoid street exchange booths with high fees and use ATMs or cards. Charles Bridge is quietest early in the morning. Český Krumlov is worth a night's stay. Validate public transport tickets, as fines are heavy. Schengen visa applies.

sk-slovakia.places: Bratislava, High Tatras, Štrbské Pleso, Spiš Castle, Slovak Paradise National Park, Banská Štiavnica

sk-slovakia.climate: Continental climate: Bratislava is warm in summer (22–28°C) and -3 to 3°C in winter. The High Tatras are cool with lots of rain and snow: deep snow in winter and frequent afternoon thunderstorms in summer.

sk-slovakia.tips: High trails in Tatras National Park close each year from about early Nov to mid Jun (check park notices). Mountain weather changes fast, so bring rain gear and warm layers. Bratislava is an easy day trip from Vienna. The currency is the euro; Schengen visa applies.

hu-hungary.summary: Best: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; Lake Balaton in summer, thermal baths in winter

hu-hungary.avoid: Jul–Aug Budapest often has 35°C heatwaves, and most old buildings and flats have no air conditioning. Nov and Jan–Feb are grey, cold and foggy. The national day fireworks in Aug draw huge crowds.
hu-hungary.tips: The currency is the forint; cards are accepted in most places. Bring a swimsuit and flip-flops to the thermal baths; weekends are crowded. Book Lake Balaton holiday homes early for summer. The Danube night view is loveliest at blue hour in the evening. Schengen visa applies.

pl-poland.places: Kraków Old Town and Wawel Castle, Wieliczka Salt Mine, Auschwitz-Birkenau Memorial, Warsaw, Gdańsk, Malbork Castle, Zakopane, Wrocław
pl-poland.summary: Best: May–Sep for cities and the coast, Dec for Christmas markets
pl-poland.climate: Temperate continental climate: summer is warm (20–26°C) with the odd heatwave; winter is cold (-5 to 2°C), with grey days and snow in turn. The Baltic coast in the north is cool and windy; the Tatra Mountains in the south get lots of snow.
notes: -5 to 1°C, cold and gloomy; ski season in Zakopane, few tourists in the cities

pl-poland.tips: The currency is the złoty; cards are widely used. Book an entry or guided tour time slot for the Auschwitz-Birkenau Memorial ahead on the official website. Buy tickets ahead for the salt mine and Wawel Castle in high season. Most shops close on Sundays. Schengen visa applies.

si-slovenia.places: Lake Bled, Lake Bohinj, Ljubljana, Postojna Cave, Škocjan Caves, Triglav National Park, Soča Valley, Piran
si-slovenia.summary: Best: May–Jun and Sep for lakes and mountains, Jul for Alpine hiking

notes: -4 to 3°C, foggy in Ljubljana; skiing at Kranjska Gora

si-slovenia.tips: Go to Lake Bled early in the morning; a traditional pletna boat takes you to the island. The caves are about 10°C all year, so bring a jacket. Motorways need a digital vignette. Buses from Ljubljana to the sights are easy. The currency is the euro; Schengen visa applies.

hr-croatia.places: Dubrovnik, Split, Hvar, Plitvice Lakes National Park, Krka National Park, Zadar, Rovinj, Zagreb
hr-croatia.summary: Best: May–Jun and Sep for the coast; Jul–Aug is island high season; Dec for Zagreb's Advent market
hr-croatia.climate: Mediterranean climate on the coast: hot and dry in summer (26–32°C), mild and rainy in winter (6 to 13°C). Inland, Zagreb and Plitvice have a continental climate, cold with snow in winter.
notes: Coast 6 to 12°C, inland -2 to 4°C; few ferries, many hotels closed

hr-croatia.tips: Croatia has joined the Schengen area and uses the euro. Walk Dubrovnik's city walls early morning or in the evening to avoid the heat and the cruise crowds. Book island ferries ahead in high season. Plitvice Lakes National Park needs an online booking for an entry time slot. Beaches are mostly pebbly, so bring water shoes.

me-montenegro.places: Kotor Old Town, Bay of Kotor, Perast, Budva, Sveti Stefan, Mount Lovćen, Durmitor National Park, Tara River Canyon
me-montenegro.summary: Best: May–Jun and Sep for the bay and old towns, summer for hiking in Durmitor
me-montenegro.climate: Mediterranean climate on the coast: hot in summer (26–32°C), mild and rainy in winter (6 to 13°C), and the Bay of Kotor gets a great deal of rain in winter. The Durmitor mountains in the north are cool in summer, with deep snow in winter.

me-montenegro.tips: Montenegro uses the euro but is not in the Schengen area; visa rules depend on nationality, and holders of a valid Schengen visa may be able to enter for a short stay, so check the latest rules before you go. Climb Kotor's walls early in the morning. Driving is easy, but mountain roads are narrow and winding; take care on the Kotor Serpentine.

ba-bosnia.tips: The currency is the convertible mark; some shops take euros. Ramadan dates change every year, and some restaurants change their daytime hours then. Stay a night in Mostar to see the Old Bridge at night and miss the midday tour groups. Not in the Schengen area; visa rules depend on nationality, so check before you go.

al-albania.climate: Mediterranean climate on the coast: hot and dry in summer (28–34°C), mild and rainy in winter (7 to 14°C). The Albanian Alps in the north get lots of snow in winter and are cool in summer, good for hiking.

al-albania.tips: The currency is the lek; small places mostly take cash. Mountain roads are narrow and winding, so drive with care. For the northern hike, the Lake Koman ferry links up the route. Not in the Schengen area; visa rules depend on nationality, and holders of a valid multiple-entry Schengen visa may not need a visa, so check before you go.

Orthodox holidays follow the old calendar, so dates differ from Western Europe. The floating clubs open mainly in summer. At night, take taxis through a proper ride-hailing app.

A hire car is the most flexible way to see Transylvania; country roads are so-so. There are brown bears in the mountains: don't feed them, and don't get out of the car to go near. The high mountain roads open depending on the snow.

no-fjords.tips: Norway is very expensive; buy simple meals at supermarkets. Fjord weather changes fast, so bring a waterproof jacket and hiking boots. Book popular routes like Norway in a Nutshell ahead in high season. Trolltunga takes about 10–12 hours return and Kjeragbolten about 6–10 hours, both physically hard. Schengen visa applies; the currency is the Norwegian krone.

highlights: Northern lights season
Midnight sun

Dog sledding and Sami reindeer experiences
Finnmark dog sled race (Alta)
no-arctic.avoid: Apr and Aug have neither the northern lights nor much snow and ice. In winter the North Cape road often needs a convoy escort or is closed. During polar night daylight is very short, so drive with care.
no-arctic.tips: In winter you need full cold-weather gear (down jacket, thermal underwear, non-slip boots). The northern lights depend on solar activity and cloud, so stay 3 nights or more. Winter driving needs snow experience; you can join a tour or take the coastal ship. Book whale watching and dog sledding ahead. Schengen visa applies.

se-sweden.places: Stockholm Old Town, Vasa Museum, Stockholm Archipelago, Gothenburg, Visby, Kiruna, Icehotel in Jukkasjärvi, Abisko National Park
se-sweden.summary: Best: Jun–Aug for the Stockholm Archipelago, Feb–Mar for northern lights and the Icehotel in the north
se-sweden.climate: Temperate in the south: Stockholm is 15–23°C in summer and -4 to 1°C in winter. Lapland in the north is subarctic, often below -15°C in winter, with polar night and the midnight sun; Abisko has few clouds, good for the northern lights.

se-sweden.avoid: Oct–Nov is grey, cold and rainy with no snow, not good in the south or the north; in Jul locals take long holidays and some small restaurants close; many shops close on Midsummer Day itself.
se-sweden.tips: Sweden is almost cashless, most places take cards only. Winter in the north needs polar-grade warm gear. Book the Icehotel months ahead. A night train runs from Stockholm to Kiruna. Archipelago ferries run often in summer. Schengen visa applies; the currency is the Swedish krona.

fi-south.places: Helsinki, Suomenlinna, Nuuksio National Park, Porvoo, Turku, Turku Archipelago, Tampere, Olavinlinna Castle in Savonlinna, Finnish Lakeland
fi-south.summary: Best: Jun–Aug for summer in the Lakeland and archipelago, Dec for Christmas spirit
fi-south.climate: Temperate continental climate. Summer is cool and pleasant (17–23°C) with very long days; winter is cold and dark (-7 to -1°C), and the sea and lakes freeze; spring and autumn are short.
notes: -7 to -2°C, about 6 hours of daylight, the sea freezes; try sauna and ice swimming

fi-south.avoid: Nov is dark with no snow, the dullest month; over Midsummer the cities empty out and many shops close; in Jul locals are on holiday and some businesses close.
fi-south.tips: Public saunas are at the heart of Finnish culture, well worth trying. The Helsinki–Tallinn ferry takes about 2 hours, good for a day trip. Book Lakeland cottages ahead in summer. Roads are icy in winter, take care not to slip. Schengen visa applies; the currency is the euro.

fi-lapland.places: Santa Claus Village in Rovaniemi, Saariselkä, Levi, Inari, Kittilä, Ivalo, Kemi icebreaker, Urho Kekkonen National Park
fi-lapland.summary: Best: Dec–Mar for northern lights and snow, Sep for autumn colours and northern lights
fi-lapland.climate: Subarctic climate. Winter is long and bitterly cold (-20 to -8°C, below -30°C in cold snaps), with polar night in the north; summer is short and cool (12–20°C), with the midnight sun but lots of mosquitoes.
notes: -17 to -8°C, polar night ending in the north; northern lights, dog sledding and snowmobiles
-16 to -7°C, days getting longer, best snow, peak northern lights season

fi-lapland.avoid: The May snowmelt and the Oct in-between period are dull with little to do; Jul has swarms of mosquitoes; rooms over Christmas and New Year are very expensive, book over six months ahead.
fi-lapland.tips: Winter needs polar-grade warm gear; most tours provide warm overalls. Book glass igloos as early as you can. The northern lights depend on clear skies and solar activity, so stay 3–4 nights. Daylight is very short in Nov–Jan, so plan outdoor activities around midday. Schengen visa applies.

dk-denmark.places: Copenhagen, Nyhavn, Tivoli Gardens, Frederiksborg Castle, Kronborg Castle, Odense, Legoland Billund, Skagen, Faroe Islands
dk-denmark.summary: Best: May–Aug for cities and coast, Dec for Christmas at Tivoli
dk-denmark.climate: Temperate maritime climate, windy and cloudy all year. Summer is mild (16–22°C), winter grey, cold and damp (0 to 4°C); rain is frequent but light. The Faroe Islands are cooler, foggier and wetter.
notes: 0 to 3°C, grey, cold and windy, about 7 hours of daylight; enjoy cosy Danish hygge indoors
-1 to 3°C, grey and cold low season; good for museums and design shops
1 to 6°C, warm one day, cold the next; the date of Easter changes every year

11 to 20°C, about 17 hours of daylight, St Hans Eve bonfires in late Jun

dk-denmark.avoid: Nov and Jan–Mar are grey, cold and windy with short days; Legoland closes in winter; the Faroe Islands get many winter storms, which often disrupt flights and ferries.
dk-denmark.tips: Copenhagen is bike-friendly, you can rent a bike. Cards are used everywhere and prices are high. Tivoli's opening times change by season, check before you go. The Faroe Islands are not in the Schengen Area, so check visa rules separately. Mainland Denmark is in Schengen; the currency is the Danish krone.

is-iceland.places: Reykjavik, Golden Circle, Seljalandsfoss, Skógafoss, Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon, Diamond Beach, Blue Lagoon, Lake Mývatn, Akureyri, Westfjords
is-iceland.summary: Best: Jun–Sep for a road trip round the island; Sep–Mar for the northern lights, Nov–Mar for ice caves
is-iceland.climate: Subpolar oceanic climate. Warm currents keep winter from being extremely cold (Reykjavik -3 to 3°C), but it is windy and changeable; summer is cool (9–15°C). The north and the highlands are colder, and the weather can change many times in a day.
notes: Reykjavik -3 to 2°C, about 4–6 hours of daylight, ice cave and northern lights season, many storms
-3 to 3°C, days getting longer, peak ice cave season, road conditions still changeable

is-iceland.avoid: In Nov–Mar storms often close roads, and roads in the north and east are dangerous; Apr is muddy and dull; highland F-roads are closed outside summer; Jul has the highest prices.
is-iceland.tips: Check the Road Administration and Met Office websites every day before setting out. Winter driving needs 4WD and experience on ice and snow. Ice caves can only be entered with a professional guide. A windproof, waterproof shell jacket is more useful than a thick down coat. Iceland is in Schengen; prices are very high, book rooms and car hire ahead.

ee-baltic-states.places: Tallinn Old Town, Saaremaa, Lahemaa National Park, Riga Old Town and Art Nouveau District, Jurmala, Rundale Palace, Vilnius Old Town, Trakai Castle, Curonian Spit, Hill of Crosses
ee-baltic-states.summary: Best: May–Aug for old towns and coast, Dec for the Tallinn Christmas market
ee-baltic-states.climate: Between continental and maritime. Summer is cool and pleasant (18–23°C) with long days; winter is cold, dark (-7 to -1°C) and snowy; the coast is windy.
notes: -7 to -2°C, about 7 hours of daylight, cold and snowy, very few tourists

ee-baltic-states.avoid: Nov and Jan–Feb are grey and cold with short days; around Midsummer some city shops close and the countryside is crowded; Tallinn Old Town is packed on cruise ship days.
ee-baltic-states.tips: All three countries use the euro and are in Schengen. Long-distance buses link Tallinn, Riga and Vilnius, about 4–5 hours per leg. The Tallinn–Helsinki ferry takes about 2 hours. In winter bring warm clothes and non-slip shoes. On cruise ship days visit the Old Town early or late.

ru-moscow-spb.places: Red Square, the Kremlin and St Basil's Cathedral in Moscow, the Winter Palace in St Petersburg, Peterhof, Catherine Palace, Neva River, Sergiev Posad, Suzdal, Vladimir
ru-moscow-spb.summary: Best: May–Aug, white nights in St Petersburg in Jun; snow scenes in winter
ru-moscow-spb.climate: Temperate continental climate. Summer is warm (18–25°C) with the odd heatwave; winter is long, cold (-10 to -4°C) and snowy. St Petersburg is damper and cloudier, with only about 6 hours of daylight in midwinter.
notes: Moscow -10 to -4°C, snow and New Year spirit, Orthodox Christmas in early Jan

ru-moscow-spb.tips: Check the latest visa, flight and safety news before you go. Foreign bank cards have limited use there, so learn the payment options ahead and bring enough cash. Buy tickets online ahead for popular sights like the Winter Palace. Winter needs warm clothes and non-slip shoes. Book rooms ahead for the white nights.

ru-murmansk.places: Murmansk, nuclear icebreaker Lenin, Alyosha Monument, Teriberka, Khibiny Mountains, Kirovsk, Kola Peninsula
ru-murmansk.summary: Best: Jan–Mar for northern lights over snowfields, midnight sun in summer
ru-murmansk.climate: Warm currents make it fairly mild for a place inside the Arctic Circle: winter is -12 to -5°C, colder and windy in cold snaps; polar night lasts from about early Dec to mid Jan; summer is short and cool (10–17°C), with the midnight sun.

ru-murmansk.tips: Check the latest visa, flight and safety news before you go. In winter, join a tour to Teriberka and keep a spare day. You need polar-grade cold-weather gear. The northern lights depend on cloud cover, so stay several nights. Some areas near the border have entry limits, check ahead.

ru-baikal.places: Irkutsk, Listvyanka, Olkhon Island, Khuzhir village, Shaman Rock, Circum-Baikal Railway, Ulan-Ude, Trans-Siberian Railway
ru-baikal.summary: Best: Feb–Mar for blue ice and ice bubbles, Jul–Aug for lakeside hiking
ru-baikal.climate: Strongly continental climate. Winter is bitterly cold (Irkutsk -25 to -10°C) but clear and dry; summer is short and warm (18–26°C), and the lake water is ice-cold; the lake is frozen from about Jan to Apr.

ru-baikal.avoid: Apr–May and Dec–Jan are when the lake ice melts and forms: the ice is dangerous and transport to Olkhon Island is cut off; Nov is windy, grey and cold; in winter always go on the ice with a licensed guide.
ru-baikal.tips: Check the latest visa, flight and safety news before you go. Winter needs gear rated for -30°C; phone batteries freeze and shut down easily. Always follow your guide and local notices when driving or walking on the ice. In summer the Olkhon Island ferry queue is long, so allow extra time. Book Trans-Siberian tickets ahead.

ru-far-east.places: Vladivostok, Russky Island, Golden Horn Bridge, Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky, Avachinsky Volcano, Mutnovsky Volcano, Valley of Geysers, Kurile Lake
ru-far-east.summary: Best: Jul–Sep for Kamchatka's volcanoes and bear watching, Aug–Sep for Vladivostok
ru-far-east.climate: Strong monsoon influence. Vladivostok is humid and foggy in summer (18–24°C), sunniest and warmest in Aug–Sep, and dry, cold and windy in winter (-15 to -6°C). Kamchatka is cool in summer (10–17°C) and snowy in winter, and the weather in the volcano areas changes fast.

ru-far-east.avoid: In Kamchatka, from about Oct to Jun of the next year, snow limits most hiking routes and helicopter trips; Vladivostok is foggy and rainy in Jun–Jul and sometimes hit by typhoons in Aug–Sep; winter winds are biting.
ru-far-east.tips: Check the latest visa, flight and safety news before you go. Kamchatka has limited transport; volcano and bear trips must be with a proper tour, and helicopter trips depend on the weather, so keep spare days. Bring mosquito repellent in summer. Vladivostok is close to Northeast China, so you can look into crossing at the land border.

ua-ukraine.places: Kyiv, Lviv, Odesa, Carpathian Mountains, Kamianets-Podilskyi
ua-ukraine.summary: The safety situation is unusual, always check the latest travel advice before going; in normal years the best time is May–Sep
ua-ukraine.climate: Temperate continental climate. Summer is warm (22–28°C), winter cold (-6 to 0°C) and snowy; the Black Sea coast in the south is milder, and the Carpathians in the west get lots of rain and snow.

eg-egypt.places: Cairo, Pyramids of Giza, Luxor, Aswan, Abu Simbel, Nile cruise, Hurghada, Sharm el-Sheikh, Dahab
eg-egypt.summary: Best: Oct–Mar, cool and dry; Jun–Aug is scorching in the Nile Valley
eg-egypt.climate: Desert climate with little rain all year. In winter (Nov–Feb) days are about 20°C, with cool mornings and evenings; in summer Luxor and Aswan in Upper Egypt often top 40°C. You can dive on the Red Sea coast all year; the water is about 22°C in winter.

eg-egypt.avoid: In Jun–Aug the Nile Valley is often over 40°C by day, hard going for sightseeing; Mar–May has the odd khamsin sandstorm; during Ramadan some restaurants close by day and sights open shorter hours.
eg-egypt.tips: Ramadan follows the Islamic calendar and comes about 11 days earlier each year (see the season highlights for this year's dates); don't eat or drink in public by day. Touts and camel rides at popular sights often ask for money, agree the price first. Set out early in the morning for the Valley of the Kings and Abu Simbel; women should dress modestly. Check the latest safety news before going to northern Sinai and areas near the Libyan border.

ma-morocco.places: Marrakech, Fes, Chefchaouen, Merzouga, Casablanca, Atlas Mountains, Essaouira, Ouarzazate
ma-morocco.summary: Best: Mar–May and Oct–Nov; summer is scorching inland and in the desert
ma-morocco.climate: Mediterranean climate on the northern coast, with wet winters and dry summers. Inland Marrakech often tops 38°C in summer; winter days are about 18°C and nights about 5°C. The Sahara has big swings between day and night, and the Atlas Mountains have snow in winter.
notes: Marrakech days about 18°C, nights about 5°C; desert nights near freezing

Ramadan (follows the Islamic calendar, about 11 days earlier each year): most restaurants close by day and sights open shorter hours; after sunset, iftar meals and night markets are lively
ma-morocco.avoid: Jul–Aug is scorching inland and in the Sahara, over 40°C by day in the desert; during Ramadan (the date changes every year) some restaurants close by day; in Dec–Jan desert nights are near freezing, bring warm clothes.
ma-morocco.tips: Ramadan follows the Islamic calendar and comes about 11 days earlier each year (see the season highlights for this year's dates). The lanes of the old medinas are a maze, be wary of people who offer to show you the way; bargain when shopping. Most mosques are for Muslims only, but the Hassan II Mosque in Casablanca is open to visitors. On desert tours bring a headscarf, sun protection and warm clothes.

tn-tunisia.places: Tunis, Carthage ruins, Sidi Bou Said, Djerba, Douz, Matmata, Tataouine, Kairouan, El Jem Amphitheatre
tn-tunisia.summary: Best: Apr–Jun and Sep–Oct; Jul–Sep for beach holidays
tn-tunisia.climate: Mediterranean climate in the north: mild, rainy winters and hot, dry summers around 32°C. In the Saharan south summer often tops 40°C; winter days are about 18°C, with cold nights.
notes: Tunis days about 16°C, rainy and chilly; desert nights near freezing

Ramadan (follows the Islamic calendar, about 11 days earlier each year): most restaurants close by day and sights open shorter hours; after sunset, iftar meals and night markets are lively
tn-tunisia.avoid: Jul–Aug is scorching in the southern desert, over 40°C, and the beaches are packed and pricey; Dec–Feb is rainy and chilly in the north, not good for swimming.
tn-tunisia.tips: Ramadan follows the Islamic calendar, so the date changes every year (see the season highlights for this year's dates); some restaurants close by day. Check the latest safety news before going to areas near the Algerian and Libyan borders or remote mountain areas. Visit blue-and-white Sidi Bou Said in the morning to avoid tour groups; dress modestly in mosques and holy sites.

et-ethiopia.places: Addis Ababa, Lalibela, Gondar, Aksum, Bahir Dar and Lake Tana, Simien Mountains, Danakil Depression, Omo Valley
et-ethiopia.summary: Best: Oct–Feb dry season; Jan is liveliest, with Christmas and Epiphany
et-ethiopia.climate: Mostly highlands; the capital is about 2,400 m up, with days about 20–25°C all year and cool nights. Jun–Sep is the big rainy season. The Danakil Depression is one of the hottest places on earth, over 45°C in summer.
notes: Highland days about 23°C; Ethiopian Christmas on the 7th and Epiphany around the 19th are the liveliest
Days about 24°C, dry and clear; the Danakil is fairly cool, a good time to go

Timkat (Epiphany) in Gondar (around 19 Jan)
Meskel, the festival of the Cross (around 27 Sep)
Simien Mountains hiking and gelada baboons

Tribal cultures of the Omo Valley
et-ethiopia.avoid: Jun–Aug is the big rainy season: mountain hiking is hampered and country roads are muddy; in Apr–Sep the Danakil Depression is scorching, often over 45°C, not a time to go.
et-ethiopia.tips: Ethiopia uses its own calendar and clock (hours counted from sunrise), so double-check times when booking cars or tickets. The highlands are high up, take it slowly at first and protect yourself from the sun. A yellow fever vaccine is recommended; in the lowlands guard against mosquitoes and malaria. The situation in the north and some border areas changes often, check the latest safety news before you go.

ke-kenya.places: Masai Mara, Amboseli, Lake Nakuru, Nairobi, Samburu, Tsavo, Mombasa, Lamu
ke-kenya.summary: Best: Jul–Oct for the Great Migration, Jan–Feb dry season
ke-kenya.climate: Equatorial highland climate; Nairobi days are about 22–26°C, with cool mornings and evenings. Long rains in Mar–May and short rains in Nov–Dec; the coast is hot and humid at about 30°C. In the dry season the grass is short and water scarce, so animals gather and are easy to see.
notes: Days about 27°C, short dry season, clear, animals easy to see, fair prices

ke-kenya.avoid: In Apr–May the long rains make roads muddy and some camps close; in Jul–Aug high-season camp prices are high, book over six months ahead.
ke-kenya.tips: It sits on the equator but high up, so mornings and evenings are cool, bring a jacket. Yellow fever vaccine and malaria prevention are recommended; wear long sleeves against mosquitoes. Book camps ahead for high season; plastic bags may not be brought into the country. Check the latest safety news before going to the northeast bordering Somalia and some other border areas; don't walk around Nairobi at night.

tz-tanzania-north.places: Serengeti, Ngorongoro Crater, Tarangire, Lake Manyara, Kilimanjaro, Arusha, Lake Natron
tz-tanzania-north.summary: Best: Jun–Oct for dry-season game viewing, Jan–Feb for the calving season in the southern Serengeti
tz-tanzania-north.climate: Highland tropical climate; Arusha days are about 25°C. Long rains in Mar–May, short rains in Nov–Dec. The Ngorongoro Crater rim is about 2,300 m up and cold in the mornings and evenings; the summit of Kilimanjaro is below freezing all year.
notes: Days about 28°C, short dry season, wildebeest gather in the southern Serengeti to give birth

tz-tanzania-north.avoid: In Apr–May the long rains close some camps and make roads muddy, not good for climbing; in the Jul–Sep high season popular areas are crowded with vehicles, book camps six months ahead.
tz-tanzania-north.tips: The migration route changes every year with the rain, so pick your camp location by month. Yellow fever vaccine and malaria prevention are recommended. Bring warm clothes for the crater rim and for climbing. Climbing Kilimanjaro usually takes 5–8 days; choose a longer route to adjust to the altitude. Plastic bags are banned in Tanzania. Check the latest safety news before you go.

tz-zanzibar.places: Stone Town, Nungwi, Kendwa, Paje, Matemwe, Mnemba Atoll, Prison Island, Jozani Forest
tz-zanzibar.summary: Best: Jun–Oct, dry and cooler; Jan–Feb, hot and sunny
tz-zanzibar.climate: Tropical maritime climate, days about 28–33°C all year. Most rain falls in the long rains of Mar–May, with short rains in Nov; Jun–Oct is cooler and drier thanks to the southeast trade winds. The east coast has a big tidal range.
notes: Days about 32°C, hot and sunny, clear water good for diving

tz-zanzibar.avoid: Apr–May is the long rains, humid and wet, and many resorts close; late Dec to early Jan and Jul–Aug are high season, with high prices, book ahead.
tz-zanzibar.tips: The east coast has a big tidal range and the sea goes out a long way at low tide, keep this in mind when choosing a hotel. Most people are Muslim; in Stone Town cover shoulders and knees, and during Ramadan (the date changes every year) avoid eating or drinking in public by day. Recently, visitors must buy the official local travel insurance to enter, confirm before you go. Guard against mosquitoes and check yellow fever vaccine rules. Check the latest safety news before you go.

rw-rwanda-uganda.places: Volcanoes National Park, Bwindi Forest, Kibale Forest, Nyungwe Forest, Kigali, Queen Elizabeth National Park, Lake Kivu, Murchison Falls
rw-rwanda-uganda.summary: Best: Jun–Sep and Dec–Feb dry seasons for gorilla trekking
rw-rwanda-uganda.climate: Equatorial highland climate; Kigali days are about 26°C all year. The volcano area is over 2,000 m up, about 10°C in the mornings and evenings. Long rains in Mar–May, short rains in Oct–Nov; it can rain in the rainforest at any time of year.

rw-rwanda-uganda.avoid: In Apr–May the long rains make trails muddy and slippery, and trekking is very tiring; in high season gorilla permits often sell out months ahead.
rw-rwanda-uganda.tips: Gorilla permits cost about US$1,500 per person in Rwanda and about US$800 in Uganda; prices may change, book ahead. Trekking needs some fitness; bring a waterproof jacket, gardening gloves and non-slip hiking boots. Yellow fever vaccine is required; take malaria precautions. Rwanda bans plastic bags. Check the latest safety news before going to areas on the DR Congo border.

za-cape-town.places: Cape Town, Table Mountain, Cape of Good Hope, Boulders Beach penguins, Stellenbosch, Franschhoek, Hermanus, Knysna, Tsitsikamma
za-cape-town.summary: Best: Nov–Mar for sunny summer, Sep–Oct for whales and wildflowers
za-cape-town.climate: Mediterranean climate, with seasons the reverse of the northern hemisphere. Summer (Nov–Mar) is dry and sunny, days about 26°C, often with the strong southeasterly wind called the "Cape Doctor"; winter (Jun–Aug) is rainy and chilly, days about 17°C.

za-cape-town.avoid: Jun–Aug winter is rainy and windy, and the Table Mountain cable car often stops for weather; mid Dec to mid Jan is the local summer holiday high season, when rooms are pricey and must be booked early.
za-cape-town.tips: Southern hemisphere seasons are the reverse of China's. The Table Mountain cable car stops in strong winds, so plan around the weather. Stay alert to crime in Cape Town: avoid walking at night, don't leave valuables in the car, and don't go alone to some parts of the city. Recently there have been occasional power cuts, check whether your accommodation has backup power. Drive on the left.

za-kruger.places: Kruger National Park, Sabi Sand private reserve, Blyde River Canyon, God's Window, Johannesburg, Soweto, Pretoria
za-kruger.summary: Best: May–Oct dry season for game viewing: short grass, few mosquitoes, animals gathered together
za-kruger.climate: Summer (Nov–Mar) is hot and humid with thunderstorms, Kruger days about 32°C; winter (May–Sep) is dry and sunny, days about 25°C, early mornings down to 5°C. Johannesburg is about 1,750 m up, with cold winter nights.

za-kruger.tips: Seasons are reversed in the southern hemisphere. Kruger is a malaria area, with higher risk in Nov–Apr; ask a doctor about medicine and guard against mosquitoes. The park has speed limits, you may not get out of your car, and camp gates open and close on time. Johannesburg has poor safety: avoid walking at night or going around the city centre alone, and lock the doors when driving.

na-namibia.summary: Best: May–Oct dry season; Jul–Oct is the top time for game viewing in Etosha
na-namibia.climate: Desert and semi-arid climate with many sunny days all year. In summer (Nov–Mar) inland can top 35°C, with thunderstorms; in winter (Jun–Aug) days are about 22°C and desert nights near 0°C. The coast, cooled by a cold current, often has morning fog and is about 18°C.

na-namibia.avoid: Nov–Mar is scorching inland, the desert often over 40°C by day; in Feb the rains in the north block some gravel roads; in the Jul–Aug high season, book rental cars and campsites months ahead.
na-namibia.tips: Seasons are reversed in the southern hemisphere. Most driving is on gravel roads: always rent a 4WD with two spare tyres, and don't drive at night; fuel stations are far apart, fill up whenever you see one. In winter desert days and nights differ a lot, bring warm clothes. North of Etosha is a malaria area, guard against mosquitoes in the rainy season.

bw-botswana.climate: Semi-arid climate. The Nov–Mar rainy season is hot with thunderstorms, days about 33°C; the May–Sep dry season is clear and dry, days about 25°C, nights can drop below 5°C. The Okavango flood is highest in about Jun–Aug.

bw-botswana.tips: Seasons are reversed in the southern hemisphere. Botswana focuses on high-end, low-density tourism; high-season camps are pricey, book about a year ahead. Light aircraft into the interior limit luggage to about 20 kg, in soft bags only. The north is a malaria area, guard against mosquitoes. Dry-season mornings and evenings are cold, bring a warm jacket on game drives.

zw-victoria-falls.places: Victoria Falls Town, Livingstone, Devil's Pool, Livingstone Island, Knife-Edge Bridge, Zambezi River, Mosi-oa-Tunya National Park, Chobe National Park
zw-victoria-falls.summary: Best: May–Aug for big water and good views, Sep–Dec for Devil's Pool
zw-victoria-falls.climate: Subtropical highland climate. The Nov–Mar rainy season is hot with thunderstorms, about 30°C; in the May–Aug dry season days are about 25°C and nights cool. The falls' flow lags behind the rains: highest in Mar–May, lowest in Oct–Dec.

zw-victoria-falls.tips: Each side has its own appeal: the Zimbabwe side has more front-on viewpoints, the Zambian side lets you get up close. The KAZA UniVisa covers trips between both countries and day trips to Chobe; check the rules before you go. A raincoat or dry bag is a must. It is a malaria area, guard against mosquitoes; for bungee jumping and similar activities choose a licensed operator.

mg-madagascar.places: Antananarivo, Avenue of the Baobabs in Morondava, Tsingy de Bemaraha National Park, Andasibe, Ranomafana, Isalo, Nosy Be, Sainte-Marie Island

mg-madagascar.climate: Tropical climate. The eastern rainforest is wet all year, the west and south drier. Nov–Mar is the hot, wet rainy season with cyclones, Apr–Oct the cool dry season; in the highland capital, winter nights can drop to about 8°C.

mg-madagascar.avoid: Jan–Mar is the rainy and cyclone season: western roads are cut off and Tsingy is closed; from Dec roads get blocked, so long overland trips are risky.
mg-madagascar.tips: Seasons are reversed in the southern hemisphere. Roads are poor and long drives take time; hire a car with a driver or take domestic flights, which are often delayed, so leave spare time. Take malaria precautions; in the rainforest bring a raincoat and leech socks. The capital is not very safe at night, don't go out on foot. Check the latest safety news before you go.

mu-mauritius.places: Port Louis, Grand Baie, Le Morne Brabant, Seven Coloured Earths, Black River Gorges National Park, Île aux Cerfs, Blue Bay, Belle Mare, Grand Bassin
mu-mauritius.summary: Best: May and Sep–Nov, dry and comfortable; avoid the Jan–Mar cyclone season
mu-mauritius.climate: Subtropical maritime climate, warm all year. Nov–Apr is the hot, humid summer, days about 30°C, with cyclone risk in Jan–Mar; May–Oct is the cool winter, days about 24°C, with strong southeast trade winds and a windy east coast.

mu-mauritius.avoid: Jan–Mar is cyclone season, when strong winds and heavy rain can upset plans; prices are highest from late Dec to early Jan and during European holidays.
mu-mauritius.tips: Seasons are reversed in the southern hemisphere; Jun–Aug mornings and evenings are cool, bring a jacket. In winter the east coast is windy with big waves, so pick your coast by season: in winter the west and north coasts are more sheltered. Drive on the left. Most people are of Indian descent, and festival dates follow the Hindu calendar, changing every year. Protect yourself from the sun and mosquitoes.

sc-seychelles.places: Mahé, Praslin, La Digue, Vallée de Mai, Anse Source d'Argent, Anse Lazio, Victoria, Curieuse Island, Sainte Anne Marine Park
sc-seychelles.summary: Best: Apr–May and Oct–Nov, calm seas between the monsoons
sc-seychelles.climate: Equatorial maritime climate, about 27–31°C all year. Dec–Mar brings the northwest monsoon, hot, humid and rainy; May–Sep brings the southeast monsoon, drier but windy with rough seas; Apr and Oct–Nov are in-between times with calm seas. It lies outside the cyclone belt and is rarely hit directly.
notes: About 30°C, wettest time of year, many showers but mostly short

sc-seychelles.avoid: Dec–Jan has the most rain, with frequent showers; in Jun–Sep the southeast monsoon is strong, and some beaches have big waves and piles of seaweed, not good for swimming.
sc-seychelles.tips: Prices are high; travel between islands is by ferry or small plane, book ahead in high season. Different monsoons hit different coasts, so pick a sheltered beach by season. Some beaches have rip currents, watch for warning signs. You must apply online ahead for a travel authorisation to enter (there is a fee). Protect yourself from the sun and mosquitoes.

au-sydney-nsw.places: Sydney, Sydney Opera House, Bondi Beach, Blue Mountains, Hunter Valley, Byron Bay, Port Stephens, Jervis Bay
au-sydney-nsw.summary: Best: Mar–Apr and Sep–Dec, mild and pleasant; Jan–Feb beach season
au-sydney-nsw.climate: Temperate maritime climate, with seasons the reverse of the northern hemisphere. Summer (Dec–Feb) days are about 26°C, with the odd heatwave over 35°C; winter (Jun–Aug) days are about 17°C, with lots of sunny days. The Blue Mountains are cold in winter, with the odd snowfall.

au-sydney-nsw.avoid: Late Dec to Jan is the school summer holiday, with the highest flight and room prices and crowded beaches; summer sometimes brings heatwaves and bushfires, watch for fire warnings.
au-sydney-nsw.tips: Seasons are reversed in the southern hemisphere, summer is Dec–Feb. UV is extremely strong, always use sun protection; at beaches swim only between the red and yellow flags. You need a visa or electronic travel authority before arrival; quarantine is strict and food must be declared. Drive on the left. In bushfire season follow official fire warnings.

au-melbourne-vic.places: Melbourne, Great Ocean Road, Twelve Apostles, Phillip Island, Yarra Valley, Dandenong Ranges, Grampians National Park, Mornington Peninsula
au-melbourne-vic.summary: Best: Nov–Mar summer, Apr for lovely autumn colours
au-melbourne-vic.climate: Temperate maritime climate, famous for "four seasons in one day", with changeable weather. Summer (Dec–Feb) days are about 26°C, with the odd 40°C heatwave; winter (Jun–Aug) days are about 14°C, grey, cold, windy and wet. The Great Ocean Road coast is windy and cool.
notes: About 26°C, the odd heatwave, Australian Open in mid to late Jan, summer holiday high season

au-melbourne-vic.avoid: Jun–Aug is grey, cold and rainy, and the Great Ocean Road is windy with rough seas and limited views; summer has the odd 40°C heatwave and bushfire risk, keep an eye on fires.
au-melbourne-vic.tips: Seasons are reversed in the southern hemisphere. Melbourne's weather changes fast, bring a jacket even in summer. Allow two days or more for the Great Ocean Road; drive on the left and watch for wildlife at dusk. Photos and videos are not allowed during the Phillip Island penguin parade. UV is strong, use sun protection.

au-queensland.places: Cairns, Great Barrier Reef, Port Douglas, Daintree Rainforest, Whitsunday Islands, Whitehaven Beach, Gold Coast, Brisbane, Sunshine Coast, K'gari
au-queensland.summary: Best: Jun–Oct dry season; in the north, avoid the Dec–Mar rains and jellyfish
au-queensland.climate: Tropical in the north: in Cairns the Nov–Apr wet season is muggy and rainy with cyclones, days about 31°C; the May–Oct dry season is dry and fresh, days about 26°C. Brisbane and the Gold Coast in the south are subtropical, about 21°C in winter.
notes: Cairns about 31°C, hot and humid, rainy season with cyclones; Gold Coast crowded for summer holidays

au-queensland.avoid: Dec–Mar is the muggy, rainy wet season in the north, with the highest cyclone risk in Feb–Mar; in Nov–May there are box jellyfish in northern waters, wear a stinger suit and swim inside the nets.
au-queensland.tips: Seasons are reversed in the southern hemisphere. In the northern jellyfish season always wear a stinger suit in the sea; at river mouths and beaches watch for crocodile warning signs, and never go in the water where there is a warning. If you get seasick, take medicine before boat trips. UV is extremely strong, use reef-friendly sunscreen. In cyclone season follow weather warnings and buy insurance that covers weather delays.

au-northern-territory.places: Uluru, Kata Tjuta, Kings Canyon, Alice Springs, Darwin, Kakadu National Park, Litchfield National Park, Katherine Gorge
au-northern-territory.summary: Best: May–Sep, cool and dry, good for both the Red Centre and the Top End
au-northern-territory.climate: The Red Centre in the south has a desert climate: summer often tops 38°C; winter days are about 20°C and nights can drop below 0°C. Darwin in the Top End is tropical: the May–Oct dry season is sunny at about 31°C; the Nov–Apr wet season brings storms, and many parts of Kakadu close.

au-northern-territory.avoid: In Dec–Mar the Centre is scorching, over 38°C, and the north has wet-season storms, with many Kakadu roads and sights closed; in Oct–Nov the build-up season in the north is unbearably muggy.
au-northern-territory.tips: Seasons are reversed in the southern hemisphere. Climbing Uluru is banned; it is an Aboriginal sacred site, and photos are banned in some areas. In the Centre trails close early in high heat; set out early in the morning with plenty of water, and a fly net is very useful. Northern waters have saltwater crocodiles, only swim in marked areas. On long drives, mind the distances between fuel stations.

au-western-australia.places: Perth, Fremantle, Rottnest Island, Pinnacles, Ningaloo Reef, Exmouth, Shark Bay, Margaret River, Broome, Kimberley
au-western-australia.summary: Best: Apr–Jun for whale sharks, Sep–Oct for wildflowers
au-western-australia.climate: Perth has a Mediterranean climate: summer is hot and dry at about 31°C, winter mild and rainy at about 18°C. The Kimberley and Broome in the north are tropical: the May–Oct dry season is best; the Nov–Apr wet season brings storms, closed roads and cyclones.

au-western-australia.tips: Seasons are reversed in the southern hemisphere. Western Australia is huge, with sights hundreds to over 1,000 km apart; split the trip by region and take domestic flights. Long drives in the north need a 4WD and plenty of water and fuel; don't take unsealed roads in the wet season. Book Ningaloo whale shark tours ahead. Watch out for crocodiles and jellyfish in northern waters.

au-south-australia.places: Adelaide, Kangaroo Island, Barossa Valley, McLaren Vale, Clare Valley, Flinders Ranges, Coober Pedy, Whyalla
au-south-australia.summary: Best: Mar–Apr and Oct–Nov, mild; Mar has the most festivals
au-south-australia.climate: Mediterranean climate. Summer (Dec–Feb) is hot and dry, Adelaide days about 29°C, over 40°C in heatwaves; winter (Jun–Aug) is mild and rainy at about 15°C. Kangaroo Island is cooler, and the northern inland desert is scorching in summer.

au-south-australia.tips: Seasons are reversed in the southern hemisphere. Kangaroo Island is reached by ferry or plane; book the car ferry ahead in high season; driving on the island at night it is easy to hit animals. Inland places like Coober Pedy are extremely hot in summer, go in the cool season. For wine tasting, hire a car with a driver or have a designated driver; Australia has strict drink-driving checks.

au-tasmania.summary: Best: Dec–Mar summer, lavender in full bloom in Jan
au-tasmania.climate: Cool temperate maritime climate. Summer (Dec–Feb) days are about 22°C, sunny and comfortable but with strong UV; winter (Jun–Aug) days are about 12°C, with frequent snow in highlands like Cradle Mountain. The west is rainy, the east coast drier and sunnier.

au-tasmania.tips: Seasons are reversed in the southern hemisphere; even in summer bring a warm, windproof jacket. Book the Overland Track ahead in high season. Tasmania has strict quarantine, don't bring fresh fruit or vegetables onto the island. Driving at dusk and at night you may meet wombats and other animals, so try to avoid it. UV is strong, use sun protection.

nz-north-island.places: Auckland, Rotorua, Hobbiton, Waitomo Glowworm Caves, Taupo, Tongariro National Park, Bay of Islands, Coromandel, Wellington
nz-north-island.summary: Best: Jan–Mar for sunny summer days, Nov for spring with fewer people
nz-north-island.climate: Temperate oceanic climate, close to subtropical in the north. In summer (Dec–Feb) Auckland days are about 24°C; in winter (Jun–Aug) about 15°C and rainy. Rain is fairly even all year and the weather changes a lot; the high Tongariro mountains get snow in winter and you can ski.

nz-north-island.tips: Seasons are reversed in the Southern Hemisphere. Get a visa or electronic travel authority before you go and pay the tourist levy. Biosecurity checks are strict: declare food and outdoor shoes with mud on them. UV is strong, wear sunscreen. Mountain weather changes fast; bring a windproof, waterproof jacket for hikes. Drive on the left.

Glacier hikes are only by helicopter tour onto the ice. Book Milford and other big tracks ahead on the Department of Conservation website. Winter driving needs snow experience; drive on the left. Guard against sandfly bites on the West Coast and in the fiords.

Most villages rest on Sunday and some services stop. In cyclone season buy travel insurance that covers weather delays. Use sunscreen and insect repellent (dengue).

pf-french-polynesia.places: Tahiti, Papeete, Bora Bora, Moorea, Rangiroa, Fakarava, Tikehau, Huahine, Taha'a
pf-french-polynesia.summary: Best: May–Oct dry season, Jul–Oct for humpback whales
pf-french-polynesia.climate: Tropical oceanic climate, about 25–31°C all year. Nov–Apr is the hot, humid rainy season, with many showers and the odd cyclone; May–Oct is the cooler dry season, when southeast trade winds sometimes bring strong winds. The sea is about 26–29°C all year.
notes: About 31°C, hot and humid, wettest month, frequent showers, the odd cyclone

About 30°C, rain easing, more sun, good diving
About 30°C, end of the rainy season, humidity dropping, fewer visitors

About 27°C, Heiva festival in Tahiti, humpback whales start to arrive

About 28°C, sunny and dry, peak for humpback whales (Moorea and others)
About 28°C, whale watching still good, end of the dry season, fewer visitors
