highlights: Humpback whale watching off Moorea and Rurutu
Heiva i Tahiti (traditional dance and sports in Jul)
Teahupo'o surf contest (usually Aug)
Grouper spawning and the wall of sharks at Fakarava's South Pass
Diving Tiputa Pass at Rangiroa (hammerhead season)
Overwater bungalows and lagoon snorkelling in Bora Bora
pf-french-polynesia.avoid: Dec–Mar rainy season has many showers, hot and humid, the odd cyclone. Jul–Aug is the European and local holiday time; overwater bungalows cost the most, book early.
pf-french-polynesia.tips: Seasons are reversed in the Southern Hemisphere. Prices are high; island hopping is mostly by inter-island flight, and you can buy an air pass. For whale watching choose a licensed operator and keep the required distance. The currency is the Pacific franc; credit cards are widely accepted. Use sunscreen and insect repellent (dengue).

pw-palau.places: Koror, Rock Islands, Jellyfish Lake, Milky Way, Blue Corner, German Channel, Babeldaob, Peleliu
pw-palau.summary: Best: Jan–Apr, drier, calm seas and good diving visibility
pw-palau.climate: Tropical oceanic climate, about 27–31°C all year, humid with showers all year round. Feb–Apr is drier; Jun–Oct is the southwest monsoon rainy season, with bigger winds and waves. It lies on the southern edge of the typhoon belt and is sometimes brushed by the outer bands of typhoons.
notes: About 30°C, northeast trade winds, fairly calm seas, good diving visibility
About 30°C, drier; big schools of fish and sharks active at Blue Corner
About 31°C, many sunny days, peak diving season
About 31°C, end of the dry season, good seas, good for island hopping and kayaking
About 31°C, more rain, winds changing, diving still OK
About 30°C, southwest monsoon rains begin, winds and waves pick up
About 30°C, many showers, unsettled seas, some dive sites affected
About 30°C, quite rainy, sometimes brushed by typhoons, low prices
About 30°C, rainy season, rough seas, few visitors
About 30°C, rain easing, winds changing, seas improving
About 30°C, trade winds return, diving season begins
About 30°C, seas improving, Christmas holidays are peak diving season
highlights: Diving Blue Corner and German Channel (sharks, manta rays)
Kayaking the Rock Islands and the Milky Way
Snorkelling Jellyfish Lake (opening depends on jellyfish numbers; check official notices)
WWII sites and wreck diving at Peleliu
Hiking to the stone monoliths and waterfalls on Babeldaob
pw-palau.avoid: Jun–Oct southwest monsoon rainy season: rough seas, some dive sites and flights affected, sometimes brushed by typhoons.
pw-palau.tips: On arrival you must sign the "Palau Pledge" and pay an environment fee (usually included in the air ticket). Only reef-safe sunscreen is allowed; sunscreens with certain ingredients are banned. You need a permit to visit the Rock Islands. The currency is the US dollar. Leave enough time after diving before you fly.

gu-guam-saipan.region: Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands
gu-guam-saipan.places: Tumon Bay, Two Lovers Point, War in the Pacific National Historical Park, Managaha Island in Saipan, Saipan Grotto, Bird Island, Tinian, Rota
gu-guam-saipan.summary: Best: Jan–Apr, sunny dry season; avoid the Aug–Oct typhoon peak
gu-guam-saipan.climate: Tropical oceanic climate, about 27–31°C all year. Dec–Jun is the dry season, when northeast trade winds bring sunny, dry weather; Jul–Nov is the rainy season, muggy with many showers, and typhoon risk is higher in Aug–Oct. A strong typhoon can cut power and stop flights and boats for a long time.
notes: About 29°C, cool trade winds in the dry season, calm seas, good snorkelling
About 29°C, sunny and dry, good diving at the Grotto, busy around Chinese New Year
About 30°C, dry and sunny, one of the most comfortable months
About 30°C, dry season, clear water, good for hopping to Tinian and Rota
About 31°C, getting hot, end of the dry season, the odd early typhoon
About 31°C, humidity rising, flame trees in bloom, fewer visitors
About 31°C, rainy season begins, many showers; Guam Liberation Day on the 21st

About 30°C, typhoon peak, rough seas, lowest prices

highlights: Diving the Saipan Grotto (when the sea is calm)
Snorkelling at Managaha Island
Guam Liberation Day (21 Jul)
Island hopping to Tinian and Rota
Flame tree (flamboyant) blooming season
Two Lovers Point and WWII sites
gu-guam-saipan.avoid: Aug–Oct is the typhoon peak; a strong typhoon can cancel flights and cut power and water. The Jul–Nov rainy season is muggy with unsettled seas.
gu-guam-saipan.tips: Guam is US territory, so US entry rules apply; the Northern Mariana Islands have separate entry arrangements for some countries, and the rules change often, so check before you go. Use sunscreen all year and choose reef-safe products. In typhoon season, buy insurance that covers trip delays and watch the weather warnings. Rental cars drive on the right.

nc-new-caledonia.places: Nouméa, Isle of Pines, Ouvéa, Lifou, Maré, Prony Bay, Heart of Voh mangroves, Blue River Park
nc-new-caledonia.summary: Best: Sep–Nov, dry and warm; Aug is peak whale watching
nc-new-caledonia.climate: Tropical oceanic climate, kept fairly mild by the trade winds. Nov–Mar is the hot wet season at about 30°C, with tropical cyclones in Jan–Mar; Jun–Aug is the cool season, about 23°C by day and 16°C at night. Sep–Nov is dry and sunny, the most pleasant time.
notes: About 30°C, hot and humid, lots of rain, high cyclone risk, warm sea
About 30°C, peak rainy season, cyclones active, ferries may stop
About 29°C, still hot, humid and rainy, cyclone risk continues
About 27°C, less rain, weather turning comfortable, few visitors
About 25°C, cool and dry, good for hiking and driving in the south

Diving and snorkelling in the World Heritage lagoon
Scenic flight over the Heart of Voh mangroves
Hiking in Blue River Park
Flame tree blooming season
nc-new-caledonia.avoid: Jan–Mar is cyclone season; strong winds and heavy rain can stop flights and ferries. In Jun–Aug the sea is cool, best to wear a wetsuit.
nc-new-caledonia.tips: Seasons are reversed in the Southern Hemisphere. It is a French overseas territory: the currency is the Pacific franc, French is the main language, and prices are fairly high. Flights and ferries to the outer islands are limited; book ahead in high season. Many shops close on Sunday. There has been social unrest; check the latest safety situation before you go.

vu-vanuatu-cook-islands.places: Port Vila, Mt Yasur volcano on Tanna, Espiritu Santo, Champagne Beach, Pentecost Island, Rarotonga, Aitutaki Lagoon, Atiu
vu-vanuatu-cook-islands.summary: Best: May–Oct, cool dry season; avoid the Jan–Mar cyclone season
vu-vanuatu-cook-islands.climate: Tropical oceanic climate, about 24–30°C all year. Nov–Apr is the hot, humid rainy season, with tropical cyclones most likely in Jan–Mar; May–Oct is the cool dry season, when trade winds bring dry weather, and winter nights in the Cook Islands are about 18°C.
notes: About 30°C, hot, humid and rainy, cyclone season, warm sea

About 29°C, still cyclone risk, rain easing

Cook Islands cultural festival (late Jul to early Aug)
Diving the SS President Coolidge wreck off Santo
Day trip to Aitutaki Lagoon
vu-vanuatu-cook-islands.avoid: Jan–Mar is the cyclone peak; strong winds and heavy rain can stop flights and cut power, and outer islands have few facilities. Dec–Apr is hot, humid and rainy, with more mosquitoes.
vu-vanuatu-cook-islands.tips: Seasons are reversed in the Southern Hemisphere. Flights to the outer islands are few and often change, so leave spare time in your plan. Mt Yasur opens depending on the alert level, and you must go with a local guide. When visiting villages in Vanuatu, respect local customs and ask before taking photos. The Cook Islands use the New Zealand dollar. Use insect repellent (dengue).

aq-antarctica.region: Antarctic Peninsula and South Shetland Islands
aq-antarctica.places: Ushuaia, Drake Passage, South Shetland Islands, Deception Island, Antarctic Peninsula, Paradise Bay, Lemaire Channel, South Georgia, Falkland Islands
aq-antarctica.summary: Best: Dec–Feb, warmest with long daylight; trips only run Nov–Mar
aq-antarctica.climate: Polar climate. The expedition season is the southern summer (Nov–Mar), when the coast of the Antarctic Peninsula is about -5 to 5°C and daylight can last nearly 20 hours. The Drake Passage has big winds and waves, and the crossing takes about 2 days. In Apr–Oct the sea ice spreads and it is bitterly cold, with no regular tourist trips.
notes: About 0 to 5°C, midsummer, longest daylight, penguin chicks hatch, high season
About 0 to 3°C, chicks growing, more whales, little sea ice so ships can go further south
About -2 to 2°C, end of the season, peak whale activity, lower prices
Below about -5°C, sea ice spreading, expedition season over, no regular trips
About -8°C on the peninsula coast, days shorten fast, closed to tourists
Below about -10°C on the coast, very short days, only research station staff stay
Deep winter, about -10 to -20°C, sea ice cover, no tourist trips
Below about -10°C, frequent blizzards, no tourist trips
About -10°C, sea ice near its largest of the year, closed to tourists
About -8°C, sea ice still thick, expedition season not yet started
About -5 to 0°C, start of the season, clean white snow, penguins courting and nesting
About -2 to 3°C, penguins sitting on eggs, nearly 20 hours of daylight, Christmas high season
highlights: Penguins courting, nesting and sitting on eggs (snow at its most untouched)
Penguin chicks hatching and growing
Peak whale watching for humpback and minke whales
Zodiac cruises among icebergs, and kayaking
Trips that cross the Antarctic Circle (66°33'S)
King penguin colonies on South Georgia (combined trips)
Camping overnight in Antarctica (some trips)
aq-antarctica.avoid: Apr–Oct has sea ice and severe cold, with no regular tourist trips. In early Nov sea ice may block some landing sites; in late Mar the weather gets worse and there are fewer chances to land.
aq-antarctica.tips: Almost all trips leave by expedition ship from Ushuaia in Argentina and take about 2 days to cross the Drake Passage; seasickness is common, so bring medicine. You can also choose a trip that flies over the passage. In high season, book a cabin about a year ahead. Follow the IAATO (International Association of Antarctica Tour Operators) rules: stay at least 5 m from animals and clean your gear before going ashore.

xx-arctic.region: Svalbard, Greenland and the North Pole
xx-arctic.places: Longyearbyen, Ny-Ålesund, Svalbard, Ilulissat, Disko Bay, Scoresby Sund, Nuuk, North Pole
xx-arctic.summary: Best: Jun–Aug for midnight sun voyages, Mar–Apr for snow and the northern lights
xx-arctic.climate: Polar climate. In summer (Jun–Aug) Svalbard is about 3–7°C with 24-hour daylight; winter (Nov–Feb) is polar night, about -15°C and as low as -30°C. Coastal Greenland is about 5–10°C in summer; the inland ice sheet is bitterly cold all year.
notes: Svalbard about -15°C, polar night and dark all day; northern lights possible even at midday
About -16°C, daylight returning, good for northern lights and dog sledding
About -15°C, Sun Festival in Longyearbyen early in the month, snowmobiling and northern lights both possible

Humpback whales in Disko Bay
The northern lights
Snowmobiling and dog sledding
Sun Festival in Longyearbyen (early Mar)
Icebreaker trips to the North Pole (depends on whether they run that year)
xx-arctic.avoid: Nov–Jan is polar night, dark all day and bitterly cold, with few outdoor activities. May and Sep–Oct are the melt and in-between times, not ideal for snow activities or voyages.
xx-arctic.tips: Svalbard has polar bears; outside Longyearbyen you must go with an armed guide. Book summer expedition cruises six months to a year ahead. In winter bring proper cold-weather gear; batteries drain fast. North Pole icebreaker trips have been limited in recent years, so check the latest before you go. In Greenland you get around by plane, and flights are often delayed by weather.

us-northeast.places: New York, Boston, Philadelphia, Washington, D.C., Vermont, White Mountains in New Hampshire, Acadia National Park in Maine, Cape Cod
us-northeast.summary: Best: May–Jun and Sep–Oct; New England's autumn leaves peak in early to mid Oct
us-northeast.climate: Humid continental climate with four clear seasons. Winter is cold and snowy, with frequent snowstorms; summer is hot and humid, often over 30°C in New York and Washington; spring and autumn are mild and dry, the most comfortable seasons.
notes: New York about -3 to 4°C, cold with frequent snowstorms, lowest hotel prices of the year

About 2 to 11°C, warm one day, cold the next; Washington's cherry blossoms may open late in the month

About 12 to 22°C, warm and comfortable, parks in bloom, crowds over Memorial Day late in the month

Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York (fourth Thursday of Nov)
Rockefeller Center Christmas tree, Fifth Avenue window displays and the Times Square New Year countdown
us-northeast.avoid: Jan–Feb is bitterly cold with many snowstorms, and flights are often delayed. Jul–Aug is hot, humid and crowded with summer holidays. Accommodation prices soar on autumn-leaf weekends and around Thanksgiving and Christmas.
us-northeast.tips: New York hotels are expensive; in leaf season book Vermont and White Mountains inns 2–3 months ahead. For sunrise on Cadillac Mountain in Acadia in high season, reserve a car spot online. Around Thanksgiving and Christmas, traffic is heavy and flights are pricey. Chinese visitors need a US visa and must register with EVUS. In winter bring a down jacket and non-slip shoes.

us-florida.places: Miami, Orlando theme parks, Key West, Everglades National Park, Tampa, Fort Lauderdale, Kennedy Space Center, St. Augustine
us-florida.summary: Best: Dec–Apr, warm dry season with little rain; avoid the Aug–Oct hurricane peak
us-florida.climate: Subtropical to tropical climate. Nov–Apr is the dry season, warm and sunny; May–Oct is the rainy season, hot and humid with frequent afternoon thunderstorms. Jun–Nov is the Atlantic hurricane season, with the highest risk in Aug–Oct.
notes: Miami about 16 to 24°C, dry and sunny; Orlando in the north is cool in the morning and evening

us-florida.avoid: Aug–Oct is the hurricane peak, with possible flight cancellations and evacuations. Jun–Sep is very hot with many thunderstorms. Spring break in Mar and Christmas–New Year bring the biggest theme park crowds and highest ticket prices.
us-florida.tips: Book theme park tickets and hotels ahead, and make good use of skip-the-line services. In hurricane season buy travel insurance that covers hurricanes and follow the US National Hurricane Center warnings. Use sunscreen and insect repellent; don't go near alligators in the Everglades. On the Overseas Highway to Key West, watch the speed limits and weekend traffic jams.

us-south.places: New Orleans, Austin, Nashville, Charleston, Savannah, Memphis, San Antonio
us-south.summary: Best: Mar–May and Oct–Nov; avoid the hot, humid midsummer and hurricane season
us-south.climate: Humid subtropical climate. Summer is long, hot and humid, often 33–36°C, with many afternoon thunderstorms; winter is mild with the odd cold snap; spring and autumn are warm and pleasant. The Gulf of Mexico coast is hit by hurricanes in Jun–Nov.
notes: New Orleans about 7 to 17°C, mild with the odd cold snap, fewer visitors

us-south.avoid: Jul–Sep is muggy and often over 35°C, and the Gulf coast has the highest hurricane risk in Aug–Oct. During Mardi Gras and big music festivals, accommodation prices can double or more.
us-south.tips: Book hotels months ahead for Mardi Gras, Jazz Fest and SXSW. In New Orleans, avoid walking alone in quiet streets at night and watch your belongings. In summer guard against heat and mosquitoes; in hurricane season watch the warnings and buy travel insurance. Southern cities are far apart, so drive or take domestic flights.

us-california.places: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Yosemite National Park, Big Sur on Highway 1, Napa Valley, Sequoia National Park, Palm Springs
us-california.summary: Best: Apr–May and Sep–Oct; Yosemite's waterfalls are most impressive in spring
us-california.climate: Mediterranean climate, with mild, rainy winters and dry summers. The coast is cool, and San Francisco is often foggy in summer at about 15–20°C; inland and Southern California are hot in summer, and high parts of Yosemite have snow in winter. Wildfire risk in summer and autumn.
notes: Los Angeles about 9 to 20°C; rainy in Northern California, Yosemite under winter snow
About 10 to 20°C, rainy season, Big Sur roads may close for landslides, gray whales can be seen

us-california.avoid: Jul–Aug brings the biggest crowds to popular parks. The Aug–Nov wildfire season may close roads and spoil the air. Jan–Feb is rainy in Northern California, and Highway 1 at Big Sur is often cut by landslides.
us-california.tips: At Yosemite's summer peak you may need an entry reservation; book lodging inside the park a year ahead. Check road conditions on the Big Sur stretch of Highway 1 before you go. Bring a jacket in San Francisco even in summer. In Los Angeles avoid the morning and evening rush hours. Don't leave valuables in the car; break-ins are common.

us-southwest.places: Grand Canyon, Las Vegas, Antelope Canyon, Horseshoe Bend, Zion National Park, Bryce Canyon, Arches National Park, Death Valley, Monument Valley, Sedona
us-southwest.summary: Best: Apr–May and Oct for comfortable temperatures; midsummer is very hot and the plateau has snow in winter
us-southwest.climate: Dry desert and plateau climate with big day–night temperature swings. In summer the canyon floors and Death Valley often pass 40–50°C, and Jul–Sep brings afternoon monsoon thunderstorms and flash floods; winter on the plateau is cold and snowy, with snow at Bryce and the Grand Canyon's North Rim.

About 8 to 21°C, warming up, spring break crowds, Death Valley wildflowers may bloom
About 12 to 25°C, most comfortable temperatures in all the parks, golden time for hiking
About 17 to 31°C, sunny and dry, Grand Canyon North Rim usually opens mid month

us-southwest.avoid: Jul–Aug is very hot with many flash floods, and slot canyons may close at short notice. Dec–Feb has icy plateau roads and the Grand Canyon North Rim is closed. In spring break and summer holidays, parking is hard at popular parks.
us-southwest.tips: Angels Landing in Zion needs a permit from an online lottery, and Arches National Park may need a timed entry reservation in high season; Antelope Canyon is only by Navajo guided tour, book ahead. In summer carry 3–4 litres of water per person per day and don't hike at midday. Driving stretches are long with no signal, so fill up often. Check whether the Grand Canyon North Rim is open before you go.

us-yellowstone.places: Yellowstone National Park, Grand Teton National Park, Glacier National Park, Jackson Hole, Denver, Rocky Mountain National Park, Aspen, Bozeman
us-yellowstone.summary: Best: Jun–Sep when all roads are open; Sep has fewer people and autumn colours
us-yellowstone.climate: High-altitude continental climate. Winter is long and bitterly cold, often below -20°C, with heavy snow closing roads; summer days are 20–28°C and nights can be near freezing, with many afternoon thunderstorms. Spring and autumn are short, and it may snow in May and Oct.
notes: Yellowstone about -18 to -5°C, only snowcoach tours can enter, winter wildlife watching
About -15 to -2°C, bitterly cold, wolf watching by snowcoach, Rockies ski season
About -10 to 4°C, Yellowstone roads close from mid month for snow clearing, hardly any visits possible
About -5 to 10°C, some roads open mid to late month, bears come out, still snowy
About 0 to 17°C, most roads open, bison calves born, changeable weather

About 7 to 27°C, warmest; Going-to-the-Sun Road in Glacier National Park usually fully open

About 1 to 20°C, fewer people, elk rut, aspens turning gold

highlights: Elk rut and golden aspens in autumn
Bison and elk calves born, bears often seen
Alpine wildflowers in full bloom
Going-to-the-Sun Road in Glacier National Park fully open
Cheyenne Frontier Days rodeo (late Jul)
Yellowstone winter snowcoach tours, wolf watching in the Lamar Valley
Ski season in Colorado and Jackson Hole
us-yellowstone.avoid: Yellowstone roads are closed from mid Mar to mid Apr and in Nov. In May and Oct the weather is changeable and heavy snow can fall suddenly. Jul–Aug is busiest, with hard parking at popular sights.
us-yellowstone.tips: Lodging inside Yellowstone is often booked out a year ahead for summer, and Glacier National Park may need an entry reservation in high season. Stay at least 23 m from bison and at least 91 m from bears, and carry bear spray. In geothermal areas you must stay on the boardwalks. Denver is about 1,600 m up; watch for altitude sickness in the high mountains.

us-pacificnw.places: Seattle, Mount Rainier National Park, Olympic National Park, Portland, North Cascades National Park, Mount St. Helens, Columbia River Gorge, Oregon Coast
us-pacificnw.summary: Best: Jul–Sep, sunny and dry; Mount Rainier's wildflowers peak late Jul to Aug
us-pacificnw.climate: Temperate oceanic climate. Winter is mild, rainy and grey, with rain almost every day in Oct–Apr; summer is dry and sunny, Seattle about 20–27°C. Mountain snow is very deep in winter, and high mountain roads often don't open until Jul.
notes: Seattle about 3 to 9°C, endless grey rain, snowshoe hikes on Mount Rainier
About 3 to 11°C, rainy, skiing in the mountains, indoor sights in the city
About 4 to 13°C, still rainy, cherry blossoms open at the University of Washington
About 6 to 15°C, Skagit Valley Tulip Festival, changeable weather
About 8 to 18°C, less rain, waterfalls full, some mountain roads not yet open
About 11 to 22°C, warming up, still cloudy early in the month, snow still in the high mountains
About 13 to 25°C, dry and sunny, wildflowers opening at Paradise on Mount Rainier
About 14 to 26°C, driest month, alpine wildflowers at their peak, the odd wildfire smoke

highlights: Cherry blossoms at the University of Washington
Skagit Valley Tulip Festival

Orca-watching boat trips in the San Juan Islands
Golden larches in the North Cascades (late Sep to early Oct)
Salmon runs, seen at fish ladders and streams
Skiing at Stevens Pass and Mount Hood
us-pacificnw.avoid: Nov–Mar is grey and rainy with short days, and most high roads at Mount Rainier and the North Cascades are closed. In Aug, wildfire smoke sometimes spoils the views.
us-pacificnw.tips: In summer, weekend parking is hard at popular national parks, and Mount Rainier may need an entry reservation in high season; check the official website before you go. Bring a waterproof jacket all year and dress in layers. Olympic National Park is big; allow 2–3 days by car. Take care at night in some downtown areas of Seattle and Portland.

us-hawaii.places: Waikiki on Oahu, Pearl Harbor, Haleakala on Maui, Road to Hana, Hawaii Volcanoes National Park on the Big Island, Mauna Kea, Na Pali Coast on Kauai, Waimea Canyon
us-hawaii.summary: Good all year: Apr–May and Sep–Oct have good weather, fewer people and lower prices
us-hawaii.climate: Tropical oceanic climate, warm all year, about 26–31°C by day at the coast. Nov–Mar is the rainy season, with more rain on the windward (northeast) sides and big waves on the North Shore; Apr–Oct is drier. High mountain tops can be near freezing. Jun–Nov is hurricane season, but landfalls are rare.
notes: Waikiki about 19 to 27°C, rainy season, giant North Shore waves, humpback whale season
About 19 to 27°C, humpback whale peak, best whale-watching boat trips off Maui
About 20 to 27°C, less rain, spring break crowds, whales still around
About 21 to 28°C, prices drop after the high season, weather getting drier
About 22 to 29°C, dry and sunny, few people and low prices, good seas for snorkelling

About 24 to 31°C, hottest, summer crowds, hurricane season sometimes has an effect

highlights: Humpback whale season, most whales off Maui
Giant winter waves and surf contests on Oahu's North Shore
Merrie Monarch hula festival in Hilo (the week after Easter, the date changes every year)
Lei Day (1 May)
King Kamehameha Day floral parade (around 11 Jun)
Calm summer seas on Kauai's Na Pali Coast, good for boat trips and hiking
Aloha Festivals, hula and parades on each island
us-hawaii.avoid: Flights and hotels are most expensive from late Dec to early Jan and in the summer holidays. In Nov–Mar the North Shore waves are too big for swimming, and windward sides are rainy. Which volcano areas are open can change at any time.
us-hawaii.tips: Sunrise at Haleakala needs an online reservation ahead, and popular spots like Haena State Park on Kauai also need reservations. Giant winter waves on the North Shore are dangerous; watch the warning flags on the beach. Don't touch sea turtles or monk seals. Book rental cars early; you need domestic flights between islands.

us-alaska.places: Anchorage, Fairbanks, Denali National Park, Glacier Bay National Park, Ketchikan, Juneau, Kenai Fjords at Seward, Homer
us-alaska.summary: Best: Jun–Aug when cruises run and Denali is fully open; northern lights in Sep and Dec–Mar
us-alaska.climate: The southern coast has a mild, rainy oceanic climate; the interior has a bitterly cold continental climate. Summer days are about 15–22°C with nearly 20 hours of daylight; in winter Fairbanks is often below -25°C with only a few hours of daylight, but the northern lights are active.
notes: Fairbanks about -27 to -17°C, very short days, many chances for the northern lights
About -24 to -12°C, bitterly cold with many clear nights, northern lights season, Fur Rendezvous in Anchorage
About -18 to -3°C, longer days but northern lights still possible, sled dog race starts
About -6 to 8°C, snowmelt and mud, most sights not open, in-between low season
Anchorage about 4 to 15°C, cruise season begins, Denali opens mid to late month
About 9 to 20°C, near-constant daylight, wildlife active, cruise high season
About 11 to 22°C, warmest, salmon runs and bears fishing, most crowded
About 10 to 19°C, more rain, salmon season goes on, first autumn colours late in the month
About 4 to 13°C, red and yellow autumn tundra, cruise season ends, northern lights return

Inside Passage cruises and calving glaciers in Glacier Bay
Boat trips in Kenai Fjords to see humpback whales and orcas
Brown bears catching salmon at Brooks Falls in Katmai
Midnight sun events around the summer solstice
Iditarod sled dog race (starts in Anchorage in early Mar)
Northern lights in Fairbanks
us-alaska.avoid: Apr and Oct–Nov are low season: most cruises, lodges and park buses stop, and the weather is grey, cold and muddy. In Dec–Jan the interior is bitterly cold with very short days.
us-alaska.tips: Book summer cruises, Denali park buses and lodging more than six months ahead. Summer has lots of mosquitoes; bring repellent. For winter northern lights, go around the new moon and bring polar-grade warm gear. Keep your distance from bears in the wild and carry bear spray. Many sights can only be reached by small plane or boat, so leave spare time in your plan.

ca-rockies.places: Banff, Lake Louise, Moraine Lake, Jasper, Icefields Parkway, Columbia Icefield, Yoho National Park, Calgary
ca-rockies.summary: Best: Jul–Sep for blue lakes; Calgary Stampede in Jul; golden larches in late Sep
ca-rockies.climate: Alpine continental climate. Summer is short and cool, Banff about 20–24°C by day and 5–8°C at night, with frequent afternoon thunderstorms; winter is long and bitterly cold, often -15 to -25°C, with deep snow. The lakes usually don't thaw until Jun.
notes: Banff about -15 to -5°C, ski season, skating on frozen Lake Louise
About -13 to -2°C, bitterly cold and clear, best for skiing and snow activities

Bright blue water at Lake Louise, Moraine Lake and Peyto Lake
Black bears, grizzlies and bighorn sheep often seen along the Icefields Parkway
Golden larches (late Sep, Larch Valley hike)

Skiing at Banff and Lake Louise resorts
ca-rockies.avoid: Apr–May is a muddy in-between time with frozen lakes. After mid Oct, roads to Moraine Lake and other sights close. Jul–Aug lodging is expensive and parking is very hard.
ca-rockies.tips: You need a park pass to enter the national parks. Private cars can't drive to Moraine Lake; take the Parks Canada shuttle or a tour bus, booked online ahead. Book summer lodging in Banff six months ahead. Driving the Icefields Parkway in winter needs snow tyres; check road conditions. Chinese visitors need a Canadian visa.

ca-bc.places: Vancouver, Victoria, Butchart Gardens, Whistler, Tofino, Stanley Park, Sea-to-Sky Highway, Kelowna
ca-bc.summary: Best: Jul–Sep, dry and sunny; Dec–Mar for skiing at Whistler
ca-bc.climate: Temperate oceanic climate. Winter is mild and rainy, and Vancouver rarely goes below 0°C; summer is dry and sunny, about 20–25°C. The mountains get lots of snow in winter, and Whistler has a long ski season. The west coast has strong winter storms.
notes: Vancouver about 1 to 7°C, often grey and rainy, peak ski season at Whistler

ca-bc.avoid: Nov–Jan is Vancouver's wettest, darkest time. Oct and May are in-between low seasons at Whistler. In Jul–Aug, weekend ferries to and from Vancouver Island are very hard to get on.
ca-bc.tips: Be sure to book a car space ahead on BC Ferries to and from Vancouver Island on summer weekends. Snow tyres are required on the Sea-to-Sky Highway in winter. Book Whistler lodging ahead for the ski season. Vancouver's Downtown Eastside (around East Hastings Street) is less safe; avoid it at night.

ca-east.places: Toronto, Niagara Falls, Ottawa, Montreal, Quebec City, Maple Leaf Road, Algonquin Provincial Park, Prince Edward Island
ca-east.summary: Best: Jul–Aug for summer festivals; maple leaves reddest from late Sep to early Oct
ca-east.climate: Humid continental climate. Winter is bitterly cold and snowy, Quebec City often below -15°C; summer is warm and sometimes muggy, about 24–28°C; autumn is cool, and maple leaves turn fully red from late Sep to mid Oct.
notes: Quebec City about -18 to -8°C, very cold and snowy, good for snow and ice experiences
About -16 to -6°C, Quebec Winter Carnival and Winterlude in Ottawa
About -9 to 1°C, maple syrup season begins, visit a sugar shack, snow melting

Christmas markets in Quebec City and Toronto
ca-east.avoid: Jan–Feb is bitterly cold, feeling as low as -30°C. Apr and Nov are grey, cold, muddy and dull. May–Jun brings black flies and mosquitoes in the woods. Lodging is tight on autumn-leaf weekends.
ca-east.tips: Algonquin Park is busy with cars on autumn-leaf weekends; go on a weekday and book a day pass ahead. Winter wind chill is extreme, so bring full cold-weather gear. Crossing between the Canadian and US sides at Niagara needs the right visa. Quebec is mainly French-speaking, and most road signs are in French.

ca-north.places: Yellowknife, Great Slave Lake, Whitehorse, Dawson City, Kluane National Park, Churchill
ca-north.summary: Best: Dec–Mar and Sep for the northern lights; Churchill polar bears in Oct–Nov
ca-north.climate: Subarctic continental climate. Winter is long and bitterly cold, Yellowknife often -30°C in Jan, with dry, clear air good for the northern lights; summer is short, about 15–21°C, with near-constant daylight. Spring and autumn are short.
notes: Yellowknife about -31 to -22°C, extreme cold and clear skies, peak northern lights season

Polar bear viewing by tundra buggy in Churchill
ca-north.avoid: From Apr to early Aug the night sky is too bright to see the northern lights. May–Jun is the muddy ice-melt time with lots of mosquitoes. In Oct–Nov Yellowknife is often cloudy, with fewer chances for the northern lights.
ca-north.tips: On a northern lights trip, stay 3–4 nights in a row to raise your chances, and go around the new moon. In winter rent or bring polar-grade clothing and boots; camera batteries freeze easily. Churchill has no road in, only plane or train, and polar bear tours often need booking a year ahead. Chinese visitors need a Canadian visa.

mx-cancun.places: Cancún, Tulum, Playa del Carmen, Chichén Itzá, Ik Kil cenote, Cozumel, Bacalar, Mérida, Holbox Island
mx-cancun.summary: Best: Dec–Apr, sunny dry season; avoid the Sep–Oct hurricane peak
mx-cancun.climate: Tropical climate, hot all year, about 27–33°C by day. Nov–Apr is the dry season, sunny with little rain; May–Oct is the rainy season, muggy with many showers. Jun–Nov is hurricane season, with the highest risk in Sep–Oct. In summer, sargassum seaweed often piles up on the beaches.
notes: Cancún about 21 to 28°C, sunny dry season, clear sea, many North American visitors
About 22 to 29°C, some of the best weather, good for ruins and cenotes

mx-cancun.avoid: Sep–Oct is the peak of hurricanes and heavy rain. In May–Sep sargassum may pile up heavily on the beaches. Christmas–New Year and spring break in Mar have the highest prices and biggest crowds.
mx-cancun.tips: Sargassum changes every year; check the monitoring reports before you go, and you can switch to Isla Mujeres or Bacalar. Arrive at Chichén Itzá when it opens to beat the crowds and the heat. Some cenotes only allow eco-friendly sunscreen. Chinese visitors with a valid US visa or similar can enter without a visa; confirm before you go, and check the latest safety situation before you go.

mx-central.places: Mexico City, Teotihuacan, Oaxaca, Guanajuato, San Miguel de Allende, Puebla, Xochimilco, Pátzcuaro
mx-central.summary: Best: late Oct to early Nov for the Day of the Dead, or Feb–Mar for jacaranda season
mx-central.climate: Highland subtropical climate. Mexico City is about 2,240 m up and mild all year, about 21–27°C by day and cool in the morning and evening. Nov–Apr is the sunny dry season, with Apr–May the warmest; Jun–Sep is the rainy season, with frequent afternoon thunderstorms. Winter mornings and nights can be near freezing.
notes: Mexico City about 6 to 22°C, dry and sunny, cold mornings and nights; eat Rosca de Reyes for Epiphany

Jacarandas in full bloom in Mexico City

Monarch butterfly winter reserves in Michoacán

Independence Day celebrations (15–16 Sep)

Feast of the Virgin of Guadalupe (12 Dec)
mx-central.avoid: Jun–Sep rainy season has many afternoon thunderstorms. Apr–May is hot and dry with heavier air pollution. During the Day of the Dead, lodging prices soar in Oaxaca and Pátzcuaro.
mx-central.tips: Book Day of the Dead lodging months ahead. Mexico City is high up; when you first arrive watch for mild altitude sickness and use sunscreen. Use a proper ride app for taxis, and watch for pickpockets on the metro at rush hour. Safety varies a lot between states, so check the latest safety situation before you go. Chinese visitors with a valid US visa or similar can enter without a visa; confirm before you go.

cu-cuba.places: Havana, Trinidad, Varadero, Viñales, Cienfuegos, Santa Clara, Santiago de Cuba
cu-cuba.summary: Best: Dec–Mar, cool dry season; avoid the Sep–Oct hurricane peak
cu-cuba.climate: Tropical climate. Nov–Apr is the dry season, about 26–28°C by day, sunny and comfortable; May–Oct is the rainy season, hot and humid at about 31–33°C, with many afternoon thunderstorms. Jun–Nov is hurricane season, with the highest risk in Sep–Oct.

cu-cuba.avoid: Sep–Oct is the hurricane peak; Jul–Aug is very hot and humid. Infrastructure is weak, and power cuts and fuel shortages can affect transport and lodging.
cu-cuba.tips: Bank cards issued in the US don't work in Cuba; bring enough cash in euros. Internet is limited, so download offline maps ahead. Casas particulares (homestays) are a good experience and most can include breakfast. Power cuts may happen, so allow extra time for transport. Chinese ordinary passports can enter visa-free, while most other nationalities need a tourist card; the rules change often, so confirm before you go and check the latest safety situation.

bs-caribbean.places: Nassau in the Bahamas, the Exumas, Montego Bay in Jamaica, Punta Cana in the Dominican Republic, San Juan in Puerto Rico, Aruba, the Pitons in St Lucia, British Virgin Islands
bs-caribbean.summary: Best: Dec–Apr, sunny dry season; Aruba is outside the hurricane belt and good all year
bs-caribbean.climate: Tropical oceanic climate, about 27–31°C all year. Dec–Apr is the dry season, sunny and comfortable with trade winds; May–Nov is hot and humid with many showers, and Jun–Nov is hurricane season, with the highest risk in Aug–Oct. Aruba and other southern islands are dry and rarely hit by hurricanes.
notes: About 24 to 29°C, sunny dry season, pleasant trade winds, high season prices

Sailing in the British Virgin Islands, with moderate wind and waves
bs-caribbean.avoid: Aug–Oct is the hurricane peak, with possible flight cancellations. Prices are highest from late Dec to early Jan and during spring break in Mar. In summer some coasts may have sargassum seaweed.
bs-caribbean.tips: Visa rules differ by island (Puerto Rico needs a US visa); check each one before you go. In hurricane season buy insurance that covers hurricanes, or choose Aruba outside the hurricane belt. Book all-inclusive resorts early for high season. Some areas of Jamaica and other places are less safe; don't walk alone outside the resort at night, and check the latest safety situation before you go.

cr-costarica.places: Arenal Volcano, La Fortuna, Monteverde Cloud Forest, Manuel Antonio National Park, Tortuguero National Park, Corcovado National Park, Guanacaste beaches, San José
cr-costarica.summary: Best: Dec–Apr, dry season on the Pacific side; the Caribbean side is drier in Sep–Oct
cr-costarica.climate: Tropical climate. The lowland coasts are about 28–32°C, while the Central Valley and cloud forests are cool, about 15–24°C. On the Pacific side Dec–Apr is the dry season and May–Nov the rainy season, wettest in Sep–Oct; the Caribbean side is rainy all year but drier in Sep–Oct.
notes: Pacific coast about 22 to 33°C, sunny dry season, book early for high season

cr-costarica.avoid: Sep–Oct brings heavy rain on the Pacific side, and some dirt roads are hard to drive. From late Dec to early Jan and in Easter Holy Week, lodging is tight and expensive.
cr-costarica.tips: In the dry season book rental cars and popular eco-lodges ahead; in the rainy season rent a 4x4. Buy Manuel Antonio National Park tickets online ahead; it closes on a fixed day each week. A guide makes it easier to spot sloths and birds. Don't leave valuables in the car; watch for rip currents. Check visa rules before you go.

gt-guatemala-belize.places: Antigua Guatemala, Lake Atitlán, Tikal, Flores, Chichicastenango, Acatenango Volcano, Great Blue Hole in Belize, Ambergris Caye, Caye Caulker
gt-guatemala-belize.summary: Best: Nov–Apr dry season; Holy Week processions in Antigua are grandest in Mar–Apr
gt-guatemala-belize.climate: The highlands (Antigua, Lake Atitlán) have spring-like weather, about 22–26°C by day and cool at night; the lowlands of Tikal and Belize are hot and humid, about 30–33°C. Nov–Apr is the dry season and May–Oct the rainy season; the Caribbean coast has hurricane risk in Jun–Nov.
notes: Antigua about 12 to 24°C, sunny dry season, clear views on volcano hikes

gt-guatemala-belize.avoid: Sep–Oct has the most rain, high hurricane risk in Belize, and landslides on mountain roads. During Holy Week, Antigua lodging is fully booked and prices double. Apr–May is very hot in the lowlands.
gt-guatemala-belize.tips: Book Holy Week lodging six months ahead. The Acatenango hike needs a guide, and the summit is freezing at night. Some parts of Guatemala City are unsafe; use proper transport and check the latest safety situation before you go. English is widely spoken in Belize and US dollars are accepted. Diving the Great Blue Hole usually needs an advanced diving certificate.

pa-panama.places: Panama City, Miraflores Locks on the Panama Canal, Casco Viejo (old town), San Blas Islands, Bocas del Toro, Boquete, Pearl Islands
pa-panama.summary: Best: Jan–Mar, dry season on the Pacific side; Bocas is drier in Sep–Oct
pa-panama.climate: Tropical climate, hot and humid all year, about 24–32°C in the lowlands, cool in the Boquete highlands. Dec–Apr is the dry season, sunny and windy; May–Nov is the rainy season, wettest in Oct–Nov. The Caribbean side is rainy all year. It lies south of the hurricane belt and is very rarely hit by hurricanes.
notes: Panama City about 23 to 32°C, sunny and windy dry season, good for island hopping

pa-panama.avoid: Oct–Nov has the most rain, and the mountain road and boat trip to San Blas are affected by weather. In Jan–Mar strong trade winds make San Blas speedboats bumpy. During Carnival many businesses in Panama City close.
pa-panama.tips: US dollars are used. San Blas is self-governed by the Guna people: pay the entry fee, bring cash and your passport, and expect simple lodging. To see the canal, pick a time when ships are passing through. The Darién area is dangerous, don't go; check the latest safety situation before you go. Chinese visitors with a valid US visa or similar can enter without a visa; confirm before you go.

co-colombia.places: Cartagena, Medellín, Bogotá, Salento in the Coffee Triangle, Cocora Valley, Tayrona National Park, Santa Marta, Guatapé, Rosario Islands
co-colombia.summary: Best: Dec–Feb dry season with a sunny Caribbean coast; Medellín Flower Festival in Aug
co-colombia.climate: Tropical climate, with temperature set by altitude: Cartagena is hot and humid at about 25–32°C, Medellín is spring-like at about 17–28°C, Bogotá is cool at about 7–19°C. The Andes have two rainy seasons, Apr–May and Oct–Nov; the Caribbean coast is wetter in May–Nov.
notes: Cartagena about 24 to 31°C, sunny dry season, quite crowded in coast high season

co-colombia.avoid: Apr–May and Oct–Nov are the mountain rainy seasons, with landslides on roads. Tayrona closes for short spells several times a year (often in Feb, Jun and Oct). From late Dec to mid Jan local holidays push prices up.
co-colombia.tips: Tayrona's closing dates are announced each year; confirm before you go. Bogotá is about 2,600 m up; watch for altitude sickness. Keep your phone out of sight on the street and don't show off valuables; use a ride app for taxis, and don't accept drinks from strangers. Some remote areas have safety risks, so check the latest safety situation before you go.

ec-galapagos.places: Quito, Galápagos Islands, Santa Cruz Island, Isabela Island, Yasuní in the Amazon, Cotopaxi Volcano, Cuenca, Baños, Chimborazo
ec-galapagos.summary: Good all year: in the Galápagos, Dec–May has warm, calm seas and Jun–Nov the richest sea life
ec-galapagos.climate: Quito is about 2,850 m up, about 10–20°C, drier in Jun–Sep. In the Galápagos Dec–May is the warm season, with warm sea, many showers and calm water; Jun–Nov is the cool season, when the Humboldt Current cools the sea to about 20°C, with more mist and bigger waves but the richest sea life.

highlights: Warm, calm Galápagos seas, snorkelling with turtles and sea lions
Waved albatross breeding on Española

Andes dry season, hikes on Cotopaxi and Chimborazo

Quito founding festival (early Dec)
ec-galapagos.avoid: In Sep the Galápagos seas are roughest and many cruise boats go into dock for repairs. Feb–Apr is the rainiest time in the Andes. Liveaboard cruises cost the most over Christmas–New Year and in Jul–Aug; book early.
ec-galapagos.tips: The Galápagos charge a national park entry fee (quite high) and you need a transit control card; quarantine checks are strict. The cruise route decides which islands you can visit, so compare ahead. Quito is high up; rest after you arrive to adjust. Stay 2 m from animals. Ecuador uses the US dollar. Some cities are unsafe, so check the latest safety situation before you go.

pe-peru.places: Machu Picchu, Cusco, Sacred Valley, Inca Trail, Rainbow Mountain, Lake Titicaca, Lima, Nazca Lines, Colca Canyon, Puerto Maldonado in the Amazon
pe-peru.summary: Best: May–Sep, sunny dry season in the highlands; the Inca Trail closes in Feb
pe-peru.climate: In the Andean highlands (Cusco about 3,400 m up), May–Sep is the dry season, sunny at about 18–21°C by day and often below 0°C at night; Nov–Mar is the rainy season, wettest in Jan–Feb. Coastal Lima has little rain all year and is grey, cool and misty in Jun–Oct. The Amazon is hot and humid all year.
notes: Cusco about 7 to 19°C, rainy season, lots of afternoon rain, landslides possible on mountain roads

pe-peru.avoid: In Feb the Inca Trail is closed and it rains most, and trains may stop for landslides. Jan–Mar is the highland rainy season. In Jun–Aug high season, Machu Picchu tickets and Inca Trail permits often sell out early.
pe-peru.tips: Machu Picchu tickets come by time slot and route; buy them ahead on the official website. Inca Trail permits sell out 4–6 months ahead in high season and must go through a licensed agency. Cusco is about 3,400 m up; adjust lower down in the Sacred Valley first, drink plenty of water and walk slowly. Watch for pickpockets in Lima and Cusco. Check the latest safety situation before you go.

bo-bolivia.places: Uyuni Salt Flat, La Paz, Copacabana, Isla del Sol, Laguna Colorada, Laguna Verde, Sucre, Potosí, Death Road

bo-bolivia.climate: Highland climate. Uyuni and La Paz are both about 3,600 m up, with strong sun and big temperature swings. Nov–Mar is the rainy season, when water on the salt flat makes the "sky mirror"; May–Oct is the dry season, sunny but nights can drop to -15 to -20°C, colder still around Laguna Colorada.

bo-bolivia.avoid: In Jan–Feb heavy rain can cut the salt flat and Laguna Colorada 4x4 routes. In Jun–Aug nights are bitterly cold and simple lodges keep little heat. In Nov neither the mirror nor the dry-season scenery is at its best.
bo-bolivia.tips: La Paz and Uyuni are both over 3,600 m; rest when you arrive, and you can carry altitude sickness medicine (as your doctor advises). Lodging on the three-day 4x4 tour is basic; bring a thick sleeping bag and sunscreen. Pick a tour company with good reviews. Check visa rules before you go. Strikes and road blockades happen; check the latest safety situation before you go.

cl-santiago-atacama.places: Santiago, Valparaíso, Viña del Mar, San Pedro de Atacama, Valley of the Moon, El Tatio Geysers, Colchagua Valley, Casablanca Valley
cl-santiago-atacama.summary: Best: Mar–Apr for the grape harvest and Oct–Nov for spring; the Atacama is good all year
cl-santiago-atacama.climate: Seasons are reversed in the Southern Hemisphere. Santiago has a Mediterranean climate: Dec–Feb is hot and dry at about 30°C, and Jun–Aug is a rainy winter at about 3–15°C. The Atacama is extremely dry, about 22–28°C by day and cold at night, with the odd highland summer storm in Jan–Feb.

cl-santiago-atacama.avoid: In Jun–Aug Santiago's winter is rainy with heavier air pollution. In Jan–Feb highland storms may close Atacama sights, and it is also the peak of the local summer holidays. Services are reduced in National Day week in Sep.
cl-santiago-atacama.tips: Seasons are reversed in the Southern Hemisphere. San Pedro de Atacama is about 2,400 m up and El Tatio Geysers about 4,300 m; the pre-dawn start is freezing, and watch for altitude sickness. Choose stargazing tours around the new moon. Watch for pickpockets in Santiago and Valparaíso. Check visa rules before you go.

cl-patagonia.places: Torres del Paine National Park, Puerto Natales, Punta Arenas, Magdalena Island, Carretera Austral, Marble Caves, San Rafael Glacier, Coyhaique
cl-patagonia.summary: Best: Dec–Mar, southern summer with all trails open; Mar–Apr for autumn colours and fewer people
cl-patagonia.climate: Seasons are reversed in the Southern Hemisphere. Cold temperate climate, known for strong winds and changeable weather; you can get four seasons in one day. Summer (Dec–Feb) days are about 12–18°C with up to 17 hours of daylight; winter (Jun–Aug) is about -3 to 5°C, snowy with short days.

cl-patagonia.avoid: In May–Sep winter most campsites, boat trips and road services stop. In Nov–Jan gales can pass 100 km/h, affecting hikes and flights. In Dec–Feb campsites and lodging are very hard to get.
cl-patagonia.tips: Seasons are reversed in the Southern Hemisphere. Book Torres del Paine campsites and refugios months ahead; you can't stay overnight in the park without a booking, and entry tickets must be bought online. Dress in layers and bring a windproof, waterproof jacket. The Carretera Austral is mostly gravel, some stretches need ferries, and petrol stations are few.

cl-easter-island.places: Hanga Roa, Tongariki, Rano Raraku, Anakena Beach, Orongo, Rano Kau volcano, Ahu Akivi
cl-easter-island.summary: Best: Jan–Mar, warm with little rain; Tapati festival in early to mid Feb
cl-easter-island.climate: Seasons are reversed in the Southern Hemisphere. Subtropical oceanic climate, mild all year. Summer (Dec–Mar) is about 22–28°C with the warmest sea; winter (Jun–Aug) is about 15–20°C, windy and rainy. Apr–Jun has a bit more rain, with showers that come and go fast.

cl-easter-island.tips: Most people fly from Santiago, about 5 hours; book flights early. You need a Rapa Nui National Park ticket, most sites must be visited with a licensed guide, and you can only enter Rano Raraku and Orongo once. Don't touch the moai statues. You must fill in a form to enter the island, and you can stay no more than 30 days.

ar-buenosaires-north.places: Buenos Aires, Iguazu Falls, Mendoza, Salta, Quebrada de Humahuaca, Cafayate, Córdoba
ar-buenosaires-north.summary: Best: Mar–Apr and Oct–Nov for pleasant weather; Mendoza wine harvest festival in Mar
ar-buenosaires-north.climate: Seasons are reversed in the Southern Hemisphere. Buenos Aires has a humid subtropical climate: Dec–Feb is hot and humid at about 28–32°C, Jun–Aug about 8–15°C. Iguazu is hot, humid and rainy all year. Salta in the northwest and Mendoza are dry, with summer thunderstorms and clear, cold winters.

ar-buenosaires-north.tips: Seasons are reversed in the Southern Hemisphere. Argentina's inflation and exchange-rate rules change fast; check the latest ways to pay before you go; paying with a foreign card usually gets a better rate. Allow a full day for the Devil's Throat trail on the Argentine side of Iguazu. Don't go to La Boca in Buenos Aires at night, and watch for phone snatching on the street.

ar-patagonia.places: El Calafate, Perito Moreno Glacier, El Chaltén, Mount Fitz Roy, Ushuaia, Tierra del Fuego National Park, Beagle Channel, Bariloche, Valdés Peninsula
ar-patagonia.summary: Best: Nov–Mar for hiking and glaciers; Sep–Oct is peak whale watching on the Valdés Peninsula
ar-patagonia.climate: Seasons are reversed in the Southern Hemisphere. Cold temperate climate, known for strong winds. In summer (Dec–Feb) El Calafate is about 8–20°C and Ushuaia about 5–14°C, with long days; winter is about -5 to 5°C and snowy, and Ushuaia and Bariloche become ski areas.

ar-patagonia.avoid: In May–Sep most hikes, glacier boat trips and lodging in El Calafate and El Chaltén close. Dec–Feb is windy, with tight and pricey lodging. In the Jul winter holidays ski areas charge the most.
ar-patagonia.tips: Seasons are reversed in the Southern Hemisphere. Places in Patagonia are very far apart, and you usually need domestic flights to connect them. Glacier treks have age limits and must be booked ahead. It is windy and the weather changes a lot; bring a windproof jacket and sunglasses. Argentina's exchange rate changes fast; check the latest ways to pay before you go.

br-rio.places: Rio de Janeiro, Christ the Redeemer, Sugarloaf Mountain, Copacabana, São Paulo, Brazilian side of Iguazu Falls, Paraty, Ilha Grande, Ouro Preto
br-rio.summary: Best: Carnival in Feb–Mar, or May–Sep, dry and cool with fewer people
br-rio.climate: Seasons are reversed in the Southern Hemisphere. Rio has a tropical climate: Dec–Mar is hot and humid with many thunderstorms, often over 35°C; May–Sep is dry and mild, about 20–27°C. São Paulo is higher up, cooler and rainier. Iguaçu is hot and humid in summer and can cool to about 10°C in winter.
notes: Rio about 24 to 31°C, very hot and humid, afternoon thunderstorms, beaches busy in the summer holidays

br-rio.avoid: During Carnival and New Year, lodging prices rise several times over; book six months ahead. Dec–Mar is muggy with heavy storms, and mudslides are common in the hills. Many local visitors in the Jul winter holidays.
br-rio.tips: Seasons are reversed in the Southern Hemisphere. Stay alert in Rio: don't take valuables to the beach, avoid walking alone at night, don't enter favelas on your own, and check the latest safety situation before you go. Chinese visitors need a Brazilian visa. From Iguaçu you can also visit the Argentine side; crossing the border needs the right visa.

br-amazon-pantanal.places: Manaus, Amazon jungle lodges, Pantanal, Cuiabá, Lençóis Maranhenses white sand dunes, Fernando de Noronha, Salvador, Fortaleza
br-amazon-pantanal.summary: Best: Jul–Sep for jaguars in the Pantanal, Jun–Aug when the Lençóis lagoons are fullest
br-amazon-pantanal.climate: Southern Hemisphere tropical climate, hot all year at about 25–33°C. In the Amazon Dec–May is the rainy season, when rivers rise sharply, and the water drops in Jun–Nov; in the Pantanal large areas flood in the Nov–Mar rainy season, and animals gather in the Jul–Oct dry season. The northeast coast is rainy in Apr–Jul.
notes: Manaus about 24 to 31°C, rainy season, much of the Pantanal under water
About 24 to 31°C, lots of rain, Salvador Carnival (the date changes every year)

About 24 to 31°C, high water in the Amazon, paddle through the flooded forest

br-amazon-pantanal.avoid: Jan–Apr is the rainy season in the Amazon and the Pantanal, and flooded Pantanal roads are hard to get through. In Oct–Dec the Lençóis lagoons dry up. Salvador is rainiest in Apr–Jun.
br-amazon-pantanal.tips: Seasons are reversed in the Southern Hemisphere. For the Amazon and the Pantanal, a yellow fever vaccine is advised; bring long sleeves and insect repellent. Noronha charges a daily environmental fee, the national park charges extra, and lodging on the island is pricey, so book early. Take care at night in Salvador's old town, and check the latest safety situation before you go. Chinese visitors need a Brazilian visa.
